Abbott is a global healthcare leader, creating breakthrough science to improve people’s health. We’re always looking towards the future, anticipating changes in medical science and technology.

Abbott Rapid Diagnostics is part of Abbott’s Diagnostics family of businesses, bringing together exceptional teams of experts and industry leading technologies to support diagnostic testing which provides important information for treatment and management of diseases and other conditions.

Within this function sits the Abbott Toxicology Business Unit in which we deliver Occupational Health services across the UK, helping customers/clients comply with health legislation and industry standards.  We support them to manage the ongoing health of their employees and engage their workforce to improve and promote health and wellbeing.

Abbott Occupational Health provides a full range of services (managing health, safety and wellbeing) by both remote case management and onsite provision.  We also provide access to our 20 medical centres across the UK.

We are recruiting an **Occupational Health Advisor based in Crewe,** in which you will work in a medical centre and on customer sites 4 days a week. You will be responsible for the delivery of a full range of Occupational Health duties including completing case management assessments, medical, health surveillance and wellbeing services.

You will be able to demonstrate that you are customer centric and business focused, striving to make a difference by building relationships and demonstrating excellence of clinical performance for our customers.

You will act as a proactive advocate, mentoring other health professionals and actively supporting the clinical governance network and peer to peer review process.

You will work as part of a nationally based team supported by the Clinical Team Leaders, where learnings are shared on a positive and professional basis.

**This position full time; working 4 days a week on site**

**What You’ll Do**

You will support the growth of a dynamic occupational health business ensuring you deliver exceptional clinical performance coupled with taking an active role in mentoring other health professionals.

Responsibilities include

* Work in conjunction with our customers, either at a medical Centre or customer site to provide support, advice and guidance to managers and employees in relation to sickness absence, workplace environment, risk assessment, stress management and return to work following absence.
* Conduct health surveillance / assessments including the undertaking of fitness to work in safety critical posts.
* Provide advice to managers and HR regarding staff who cannot undertake their normal duties and responsibilities, whilst working within the guidelines of customers policy.
* Provide advice and support to managers and supervisors undertaking risk assessments relating to health matters affecting their staff.
* Ensure that knowledge is maintained of up-to-date legislation and best practice relating to all Occupational Health issues.

* Complete case management assessments.
* Attend clinic meetings that share best practice, client clinical delivery excellence and problem solves within professional boundaries of confidentiality.
* Undertake and act upon reflective learning from peer review and actively build a profile that conforms to NMC revalidation expectations.

**Required Qualifications**

* A Degree, Diploma or Certificate in Occupational Health (and be on Part 3 of NMC Register) or be working towards this with evidence of continual professional development.
* A qualification in Hand Arm Vibration and experience of collecting samples for drug and alcohol testing using chain of custody protocols is desirable.
* Excellent organizational skills to manage the diverse customer base and demands.
* Good written and oral communication skills.
* The ability to produce clear and concise reports to managers.
* The ability to carry out medicals / surveillance including audiometry, spirometry, skin assessment, HAVS and safety critical medicals.
* The ability to conduct case management assessments and to produce clear succinct reports that provide structured advice to Line Managers and employers.
* Be able to work closely and effectively with HR, health and safety  
  professionals and our occupational health partners to provide an  
  efficient and cost-effective service to our customers.
* Be able to prioritize workload and use experience and initiative to refer complex cases appropriately.
* Be able to travel between sites.
* Be competent in the use of computers including Microsoft and Excel software.

# Staff Tech Lead, Web & Developer Products

London, UK (Remote)

Our everyday digital experiences are in the middle of a realtime revolution: chatting alongside a livestream, getting realtime financial updates, or working with colleagues in a shared online space. Consumers now expect realtime as standard, and Ably powers a large part of it.

We put developers first. Our products help teams build, extend, and deliver realtime digital experiences, delivering over 700 billion messages to more than 2 billion devices every month. Teams at HubSpot, Fin, Dialpad, NASCAR, Sportsbet, and General Motors all build on Ably.

Working at Ably means helping build the infrastructure that will shape the next generation of the internet. More of what people do online is becoming live, shared and interactive, which only makes what we build more relevant and more necessary. AI is the latest place that shows up. There's still so much to build, and we'd like your help with it.

## **About this role**

As the Staff Tech Lead for the Developer Experience team at Ably, you’ll report directly to our CTO and co-own the DevEx vision and strategy. You’ll lead the engineering team that owns our customer-facing web platform - our dashboard, documentation platform, and control plane - transforming it into a world-class experience for our users.

You are a senior, hands-on engineer who’s passionate about building for developers like yourself; someone who’ll obsess over the developer journey and elevate the user experience of the Ably platform. You’ll blend deep full-stack expertise with a strong product mindset, and lead a team of engineers working on initiatives where the feedback loop is immediate, because you and your team are the target users of the very ecosystem you are building.

Ably is an AI-forward organisation and this is a leadership role for an AI-first engineer. You must have confident, hands-on experience of AI-assisted development and be able to define how a team actually works with these tools day to day, and tell the difference between genuine leverage and noise.

## **Day to day you will**

* **Obsess over developer experience.** You’ll have broad responsibility for elevating how developers interact with Ably’s platform and services, partnering with the DevEx PM as a unified leadership team to deliver a developer experience that becomes a reference point for the industry.
* **Define and lead on AI-first working practices.** You’ll be the catalyst and standard-setter for AI-enabled development across the team. You’ll leverage LLMs and AI tools to accelerate velocity, design workflows, set the guardrails and coach engineers to use them well - without compromising on engineering integrity.
* **Lead technical execution and vision.** You’ll lead a team of five engineers building customer-facing web applications and own the technical architecture and design decisions for our dashboard, docs platform, marketing website, and billing UI.
* **Drive a product-first engineering culture.** You’ll foster an environment where engineers are themselves principal stakeholders of product features, and obsess over customer outcomes. You’ll challenge the "feature factory" mentality and build a team that takes true ownership of the product.
* **Thrive in a rapid iteration environment.** You’ll operate in a high-velocity workspace where PMs, customers, and engineers co-create features. You’ll lead the team in working full-stack to iterate, improve, and ship improvements quickly.
* **Guide engineering outcomes and quality.** You’ll set and enforce high standards for code review, testing, and production readiness. You will participate in incident response and coordinate with the Infrastructure team on platform dependencies and deployments.
* **Mentor and grow the team.** You’ll manage performance, career development, and hiring. You will hold the team accountable for delivery commitments while providing the mentorship needed to turn engineers into product-minded leaders.

## **We'd love to talk if you have**

* Real, demonstrable experience leading AI-first engineering. You champion the use of AI as a productivity multiplier for the team, and have led a team that ships with LLMs and AI tooling embedded in its daily workflow. You see AI as an enabler for higher velocity and output, not a replacement for engineering judgment, and hold strong, evidence-based views on what works and what doesn’t.
* Extensive experience leading technical teams in technical B2B SaaS or API-first products, with a track record of product-minded engineering teams that take initiative and ownership of product outcomes.
* A strong software engineering background with genuine full-stack fluency. You must have enough depth across the web stack to credibly lead and challenge senior web engineers. Hands-on experience with React and TypeScript is valuable, but sound engineering judgement and technical gravitas matter more than specific frameworks.
* You have a natural empathy and strong instincts for what developer customers want because you are the target user. You are genuinely excited about building developer tools and can tap into immediate feedback loops. You understand API design, documentation, and the nuances that differentiate a great developer journey.
* Experience at a startup or growth-stage company or adaptability to thrive in a fast-paced, agile environment with a focus on rapid iteration. To be effective in this role you’ll need excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills.

## **Bonus points if you have**

* Deep production experience building and shipping customer-facing web applications at scale with React and TypeScript.
* Experience delivering solutions used by software developers (developer tooling or APIs) or similar technical personas.
* An understanding of pub/sub and familiarity with distributed systems and event based architectures.

## **What’s it like to work at Ably?**

You'll join a team of around 60 people, working directly alongside senior engineering and leadership. No layers, no bureaucracy, and real ownership from day one.

### Remote-first

We hire the best people wherever they are across the UK and Europe, trust them to own their work, and share decisions and feedback openly. Twice a year, in February and August, we all meet in person, and we expect everyone to be there.

Remote-first comes with trade-offs. On one side: flexibility, no commute, long stretches of focus time, and a wider pool of people to hire from. On the other: it can feel isolating, relationships take effort to build, and you miss the chance conversations an office creates. As our only recruiter, you'll need to manage your own time and stay close to the hiring managers and candidates you work with.

Edinburgh, UK

Addepar is a global data and AI platform empowering investment professionals to turn complex financial information into actionable intelligence. Addepar unifies portfolio, market and client data in a total portfolio view and delivers AI-powered insights within investment and client workflows. More than 1,500 firms in 60 countries use Addepar to manage and advise on nearly $10 trillion in assets. Its open platform integrates with 650 software, data and consulting partners to power end-to-end investment operations across firms of all sizes and levels of complexity. Addepar supports clients worldwide with offices in New York City, Salt Lake City, São Paulo, London, Edinburgh, Geneva, Warsaw, Dubai, Pune and Singapore.

#### **The Role**

We are currently seeking an Assurance & Deal Desk Analyst to join our GTM Operations team in Edinburgh. As an Assurance & Deal Desk Analyst, you will be the operational backbone of two connected processes: client and prospect Assurance (security and compliance due diligence, including trust center profiles and bespoke questionnaires) and Deal Desk (quoting, approvals and contracting). You will keep deals moving, hold the line on process and policy, and work closely with cross-functional leaders across Information Security & Risk (ISR), Legal, Compliance, Product, Finance and Sales to make both processes faster and more scalable.

Applicants must have, and maintain, the right to work in the United Kingdom from the first day of employment. Please note that visa sponsorship is not available for this role.

**What You’ll Do**

* Own the day-to-day operations of the client and prospect Assurance process: triage incoming due-diligence requests, confirm prerequisites (such as an NDA on file for prospects), and guide GTM partners on sharing the right trust center (Whistic) profile based on client ARR tier.
* Manage the Assurance Jira intake queue: review bespoke documentation and questionnaire requests, apply ARR-tier rules, route exceptions for approval, and track every request to completion against clear turnaround targets.
* Coordinate responses to bespoke security and compliance questionnaires using approved collateral, partnering with subject-matter experts in ISR, Legal, Compliance and Product to keep answers accurate and consistent.
* Support the Deal Desk process in Salesforce and CPQ: quote review, SOW and order form routing, and approval workflows across GTM Operations, Finance and Legal; review deals for policy and pricing compliance and escalate non-standard terms.
* Build trusted working relationships with cross-functional leaders in ISR, Legal, Compliance, Product, Finance and Sales; set clear expectations on timing and resolve competing priorities to keep deals moving.
* Maintain our trust center profiles and approved answer library, flagging stale or missing content and driving updates with content owners.
* Keep Salesforce and Jira records (contacts, accounts, NDA status, profile share and access data, request status) accurate and audit-ready.
* Report on Assurance and Deal Desk volume, turnaround time and bottlenecks, and take initiative to design, document and continuously improve repeatable processes, leading small-to-medium process improvement and automation projects with limited guidance.
* Contribute to GTM Operations process documentation and enablement for Sales and Client Success teams.

#### **Who You Are**

* Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience.
* At least four years of related experience in sales operations, deal desk, security or compliance operations, contracts, or a similar process-driven role (or at least two years of related experience with a Master’s degree).

* Work closely with engineering, production and quality colleagues to make sure customer requirements are understood and achieved.

**Duties and responsibilities:**

* Design, develop, implement and oversee the organisation’s EHS programmes and procedures to safeguard employees, contractors, visitors and surrounding communities.

* Develop and maintain a risk-based internal EHS audit programme, ensuring findings, corrective actions and effectiveness reviews are completed and reported to senior management.

*Qualifications*

*Experience*

* Experience of regulatory liaison, incident investigation, contractor governance and senior management reporting.

*Technical Knowledge*

*Technical Knowledge*

# Aon Graduate Programme 2027 - Commercial Risk Consulting

**Commercial Risk Consulting - Graduate Programme 2027**

**Start Date** 1st September 2027

**Application closing date** 7th December 2026 *Please note, we may close earlier if we receive the quantity, quality & diversity of applications required.*

**Better Decisions Begin with You**

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organisation, we are united through trust as one inclusive, diverse team, and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

**Launch Your Career in Commercial Risk Consulting**

Join Aon as a Commercial Risk Consulting graduate and, from day one, you’ll be an integral part of either our Strategic Engagement (Inpoint) or Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS) team. You’ll help clients navigate complex business challenges, handle risk and make better-informed decisions.

**Strategic Engagement (Inpoint):**

Inpoint is Aon’s carrier engagement and management business, working primarily with insurers across Commercial Risk. Our teams use market insight, portfolio analytics and Aon’s broader capabilities to build stronger, more strategic relationships with carrier partners.

Strategic Engagement is focused on helping Aon and its carrier partners identify shared priorities, understand portfolio performance and turn insight into meaningful action. This is not a traditional strategy consulting role. It is a relationship-led, data-informed opportunity at the centre of Aon’s engagement with the insurance market.

As a Strategic Engagement Graduate, you will work with colleagues across Strategy & Technology Group (STG), the Global Broking Centre (GBC) and Commercial Risk UK. You will help prepare insight for senior conversations with insurers, support engagement on portfolio opportunities and contribute to initiatives that strengthen how Aon and its carrier partners work together.

The role offers exposure to senior leaders across Aon and the insurance market. It also provides the chance to build a strong understanding of commercial insurance, carrier priorities, broking, and portfolio dynamics.

**What You Will Do**

* **Analyse market, carrier and portfolio information** to identify trends and opportunities, turning data and analytics into practical insights for carrier and internal partners discussions
* **Support strategic relationship planning and engagement** for key insurers, helping teams establish clear priorities, actions and follow-through while deepening your knowledge of customer relationship management
* **Collaborate across Inpoint, GBC and Commercial Risk UK** to understand carrier objectives, capture insight and coordinate engagement with the market, building your project management and consulting skills over time
* **Contribute to strategic carrier meetings and senior collaborator discussions** and learn how strong commercial relationships are developed throughout Aon and the insurance sector
* **Prepare clear, high-quality materials and presentations** for strategic meetings and portfolio reviews, using focused research and document review to communicate complex information concisely

**Aon M&A and Transaction Solutions (AMATS):**

Mergers and Acquisitions (M&A) and other event-driven situations can be complex, time-critical and highly specialised. The AMATS team typically assists clients in three core areas, prior to, during and/or after completion of an M&A deal or other investment opportunity, by:

* Providing due diligence on an ‘target’ business across a wide range of deal-critical areas, including risk & insurance, cyber & digital, human capital and climate maters. This diligence evaluates the target’s risk exposures - past, current, and future - which may impact transaction value for the buyer
* Arranging insurance solutions aimed at de-risking transaction liabilities and enhancing investor returns, often removing deal-breaking risks. This involves structuring and placing solutions like warranty & indemnity insurance and using insurance capital to mitigate contingent risks, such as tax and litigation
* Delivering portfolio value creation programmes for financial sponsors, including private equity, infrastructure funds, and real estate investors. Use their portfolio scale and insights from analysis. Coordinate efforts to reduce the total cost of risk and improve governance

The clients include financial sponsors  and Corporates, with transaction sizes ranging from small UK domestic deals (such as Voyage Care’s acquisition of Orchard Healthcare) to some of the largest cross-border transactions (such as KONE’s $34.4 billion combination with TK Elevators). Further deal examples can be found on Aon’s LinkedIn page.

You’ll gain exposure to several parts of our transaction advisory and broking business to help build your understanding of why clients implement M&A deals and how Aon supports their business and investment objectives.

**What You Will Do**

* **Support transaction advisory work** for private equity, infrastructure, real estate and corporate clients, helping the team research and analyse risks connected with M&A deals
* **Support the arrangement of M&A insurance solutions** by helping colleagues prepare information for the insurance market and learning how transaction risks can be transferred
* **Coordinate Aon expertise across practices and geographies** while developing your internal network and learning to handle actions and workstreams across a fast-moving transaction process
* **Help identify relevant Aon products, services and solutions** that may support client deal and investment objectives, applying commercial judgement and broader business context
* **Build strong collaborative connections** with clients, insurers, M&A advisers and internal collaborators, while developing your consulting and business communication skills over time

**Your Development**

As an Aon Graduate, you will be enrolled onto our Launch Programme when you join. Alongside your broader development, you will progressively build the technical and professional capabilities needed for the role. This development programme is built around the following core elements: As your experience grows, you will also learn to apply client, industry and risk context when reviewing AI-generated insights, and to coordinate digital tools, specialist resources and stakeholders as part of an effective delivery workflow.

*1. Business learning*. On the job learning and experiences giving you the opportunity to develop your knowledge and understanding of the team and solution line you have joined.

*2. Centralised learning*. Our UK graduates complete in an Aon Induction, monthly webinars, business skills training and workshops; all designed to help you develop your knowledge of Aon, build your confidence and your network across our business.

*3. Professional Qualifications.* To enable you to be as successful as possible, as part of your role, you will be expected to complete our Go Further Apprenticeship programmes. We’ll fully support your study towards the level 4 Diploma in Insurance from the CII (Chartered Insurance Institute) and beyond. To support you as you study for your exams, you’ll receive paid study leave, plus an extensive range of study and tuition materials.

**Your career beyond your Graduate programme**

Once you’ve completed the formal graduate programme, you’ll continue to receive lots of support at Aon. As well as continued technical and business skills training, you’ll receive support for your CII qualifications. To aid your professional development you’ll receive regular performance feedback, and work with your line manager towards promotions.

**Next Steps**

If you are interested in this programme and would like to apply, here is some useful information:

Please review the information on each team and select your first-choice preferred team should you be successful. Please note that, where possible, we will try to consider you for your first-choice preference, however we cannot guarantee your first choice due to availability of roles. If your top preference is unavailable at the time of your Assessment Centre, we will also consider you for the other teams.

**Entry Requirements:**

* You will need to have or be on track to achieve a 2:1 degree (or equivalent) in any degree subject.
* To ensure compliance with UK law, successful candidates must demonstrate their right to work in the UK throughout the duration of their time in role.

**What are we looking for?**

* **Motivation and ambition to pursue a career in Commercial Risk Consulting.** You should be able to explain why Strategic Engagement (Inpoint) or AMATS at Aon interests you and how it aligns with your longer-term goals
* **AI literacy, prompt engineering and AI judgement.** Comfortable using AI-enabled technologies such as Copilot, analytics platforms and digital productivity tools, able to refine outputs and assess their accuracy, relevance and appropriateness
* **Client centricity, strategic thinking and commercial awareness.** Curious about the insurance market and able to connect your work to client and carrier outcomes while considering wider business priorities
* **Critical thinking, problem solving and analytical skills.** Able to analyse information, identify patterns, challenge assumptions and draw evidence-based conclusions using digital tools and data
* **Strong communication and collaboration skills.** Able to explain complex information clearly, ask thoughtful questions and build positive working relationships with a range of internal and external partners
* **Results driven, dependable and adaptable.** Takes ownership, applies feedback, continuously develops skills and can manage changing priorities while delivering accurate, high-quality work
* **Inclusive.** Values different perspectives, challenges assumptions and helps create an environment where everyone feels respected and able to contribute

**Locations:**

Here are the locations where we have graduate opportunities this year: **London**

We recognise the value for our Early Career colleagues of being in the office environment from the beginning of their programme. As a new graduate, you will spend the first 6 months based in the office to support your learning, development, and progression. This will enable you access to support from managers, collaborate with colleagues as well as grow your network across Aon. After completing this initial training period, you will then have the opportunity to work more flexibly, spending at least 3 to 4 days face to face in the Aon office or with clients.

**Aon UK Graduate Recruitment: What to Expect**

We know applying for your first graduate role can be exciting, and sometimes a little daunting. At Aon, we’re committed to making our recruitment process as transparent and supportive as possible. Here’s how our selection journey works, and what you can expect at each stage:

**1. Application Review**

* We process applications on a rolling basis, moving candidates forward as they complete each stage.
* Every application is carefully reviewed by our team (not by AI).
* Due to the high volume of interest, this stage can take up to two weeks.
* Please note: We do not review CVs or cover letters at this point.

**2. Online Assessment**

* We understand you want to put your best foot forward, so you’ll have 5 calendar days to complete the online assessment.
* If you need more time, just let us know as extensions are available.

**3. Video Interview**

* Preparation matters, so you’ll have up to 10 days (240 hours) from receiving your invitation to record and submit your video interview.
* Rest assured: Every video interview is reviewed by a real member of our recruitment team, not an AI system.
* You’ll typically hear back from us within 2-3 weeks after submitting your interview, though times may vary depending on the number of applications.

**4. Assessment Centres**

* Our assessment centres are held in person at the Aon office closest to the location you applied for.
* Please note: Due to the large number of applications, not every candidate who completes a video interview will be invited to an assessment centre.
* Assessment centres usually run after Christmas, from mid-January.
* If selected, you’ll have 7-14 days’ notice to help you arrange any travel.
* We run a limited number of Assessment Centre so please make every effort to attend if invited.
* We reimburse reasonable travel costs (such as standard class train tickets). Flights and hotels are only covered if agreed in advance.
* At the assessment centre stage, your CV and cover letter will be shared with hiring managers. This helps them get a fuller picture of you as a candidate—but these documents are not used for initial screening.

**What is Aon's guidance of the use of AI during the selection process?**

As an innovative global leader, we recognize and embrace the power of Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help job seekers be more efficient in their recruitment processes. In fact, Aon is in the business of developing and implementing innovative AI tools that support both colleagues and clients, which you’ll use as an Aon colleague if you join our team.

AI can be a helpful tool for researching Aon, preparing for interviews or refining your CV, it should support, not replace, your own thinking, judgement, skills and experiences. Any application materials you submit should accurately reflect your achievements, capabilities and potential.

We ask that you refrain from using AI when completing assessments or during live or pre-recorded interview processes, which will often include an in-person interview where the technology will not be available to you. Additionally, virtual or in-person interviews should not be recorded or transcribed.

At Aon, we foster a culture of inclusiveness, fairness and transparency. We expect all candidates to embrace these principles in every interaction with us.

**Can I apply for more than one programme or role?**

We ask candidates to submit one Early Carers application per recruitment cycle. We encourage you to explore our opportunities carefully and apply for the programme or role that best matches your skills, interests and career goals. This helps you focus on submitting your strongest application and ensures we can assess candidates fairly and efficiently.

If, during the selection process, we believe another opportunity at Aon may be a better fit for your experience and aspirations, our recruitment team may discuss alternative options with you.

If you're unsure which programme is right for you, we recommend reviewing the programme information on our careers site or attending one of our events before applying.**Top Tip**: Choose the role you're most excited about, rather than treating a second application as a back-up option. We want to understand where your genuine interests lie and how you see your future career developing.**We’re here to support you every step of the way. If you have any questions or need accommodations, just contact our team -****graduates@aon.co.uk****. Good luck, and we look forward to seeing what you can bring to Aon!**

Apolitical's mission is to make governments smarter for people and the planet and we reach over 40 million public servants through our partnerships with governments globally. Apolitical’s corporate partners include organisations such as Google, AWS and Microsoft who work with us at scale with governments and public sector bodies worldwide.

Our flagship AI platform, Futura, helps governments identify where AI can make a difference and equips public servants with personalised learning to put it into practice. PolicyNova and PolicyNavigator support evidence-based policy research, while our Government AI Campus and Frontier Science & Tech and Resilience Platforms provide practical learning to help public servants respond to emerging challenges.

#### The Role

Apolitical is entering a significant phase of commercial growth. Our priority is to expand government adoption of our learning programmes, communities and AI-powered products through larger, longer-term agreements.

Governments, schools of government, ministries and government-adjacent bodies are our core customers. This role is dedicated to them, working alongside a separate Director who leads our foundation and corporate partnerships.

As a Director of Public Sector Partnerships, you will contribute to our public sector revenue, leading complex agreements with governments from qualification through procurement and negotiation to contract signature. Your immediate mandate is to convert our existing government pipeline into revenue, while growing our current accounts and building a sustainable pipeline of new public sector business internationally.

You will work closely with Partnerships and Delivery and Product, and with our foundation and corporate partnerships lead on programmes where a funder supports a government.

**You will:**

* Lead complex public sector sales – own government opportunities through the full commercial cycle, including stakeholder engagement, proposals, tenders and procurement, negotiation and contract signature.
* Build and qualify pipeline – generate new business with governments and public sector bodies internationally, and direct effort towards the opportunities with the strongest revenue potential.
* Grow existing government accounts – secure renewals and expand our current government partnerships into larger, multi-year or multi-department agreements.

**Within three months, you'll:**

* Be progressing priority government opportunities through proposals, procurement and commercial negotiations.
* Have agreed priority regions and segments, and established a qualified pipeline of new public sector business against them.
* Have renewal and expansion plans in place for our key government accounts, developed with Partnerships and Delivery.

* Have secured revenue-generating agreements with governments and demonstrated measurable progress against agreed commercial objectives.
* Be independently managing your pipeline and accounts with reliable forecasting and clear visibility of commercial risks.
* Be contributing government insight that shapes our commercial priorities, pricing and propositions.

Success in this role is measured by new public sector revenue closed against your annual target, renewal and expansion revenue from existing government accounts, the quality of your qualified pipeline and the accuracy of your revenue forecasts.

#### About you

You will have experience securing significant, multi-year agreements with governments or public sector bodies, whether through selling technology-enabled products and services or through institutional partnerships. You understand how governments set priorities, fund programmes and buy.

**You'll thrive here if you:**

* Have personally owned and closed significant agreements through complex, multi-stage processes, including formal procurement.
* Can build credibility with senior government officials and influence decisions across ministries, agencies and approval layers.
* Bring strong commercial judgement, including opportunity qualification, pricing, negotiation and margin management.
* Can translate our products into clear propositions that address government policy goals and workforce challenges.
* Are disciplined in pipeline management, forecasting and prioritising commercial effort.
* Operate effectively with autonomy and ambiguity across different government systems and cultures, taking responsibility for decisions and outcomes.
* Are motivated by helping governments become more effective for people and the planet.

**Show us in your CV if you have:**

* Experience selling AI, data, learning or software products to governments or public sector bodies.
* Experience securing multi-year contracts or funding from governments, or from bilateral or multilateral donors.
* Experience working with public sector buyers in more than one country or region.

* Your experience is primarily in relationship management without personal accountability for securing and signing agreements.

We use skills-based assessments and structured interviews to focus on what predicts success in the role. ### **Technical direction and quality**

* Hold the team to clear standards for security, accessibility, search and performance (detailed below).

### **Web standards: accessibility, search and performance**

* Own accessibility to WCAG 2.2 AA as a minimum, with awareness of the European Accessibility Act and UK public-sector regulations where they apply. Build it into components, content models and testing, combining automated tools (axe, Lighthouse) with manual keyboard and screen-reader checks.
* Own technical SEO: semantic HTML, structured data (schema.org), metadata, canonicals, sitemaps, hreflang for multi-region sites, and redirect strategy during migrations.
* Prepare properties for answer engine optimisation (AEO) and generative engine optimisation (GEO), so content is structured, attributable and easy for AI search and assistants to find, understand and cite.
* Set performance budgets and hold the team to Core Web Vitals targets (LCP, INP, CLS), using real-user monitoring as well as lab testing.
* Build these checks into CI so regressions are caught before release, not after.

### **AI-assisted engineering**

* Lead a team working in a heavily AI-tooled environment, using coding assistants and agents such as Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or Cursor, and set clear rules for how they are used.
* Preserve codebase quality: AI-generated code meets the same standards for review, testing, security and maintainability as hand-written code.
* Keep people accountable: every change has an owner who understands it, and architecture decisions are not delegated to tools.
* Maintain the guardrails that make AI output reliable, including linting, type checking, test coverage, documented conventions and context files the tools can follow.
* Watch for AI-specific risks, such as client data or secrets in prompts, licence and IP concerns, and duplicated or inconsistent code.

### **Migrations and integrations**

* Plan and lead content and platform migrations from legacy or monolithic CMS platforms to headless, including content audits, mapping, transformation and URL redirect strategy.
* Design repeatable migration and automation pipelines using n8n or similar tools, alongside custom Node scripts where needed.
* Lead integration development between the CMS and the client's wider estate, such as CRM, DAM, PIM, search, analytics, marketing automation and identity.
* Own API design, webhooks and event-driven patterns, with clear error handling, monitoring and rollback.

* Own documentation for architecture, content models, integrations, design decisions and technical specifications.
* Turn one-to-one guidance into reusable material so onboarding and handoff don't depend on any one person.
* Stay current on [client-specific compliance requirements, e.g. UK GDPR, cookie consent (PECR) and accessibility obligations].

* Break plans down into well-formed tasks and stories the team can act on.
* Delegate work fairly and evenly across the team.

### **Delivery**

* Lead technical input to planning, estimation and backlog refinement.
* Track progress against milestones and budget with the project manager.
* Identify technical risks early, particularly around migration cut-over and third-party integrations, and escalate critical issues before they become surprises.

### **Commercial awareness**

* Seek client feedback and fold it into development cycles.
* Spot genuine opportunities to add value for the client, and bring them to the account team.

## **What success looks like**

* **Delegation is healthy.** Work is spread across the team, not bottlenecked on you.
* **Documentation survives handoff.** A new engineer can onboard and maintain the system from what is written down.
* **Migrations land cleanly.** Content moves with no lost pages, broken links or SEO drop, and cut-overs happen on the planned date.
* **Standards are measurable.** Properties meet WCAG 2.2 AA and Core Web Vitals targets, and are visible in both traditional and AI-driven search.
* **Quality holds as speed rises.** AI tooling increases throughput without increasing defects, accessibility issues or performance regressions.
* **Editors are self-sufficient.** Content teams can build and publish pages without developer help.

· Test Manager, AI Test Engineer

· Software development & programming (e.g. Python, Java, C#)
· AI application development (e.g. Microsoft Copilot, Azure AI, OpenAI)
· Testing & quality assurance (e.g. Selenium, JMeter)
Who we’re looking for
To be considered for a role there are essential criteria to be met. You must:
· Provide evidence that you are in the process of obtaining an autism diagnosis OR evidence you already have a diagnosis OR alternative documentation to evidence autism.
· Have the right to work in the UK.
· Demonstrate coding proficiency in at least one of Python, Java or C++.
Professional experience, academic achievements, or a certification such as PCAP would be indicators of proficiency.
· Be able to meet the requirements of the Civil Service Nationality Rules.
· Be able and willing to undergo the vetting required for sensitive roles with public sector clients, and then obtain and maintain a security clearance at a level as may be required (BPSS, SC, or DV).
You can see an overview of the UK government security vetting process on the Cabinet Office YouTube channel. At a minimum you will be required to have been a UK resident for the last five years.
· Be able and willing to commute to and from work in central London/Manchester/Leeds/Newcastle for two or three days per week.
As a responsible employer we are aware of the sensory and emotional impact of long journeys; we consider a reasonable commuting time to be no more than 1.5 hours in each direction.
· Be willing to upskill in artificial intelligence and accept placements into roles in which AI may be used or deployed.
· Accept that arrangements for your upskilling will include the development of skills in technical domains that may be new to you. These new skills will complement those that you already possess. This will enhance your personal profile and also improve auticon’s ability to find engagements for you.

# Independent Member, Financial Markets Infrastructure Committee (FMIC)

London, United Kingdom

## Job Description

**Introduction**

The Bank of England’s Court of Directors is seeking to appoint a new independent member to the Financial Market Infrastructure Committee (FMIC).

The Bank of England sits at the heart of the UK’s economy and financial system. Its mission is to promote the good of the people of the United Kingdom by maintaining monetary and financial stability.

The FMIC was established as a statutory committee of the Bank under the Bank of England Act 1998 (as amended by the Financial Services and Markets Act 2023). The FMIC governs the work of the Bank of England on financial market infrastructure encompassing supervision and policy for payment systems (including stablecoin), central counterparties and central securities depositories.  Its decisions play a crucial role in ensuring the resilience of the systems and markets on which both retail and wholesale users depend.  This is a particularly interesting time given the extent of technological change and innovation taking place across the FMI landscape and a unique opportunity to play a part in a once-in-a-generation modernisation of money and markets.  For more information on the FMIC’s work, see our most recent annual report available here (see here).

The coming period will see the FMIC – along with the Bank’s other policy committees – continue to deal with a wide range of issues. This will include assessing financial and operational risks to the resilience of FMIs and ensuring the Bank’s approach to supervision remains appropriate to the evolving market context. The Committee will continue to embed the new responsibilities of the Bank in relation to rulemaking and the secondary innovation objective through which the Bank seeks to facilitate innovation in the provision of FMI services.

The knowledge and analytical rigour that the independent members bring to bear on the Committee’s work, along with the challenge they provide, ensures that the FMIC’s decision making is robust and effective.

**Appointment description**

Key responsibilities of FMIC Members

• Providing independent challenge, perspective and insights across the breadth of the FMIC’s policymaking and supervisory remit.

• Contributing an understanding of the broader context to FMIC discussions.

• Providing oversight of the FMIC’s strategy and delivery.

**Organisation description**

The FMIC is accountable to Parliament and reports to it annually. The FMIC has several non-delegable responsibilities which include the Bank’s FMI related policy-making functions.

FMIC is chaired by the Governor or Deputy Governor for Financial Stability. Its other members consist of  4 Bank members (including the Bank’s Executive Director for FMI), and at least 3 (currently 4) independent members. The Committee meets regularly to take decisions on rules and on firm-specific issues. In addition, it sets the strategy and approach to supervision.

**Minimum criteria**

* **Strong and proven financial sector knowledge and experience at a senior level**– candidates must have the experience necessary to make independent decisions. They must demonstrate that they have used their financial sector expertise operating at a senior level in or in relation to financial services organisations, ideally financial market infrastructure firms.

**Essential criteria**

* **Decision-making skills** – the FMIC makes decisions that directly affect firms and people.  All members should have strong leadership skills, a strategic mindset, and be ready to take tough decisions and stand by them.

* **Analytical ability**– candidates will need to be able to absorb large volumes of complex information and reach reasoned and robust conclusions.

* **Independence of thought and interpersonal skills** – Candidates must be able to exert influence within the FMIC providing robust challenge whilst working closely and constructively with FMIC members.

* **Excellent communication skills**– the Bank has to communicate with firms, trade associations, civil society, ministers and relevant Parliamentary Committees. External members of the Committee can be called before the Treasury Committee in the Commons and the Financial Services Regulation Committee in the Lords (along with other members) to explain the FMIC’s policies.

* **Undisputed integrity and standing** – candidates should have no reservations about meeting the requirements of the Bank’s Code of Conduct and the Conflicts Code for the FMIC. An assessment of potential conflicts of interest will be undertaken as part of the selection process.

**Desirable criteria**

* An understanding of how regulation can enable responsible innovation and/or influence regulatory approaches in other jurisdictions.

* An understanding of how financial infrastructure firms effectively implement and maintain technology infrastructure, and the opportunities and risks that technological developments may pose for the industry and regulators.

* An understanding of how policy is developed and implemented, including the theory of regulation.

**Appointment terms**

Members will normally be appointed for a fixed term of 3years.  Members may typically serve no more than 2consecutive terms. Members will ultimately be accountable to Court.

**Conflicts of interest**

Members will be subject to FMIC’sconflicts-of-interest policy.  Applicants must declare any actual or potential conflicts before appointment and any conflicts that arise during their term. Candidates should therefore consider carefully whether their existing appointments, responsibilities or interests could affect, or reasonably be perceived to affect, their ability to serve on the committee.

**Time commitment and remuneration**

The anticipated commitment is 30days**.** The pay rate for the role is £31,500 per annum and reasonable expenses will be paid in accordance with Bank policies.

**Diversity and equality of opportunity**

The Bank of England values and promotes diversity and is committed to equality of opportunity.

We believe that drawing on different perspectives, backgrounds and experiences supports effective decision-making and better outcomes for the public. Appointments will be made on merit following a fair and open process.

**How to apply**

Interested candidates should submit their application by completing the application form including the application questions and uploading their CV.

Closing date is **16 November 2026 at 23:59**

**Our Approach to Inclusion**

The Bank values diversity, equity and inclusion. We play a key role in maintaining monetary and financial stability, and to do that effectively, we believe we need a workforce that reflects the society we serve.

At the Bank of England, we want all colleagues to feel valued and respected, so we're working hard to build an inclusive culture which supports people from all backgrounds and communities to be at their best at work. We celebrate all forms of diversity, including (but not limited to) age, disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, race, religion, sexual orientation and socioeconomic status. We believe that it’s by drawing on different perspectives and experiences that we’ll continue to make the best decisions for the public.

Finally, we're proud to be a member of the Disability Confident Scheme. If you wish to apply under this scheme, you should check the box in the ‘Candidate Personal Information’ under the ‘Disability Confident Scheme’ section of the application.

**Security Vetting Process**

**Lead selected strategic People & Culture projects**

• Own a portfolio view of significant People projects, creating clear visibility of scope, outcomes, milestones, owners, risks, dependencies, capacity and decisions alongside the M&A pipeline.

• Balance the broader People project portfolio with M&A demand, identifying resource conflicts and sequencing issues early and bringing clear recommendations to the M&A Director, Chief People Officer and People Leadership Team.

**Support the team to deliver specialist elements of strategic projects**

• Coordinate contributions from People specialists, People Operations, Payroll, Technology, Information Security, Finance, Legal, business leaders, vendors and implementation partners, with each area retaining ownership of its specialist decisions and outputs.

• Support the team to shape employee experience, culture, communications, listening, consultation, manager support, training, readiness and adoption activity as part of the overall project plan.

• Support People Operations, Payroll, Technology and vendors with the project management of People technology, data, payroll, benefits and process change, ensuring requirements, testing, cutover, communications and stabilisation are visible and connected.

• Maintain clear actions, evidence, dependencies and decisions across specialist workstreams without duplicating accountabilities already held elsewhere in the People team.

• Challenge whether proposed change genuinely improves the employee and manager experience and ensure launch is followed by adoption, measurement and appropriate action.

**Build relationships, delivery capability and capacity across both focus areas**

• Remove project-management burden from the Chief People Officer, M&A Director, People leaders and specialists by owning planning, governance, coordination, reporting, dependency management and follow-through.

• Build a broad, trusted network across BKL and acquired businesses, understanding how the organisation works and who needs to be involved to make progress.

• Facilitate workshops, working sessions and decision forums with confidence, including presenting to senior leaders and bringing difficult discussions to a conclusion.

• Create and maintain reusable M&A playbooks, project methods, templates, checklists, dashboards, decision logs and handover standards that improve future delivery.

• Clarify ownership and interfaces between project delivery, specialist teams, People partnering, People Services and business-as-usual operations.

**Working pattern:** Hybrid, minimum three office days per week  
**Contract:** Permanent, full-time  
**Reports to:** Finance and Operations Director

## A bit of background on ELMO UK Group

The ELMO UK Group is growing at around 50% a year, and we’re looking for a Financial Controller who can keep the finance function ahead of that growth.

The Group includes three trading businesses — Breathe, Rotageek and ELMO — as well as a non-trading holding company. Together, the businesses are building a strong position in HR, payroll and workforce management technology, backed by the scale and support of the wider ELMO Group and our K1 private equity owners.

This is an opportunity to join at an important stage of growth. You’ll lead a team of four, own the financial control environment across the UK entities and help shape how finance operates as the business scales.

Confidence can sometimes hold us back from applying for a job. But we'll let you in on a secret: there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. ELMO UK Group is a place where everyone can grow. So however you identify and whatever background you bring with you, please apply if this is a role that would make you excited to come into work every day.

## 🌟Our Values: What We Live By

🫶Start With People - We remember our work affects real people, so we take the time to listen, understand and act with care.

🤝Own It, Together - We take responsibility for our part, support each other through the messy bits, and focus on fixing things rather than finding blame.

🙌Clear Is Kind - We speak honestly and with care. We don’t avoid difficult conversations, and we make sure people have the clarity they need to move forward.

## 🔥Why This Role Is SO Important:

We’re looking for a Financial Controller who can do more than keep the books. You’ll own accounting, controls and reporting across four UK entities and provide the accurate, timely insight that UK leadership and our investors can rely on.

You’ll lead the month-end close, statutory audits, cash management, tax, revenue recognition, controls and core finance operations. At the same time, you’ll help leaders understand what the numbers mean and challenge assumptions around cash, growth, investment and commercial decisions.

The business is growing faster than the team, so scaling through better processes, automation and AI is central to the role. You’ll use Claude to remove manual effort, improve the speed and quality of insight and build that capability across the finance team.

You’ll also play a key role in the finance transformation ahead of us, starting with the move to a new subscription management system and potentially leading into a future ERP migration. This is a hands-on role with real scope to improve how finance works across the Group.

## Key Duties & Responsibilities

Let’s be clear from the start: this isn’t a role where you simply report the numbers after the fact. You’ll build a strong control environment, improve the way finance operates and use insight to help the wider business make better decisions.

Leading the Month-End Close: Owning the close for each entity, including intercompany accounting, balance sheet reconciliations and continuous improvement in close timelines.

Using AI to Improve Finance: Using Claude and other appropriate tools to simplify and automate reconciliations, journals, variance analysis, reporting commentary and audit preparation, while building capability within the team.

Producing Management Accounts: Preparing monthly management accounts and supporting UK Board reporting and reporting packs for K1, with clear commentary on performance against budget and forecast.

Owning Statutory Reporting: Managing annual statutory audits and year-end accounts for every UK entity under FRS 101, from planning through to sign-off.

Managing Company Secretarial Compliance: Managing the third-party company secretarial provider and ensuring statutory filings for all four entities, including Companies House accounts and confirmation statements, are completed accurately and on time.

Managing Cash and Treasury: Owning 13-week cash flow forecasting, banking relationships, mandates, facilities and working-capital discipline.

Overseeing Billing and Credit Control: Managing billing, credit control and debtor management, working with commercial teams to resolve overdue balances and disputes.

Overseeing Accounts Payable: Managing weekly supplier payment runs, ensuring invoices are properly approved, coded and paid on time, and supporting purchase approval workflows and supplier contract reviews.

Calculating Sales Commissions: Calculating sales commissions accurately and on time in line with approved commission plans.

Owning the UK Tax Position: Managing VAT, corporation tax, transfer pricing and R&D tax relief, while identifying tax risks linked to deal structures, cross-border transactions, billing changes and systems.

Managing the Compliance Calendar: Working with external advisers to make sure tax and wider compliance obligations are planned, tracked and completed on time.

Reviewing Payroll: Reviewing third-party payroll output for reasonableness before payments are released.

Ensuring Accurate Revenue Recognition: Making sure SaaS revenue is recognised correctly under IFRS 15, including ARR, deferred revenue and multi-year or complex contracts.

Designing Financial Controls: Creating, documenting and maintaining strong financial controls, approval processes, segregation of duties and audit trails, including appropriate governance over AI-assisted processes.

Leading Finance Transformation: Playing a key role in the migration to a new subscription management system and potentially a future ERP migration, ensuring tax, revenue recognition, billing, reporting and controls are designed correctly from the start.

Maintaining Finance Policies: Drafting or supporting finance and company policies, including expenses, delegated authority, procurement and treasury, and keeping them up to date.

Partnering With the Business: Working with budget holders and senior leaders on forecasting, pricing, enterprise deal structure, contract reviews and investment decisions.

Leading and Developing the Team: Managing, coaching and developing a Senior Accountant, Assistant Accountant and two Finance Assistants, setting clear priorities and building capability as the business grows.

## What Success Looks Like in Your First Six Months

📊A fast, accurate and well-controlled month-end close across all UK entities.

✅Management accounts, Board reporting and investor reporting delivered accurately and on time, with clear insight and commentary.

🔍Statutory audits, year-end accounts, tax obligations and Companies House filings progressing smoothly and reliably.

💷Improved visibility and discipline across cash flow, working capital, billing, debtors and supplier payments.

🤖Practical AI improvements implemented across finance, with Claude helping reduce manual effort and improve insight.

🛡️A strong control environment with clear approvals, segregation of duties, audit trails and appropriate AI governance.

🚀The subscription management system migration progressing with finance, tax, revenue recognition and control requirements built in from the start.

🤝A well-led finance team with clear priorities, growing capability and strong confidence in the way finance operates.

## Key Competencies & Behaviours

You’re technically strong: You have the accounting knowledge and control mindset to own a multi-entity finance function and maintain high standards of accuracy and compliance.

You’re commercially minded: You understand what the numbers mean and can turn financial data into clear insight for leaders making decisions about cash, growth and investment.

You’re comfortable with complexity: You can manage multiple entities, intercompany accounting, SaaS revenue recognition, tax, audit and transformation activity without losing sight of detail.

You’re improvement-focused: You look for ways to simplify, automate and strengthen processes rather than accepting manual work as inevitable.

You’re practical with AI: You use AI tools thoughtfully, understand where human judgement is essential and can help a team adopt new ways of working responsibly.

You’re a clear communicator: You can explain financial information, risks and recommendations to finance and non-finance audiences, including senior leaders, auditors, banks and investors.

You’re a strong people leader: You set clear priorities, coach effectively and help a small finance team develop as the business grows.

You’re confident and constructive: You can challenge assumptions, raise risks early and work collaboratively with commercial and operational stakeholders.

You’re highly organised: You can manage recurring deadlines, statutory obligations, projects and competing priorities with reliable follow-through.

You take ownership: You identify what needs to change, make practical recommendations and stay accountable for the outcome.

# Police Community Support Officer (PCSO)

**Make a difference where it matters most**

Join British Transport Police as a Police Community Support Officer and play a vital role in protecting passengers, supporting communities and keeping the railway safe.

**Location:** Plymouth  
**Salary:** £29,483.96 per year  
**Shift Allowance:** Up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training  
**Annual Leave:**28 days, rising to 30 days with service

**Why become a BTP PCSO?**

Police Community Support Officers are an integral part of British Transport Police.

As a PCSO, you will provide a visible and reassuring presence across the railway network. You will engage with passengers, support railway staff, respond to local concerns and build trusted relationships with the communities we serve.

Chief Superintendent David Rams explains:

*“Our PCSOs are an integral part of British Transport Police. They carry out vital work across the railway network to keep passengers and staff safe, delivering an exceptional service to our communities across England and Wales.”*

**The difference you will make**

As a BTP PCSO, you will help prevent crime, reduce disruption, support vulnerable people and build public trust and confidence across the railway network.

No two days will be the same. You will:

* Conduct visible patrols at stations and across the rail network
* Support victims and provide reassurance to passengers, railway staff and the public
* Assist with minor investigations and intelligence gathering
* Help manage security threats and operational incidents
* Build strong relationships with communities and partner organisations
* Work alongside Police Officers and other policing colleagues
* Help identify and respond to local concerns affecting the railway

**An enhanced operational role**

Unlike PCSOs in many Home Office police forces, BTP PCSOs are trained and equipped with handcuffs. This reflects the distinctive operational environment in which our PCSOs work and the important contribution they make to keeping the railway safe.

**What we are looking for**

We are looking for people who:

* Are resilient and able to remain calm under pressure
* Can communicate confidently with people from different backgrounds
* Demonstrate excellent customer service skills
* Have strong interpersonal and relationship-building abilities
* Are committed to supporting communities and building trust
* Can use good judgement when responding to challenging situations
* Work effectively as part of a team
* Share our commitment to providing an excellent service to the public

You do not need previous policing experience to apply. We are interested in your values, motivation, transferable skills and potential to succeed in the role.

**What you will receive**

In return for the important work you undertake, you will receive:

* A salary of £29,483.96 per year
* A shift allowance of up to 20%, with a minimum of 15% after training
* 28 days’ annual leave, rising to 30 days with service
* Travel benefits
* Ongoing learning and professional development
* Access to in-house talent and development teams
* Career development opportunities across British Transport Police
* A defined contribution pension scheme administered by Royal London

**Develop your career with BTP**

A career as a Police Community Support Officer is rewarding and important in its own right.

PCSOs play a vital role in neighbourhood policing, safeguarding vulnerable people, solving problems within communities and building public trust and confidence across the railway network.

British Transport Police is committed to supporting your long-term development. You will have opportunities to broaden your knowledge, strengthen your operational skills and explore career development opportunities across the organisation.

If you later decide to pursue a career as a Police Constable, successful completion of your PCSO probationary period will also satisfy the work experience requirement for the Police Constable Entry Programme (PCEP).

This is one of several possible development opportunities available to you and does not diminish the importance or professional standing of the PCSO role.

**Working patterns**

Policing the railway requires flexibility.

You must be prepared to work shifts, including weekends and bank holidays. Further information about working patterns will be provided during the recruitment process.

**Before you apply**

Please review the following requirements carefully.

You will not be eligible to apply if:

* You have been unsuccessful at interview for a BTP PCSO role within the last three months
* You have been unsuccessful at the application or online testing stage for a PCSO, Police Officer or Special Constable role within the last three months
* You have failed BTP vetting within the last 24 months
* You have received a custodial or suspended sentence
* You have been dismissed from a police force or are currently under investigation
* You have a current County Court Judgment, unmanaged Individual Voluntary Arrangement or unresolved bankruptcy
* You do not have the right to work in the UK
* You have not lived continuously in the UK for the past three years
* You have tattoos that are considered offensive

*Visible tattoos will be assessed individually.*

**Declaring previous matters**

All cautions, convictions and previous police involvement must be declared as part of your application.

Declaring a previous matter does not necessarily mean that your application will be unsuccessful. Each case will be considered individually.

**At Cancer Research UK, we exist to beat cancer.**

  

As the world’s biggest medical research charity, we’ve helped bring eleven new cancer drugs to market. However, there is still an urgent need to bring more effective treatments to patients faster.

  

We have recently developed a new approach to driving therapeutic innovation through the creation of Cancer Research Horizons (CRH). We have brought together Cancer Research UK’s established drug discovery teams under one organisation and leadership team, combining our unique pipeline of cancer biology expertise and access to CRUK’s world-class academic network, cutting edge technology platforms and clinical expertise to 1) bring new treatments to patients faster and 2) tackle the biggest challenges in discovering cancer drugs by seeking out more radical ideas and embracing risk in our bid to achieve success.

  

Based at sites in Cambridge, the CRUK Scotland Institute in Glasgow and Newcastle University, Cancer Research Horizons employs ~180 staff from both industrial and academic backgrounds.

  

In this role you will support the overarching objective of CRH-TI to discover novel cancer therapeutic agents that will ultimately provide patient benefit. This will involve the prosecution of a laboratory-based project that is designed to expand the Medicinal Chemistry team’s technical capabilities.  
  
The successful candidate will join the Medicinal Chemistry team and will have an opportunity to apply their understanding of organic synthesis in our chemistry labs, working alongside an expert team of Medicinal Chemists.  
  
Potential elements to the project may include:

  

* Development of greener and more sustainable chemistry techniques in our labs, such as electrochemistry and the use of green solvents.

* Route development and synthesis of novel compounds that will add value and diversity to our compound libraries, for use in screening campaigns.

**We have 1 x 52-week placement to offer based in Glasgow, with negotiable start dates in September 2027.**

* Apply organic synthesis knowledge in execution of experiments and interpretation of results

* Maintain awareness of relevant current scientific literature and developments

* Provide verbal and written reports/presentations when required

* Maintain laboratory notebooks and other data to required standards

* Perform all work demonstrating due care and attention to all health and safety regulations

* Ability to provide effective and timely communication of data and progress to your supervisor, and, when required, other members of staff within the chemistry group or wider project team.

* Experience of key organic chemistry techniques

* Setting up and working up reactions

* Purification such as column chromatography

* Analysis (eg. NMR)

* Knowledge of working safely in a lab environment.

* Ability to work effectively with other members of the team and building productive relationships.

* Skills in analysis / interpretation of data and pro-actively contributing to experimental design and strategy.

* Proficiency in organising and planning your daily tasks.

# Head of Quality

Ceres Power is a global leader in solid oxide technology, driving the clean energy revolution. Our steel-supported fuel cell and electrolyser technology gives partners a decade of development advantage, accelerating innovation in power generation, green hydrogen, and distributed power solutions for data centre's. Trusted by some of the world’s most progressive companies, our proven designs deliver efficient, low-cost solutions backed by over 5 million test hours. At Ceres, innovation is in our DNA. Join us and be part of a world-class team making a positive impact on the planet.

**Purpose of the role:**

The Head of Quality will lead the development, implementation and continual improvement of the company-wide Quality Management System, providing quality leadership across R&D, laboratories, pilot and volume manufacturing, supply chain and commercial partner activities. You will ensure that raw materials, chemical formulations, ceramic powders, inks, pastes, components and finished products consistently meet defined product, process, customer and partner requirements, with particular focus on chemical and advanced materials processing, supplier quality, process capability and robust product release.

You will develop and maintain an integrated Quality Management System aligned with ISO 9001 and ISO 14001, ensuring robust and scalable processes for non-conformance, CAPA, change and deviation management, product traceability and release. This will include strengthening supplier and material quality through supplier qualification, certificate of analysis review, appropriate sampling and testing, batch disposition and effective incoming, in-process and finished-product controls.

A key focus will be supporting New Product Introduction (NPI), technology transfer and manufacturing scale-up, ensuring critical material attributes, process parameters, specifications, control plans, validation evidence and release criteria are clearly defined before industrialisation. You will also provide expert quality support to commercial partner development programmes, including material qualification, process validation, specification development and the quality requirements needed for successful technology transfer.

You will ensure laboratory and analytical methods are fit for purpose, controlled and repeatable, supported by appropriate method validation, measurement-system analysis, calibration, reference standards and data-integrity controls. Through Quality Management Reviews and meaningful quality metrics, you will identify risks and trends, address systemic issues and use data and structured problem-solving to improve right-first-time performance, process capability, supplier performance and CAPA effectiveness.

As the senior Quality leader, you will champion a strong quality culture and business process excellence across the organisation, developing capability in areas such as root-cause analysis, risk assessment, SPC and control-plan discipline. You will build and develop a high-performing team spanning quality systems, laboratory, supplier, process and manufacturing quality, with appropriate succession planning for key roles.

**Knowledge and skills required:**

* Several years’ experience in quality leadership within chemical processing, advanced materials, ceramics, coatings, inks, pastes, powders, formulated products or a related process-manufacturing environment
* A proven track record of leading and developing multi-disciplinary Quality teams, covering quality systems, laboratory/analytical, supplier and manufacturing/process quality
* Strong practical understanding of chemical and materials manufacturing, including raw-material variability, formulation and mixing, batch processing, contamination control, scale-up, process capability, sampling, testing, product release and traceability
* Experience managing or assuring quality-control laboratory, analytical and metrology activities, with a good understanding of test-method suitability, measurement uncertainty, repeatability and material/process specifications
* Strong experience maintaining and improving ISO 9001-certified Quality Management Systems, ideally with practical ISO 14001 experience. You’ll be an ISO 9001 Lead Auditor or able to demonstrate equivalent audit leadership; ISO 14001 auditor training would be an advantage
* Strong statistical and process-control capability, including SPC, process capability, Design of Experiments (DoE), measurement-system analysis and structured root-cause analysis. Experience with Minitab or equivalent is preferred, with Six Sigma Green Belt or higher beneficial
* Strong technical-writing skills, with experience producing specifications, control and quality plans, validation protocols and reports, laboratory methods, procedures and customer/partner quality documentation
* A degree or equivalent professional qualification in Chemical Engineering, Chemistry, Materials Science, Ceramics, Process Engineering or a related scientific or engineering discipline
* Experience with digital quality and manufacturing systems, including document control, MES, ERP, SharePoint, process-mapping tools and databases. Knowledge of UK REACH, GB CLP and COSHH would be advantageous
* Most importantly, you’ll bring a hands-on, pragmatic approach, comfortable managing change and complexity in a growing high-technology business and able to introduce scalable, fit-for-purpose quality controls without unnecessary bureaucracy

**About the job**

  

The Head of Internal Communications & Transformation, based in London, is a strategic communications partner to Global Corporate Functions leaders. The role also leads the communication and engagement approach for the corporate community of more than 700 employees.

The role will report into Global Head of Internal Communications, with line management responsibility of two team members.

**What impact you create at Chanel**

  

**Strategic Leadership Communications & Advisory**

* Act as a strategic communications partner to Global Corporate Functions Leaders and management teams, helping them articulate and develop tailored internal communication strategies that support their vision, priorities and transformation agenda.
* Support the preparation and delivery of key leadership communication moments, including Town Halls/leadership meetings.
* Help leaders develop clear and compelling narratives, translating complex strategies and decisions into communications that employees can understand, connect with and act upon.

**Corporate Community Engagement & Employee Experience**

* Define and lead a dedicated engagement approach for Corporate Functions teams across the organisation, ensuring cohesive and connected employee experience across locations.

**Transformation & Change Communications**

* Lead the communications approach for significant transformation and organisational change, working closely with programme leaders and other partners from early planning through implementation.

* Anticipate employee questions and communication risks, ensuring leaders are equipped to communicate confidently and consistently throughout periods of change.

  

**Insight, Measurement & Continuous Improvement**

* Define meaningful measures of communication and engagement effectiveness, using employee feedback, channel insight and engagement data to understand impact.
* Use insight to continuously improve communications, identify emerging needs and inform future strategy.
* Bring thought leadership and best practice into the organisation, identifying new approaches that can strengthen internal communications and employee engagement.

The Multi-Skilled Guarantee is a client-facing technical role responsible for ensuring the readiness, reliability and operational performance of broadcast and live-production systems. Working across vision, RF, IP networking, comms, and 2-way radio systems the role supports preparations, rehearsals and live transmission, providing calm technical leadership and rapid fault resolution in high-pressure environments.
