#### **Live Production Guarantee**

* Operational guarantee: Act as the on-site technical point of contact for assigned systems throughout set-up, line-up, rehearsal, transmission and de-rig, taking ownership of technical readiness and service continuity.
* Pre-production planning: Review briefs, drawings, schedules and technical requirements; identify risks, dependencies, spares and contingency arrangements before deployment.
* System line-up and quality control: Configure, line up and verify signal paths, monitoring, control, timing, synchronisation and comms systems to agreed production standards.
* Live fault response: Monitor system health, diagnose faults quickly and restore service with minimum disruption, communicating clearly with production and technical stakeholders.
* Escalation and handover: Maintain concise fault, change and handover records and escalate recurring or high-impact issues with clear evidence and recommended actions.

#### **Vision and Broadcast Systems**

* Vision systems: Support camera control, monitoring, routing, vision mixing, conversion and distribution. Check picture integrity, colour consistency, reference signals and return feeds.
* Broadcast engineering: Support baseband and IP broadcast infrastructure, including SDI routing, multiviewers, gateways, control systems, monitoring and associated production technology.
* Signal-flow interpretation: Create, interpret and troubleshoot complex signal-flow diagrams across vision, RF, comms and IP layers.
* Technical standards: Apply appropriate broadcast quality-control, safety, testing and documentation standards throughout preparation and delivery.

#### **RF, IP and Comms**

* RF systems: Deploy and support COFDM wireless video, receivers, antennas and associated RF infrastructure. Monitor coverage and spectrum use and resolve interference or degradation.
* Production networks: Configure switches, routers, wireless access points, VLANs, IP addressing, DHCP, DNS and secure production connectivity, including mobile, bonded and satellite solutions.
* Media over IP: Support IP-based media and timing workflows where required, including relevant audio, video, control and synchronisation protocols.
* Crew communications: Deploy and maintain wireless and wired comms systems, including Riedel Bolero or equivalent DECT and partyline platforms. Configure base stations, antennas and belt packs and support users on site.
* Remote support: Provide effective remote diagnosis and support when a deployment does not require a full-time on-site presence.

#### **Equipment Preparation and Technical Support**

* Preparation and testing: Receive, inspect, clean, configure, test and prepare equipment to the agreed brief, ensuring it is accurately labelled, documented and ready for deployment.
* Maintenance and repair coordination: Identify defects, perform first-line maintenance within competence, and ensure repairs, replacements and retesting are tracked through to completion.
* Project support: Work with Production, Kit Room, Engineering and operators to develop the correct technical solution for each job, including recce support, technical drawings and equipment lists.
* Operator and client liaison: Build professional working relationships, translate technical information clearly and provide practical guidance without losing sight of production priorities.
* Training and knowledge sharing: Deliver equipment demonstrations and practical training to team members, operators and production users, and maintain useful technical guidance and handover notes.

* Continuous improvement: Use lessons from live deployments and equipment failures to improve designs, test procedures, stock holdings, contingency plans, cheat sheets and workflows.
* Research and development: Support testing and evaluation of new technology, products and specialist solutions that improve service reliability and expand CineArk’s broadcast capability.
* Company representation: Represent CineArk professionally at client meetings, productions, industry events and trade shows, demonstrating the company’s values and technical credibility.

## Job Purpose Summary

Cables Direct, a division of CMS Distribution, owns three brands: Cables Direct, Cablenet and Newlink. They are sold directly to trade customers through the CMS Store. CMS Distribution is a specialist distributor of business and consumer technology, and where most of its portfolio is vendor brands it represents, these brands are its own.  
We are looking for a Cables Marketing Partner to own marketing for Cables Direct end to end. Because we own these brands, the role works differently from vendor marketing roles elsewhere in CMS Distribution: there is no vendor plan or vendor funding to work to. Success is measured in revenue and gross profit through the CMS Store. The work is continuous trading rather than occasional campaigns: winning new trade customers, converting them, keeping them and bringing lapsed ones back. Your audience is resellers, installers and contractors.  
You will also shape the brands themselves. With no vendor guidelines to follow, you will decide what Cables Direct, Cablenet and Newlink stand for in their market.

## Role Responsibilities

### Trading & Direct Response

* Own the always-on Cables trading calendar in line with business direction: promotions, category pushes, seasonal and stock-led activity, planned quarterly and delivered weekly with the ecommerce team on the CMS Store.
* Own acquisition and retention for the Cables categories on the CMS Store, driving traffic and managing the customer lifecycle. Support conversion, working with the Ecommerce Coordinator and Digital Performance Manager, who own site-wide conversion, on search, site content and product page quality.
* Build and run lifecycle email programmes to the trade base, including onboarding, replenishment, category cross-sell and lapsed-customer reactivation.
* Build and run retention activity across the existing trade base, prioritised by commercial value and relationship history rather than revenue alone.
* Own paid and organic demand generation for the Cables brands within agreed budget, holding each channel to a cost per acquisition and return target.
* Work with the commercial team on promotional mechanics so that activity protects gross profit rather than discounting it away.
* Identify growth opportunities such as trade events, industry bodies and partnerships with wholesalers or complementary brands.

### Own-Brand Development & Category Authority

* Develop and maintain the brand positioning, messaging and visual direction for Cables Direct, Cablenet and Newlink, working with the Creative & Design Partner on execution.
* Own the Cables content programme in line with central marketing and business direction: technical, standards-led material for the reseller or installer who has to specify a product and justify it to their customer, published through email and social media, and on the CMS Store with the ecommerce team.
* Support the ecommerce team on product content for Cables lines on the CMS Store, covering descriptions, specifications, imagery and supporting documentation.
* Contribute to brand architecture decisions as the relationship between the Cables brands and CMS Distribution develops.

### Competitive Position & Sales Support

* Own competitor monitoring for the Cables category, including new market entrants, maintaining a current view of competitor positioning, pricing signals and messaging.
* Produce the sales-facing material account teams use in retention and win-back conversations, grounded in what the business can evidence.
* Feed customer service and operational issues back to the teams that can fix them, rather than covering them with messaging.

## Additional Responsibilities

### Measurement, Data & Reporting

* Report Cables marketing performance against revenue, gross profit, channel targets and engagement metrics, monthly to the business unit and into central marketing reporting.
* Work within the current measurement constraint: Cables marketing currently runs outside HubSpot, so establish and maintain baselines through Qlik, Google Analytics and store reporting, and act as a lead contributor to HubSpot onboarding when it happens.
* Maintain the customer and prospect data the programme depends on, including segmentation of the trade base.
* Apply a test-and-learn approach, recording what was tried and what it produced so that the next decision is better informed than the last.

### Stakeholder Engagement

* Act as the named marketing counterpart for the Cables business unit, working closely with the Business Unit Director and the sales team.
* Operate within central marketing standards for brand, copy, data and campaign process, and bring Cables requirements into central planning.
* Manage the business unit marketing budget agreed with the Business Unit Director, accounting transparently for spend so that it is traceable to activity and to outcome.
* Share best practice with the marketing team and wider organisation, and own additional projects and relationships within CMS as required.

* Direct response and ecommerce marketing capability: able to plan, run and optimise trading activity against revenue and gross profit targets.
* Commercial numeracy, including gross profit, cost per acquisition, return on ad spend, and the trade-off between volume and profitability.
* Strong written communication, including the ability to write credibly for a technical trade audience.
* Analytical capability across Google Analytics, ecommerce reporting and BI platforms such as Qlik, turning data into clear recommendations.
* Hands-on experience of paid search and paid social platforms, such as Google Ads, LinkedIn and Meta, and of an email marketing platform.
* Working knowledge of ecommerce platforms and content management systems, enough to brief and support the ecommerce team on product listings and category pages.
* Brand judgement: able to develop and hold a brand position without a vendor template to follow.
* Comfortable operating with imperfect measurement while working to improve it.
* Ability to build strong relationships across a business unit that sits apart from central marketing.
* Ability to travel on occasion to other CMS sites.

### Qualifications & Experience

* BSc or BA in a relevant field, or equivalent practical experience.
* 3+ years B2B marketing experience, with direct response or ecommerce ownership essential.
* Experience marketing an own-brand or private-label range is highly desirable.
* Experience of a trade, installer or contractor audience is highly desirable.
* IT channel or technical product category experience is desirable.
* Experience with HubSpot or a comparable marketing automation platform is desirable.

Working closely with the Membership Director and key stakeholders, the postholder will lead the future evolution of the Museum and Heritage offering, exploring opportunities to enhance the physical visitor experience, expand digital engagement and interpretation, and maximise the value and reach of MCC's collections through exhibitions, partnerships and research. **Engagement & Partnerships**

* Increase access to the Collections through exhibitions, displays, loans, educational initiatives and outreach programmes, promoting the history and cultural significance of cricket to diverse audiences.
* Develop strategic relationships with collectors, museums, cricketing bodies, educational institutions and cultural organisations to enhance the Collections and strengthen MCC's position as a leader in cricket heritage.
* Lead the development of the Club's heritage publishing and content programme, including digital and print channels.

**Governance & Leadership**

* Provide strategic advice and recommendations to the Heritage & Collections Committee, supporting the delivery of its long-term priorities.
* Act as MCC's senior ambassador for heritage, representing the Club through publications, lectures, media, research and engagement with national and international stakeholders.
* Lead, inspire and develop the Heritage & Collections team, fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration and continuous improvement.

## Job Description

**The Role**

Every clinical trial depends on a commitment to the people who take part: their rights, safety and wellbeing come first, and the data they help generate can be trusted. Once a product reaches patients, that commitment continues through the monitoring of its safety and benefit-risk. This role holds the organisation to both. As Head of Patient-Facing Quality Assurance, you will lead an integrated QA organisation covering Good Clinical Practice and Good Pharmacovigilance Practice, reporting to the Head of Global R&D Quality. Your team will include PV System and Process Leads, Therapeutic Area Quality Leads, and a Head of Clinical QA or of PV and Regulatory QA, depending on which complements your own background.

  

*Hybrid (3 days a week on site), based in Maidenhead, UK, or King of Prussia, PA, with other global locations open to discussion*

  

**Why it matters**

Bringing clinical and pharmacovigilance quality under one leader is a deliberate choice. Some of the most consequential risks sit at the interfaces between them: serious adverse event reconciliation, expedited reporting, and the safety information that reaches investigators and regulators. A single function can see these clearly and act on them. The role is also a chance to shape how quality is done, not just police it. With ICH E6(R3) moving the industry toward Quality by Design and risk-based quality management, you will set the strategy, operating model and standards for how the company protects participants and patients. You will keep the specialist depth that GCP and GVP each need while making the approach consistent worldwide.

  

**What You’ll Be Responsible For**

You will provide independent, risk-based QA oversight from trial design through close-out, and across the global pharmacovigilance system. You will be the consistent quality voice in governance and a constructive challenger to the functions that own operational delivery.

* Setting the strategy, operating model, governance, capabilities and global resource model for Clinical QA and PV QA, harmonising approaches without diluting specialist expertise
* Embedding Quality by Design, critical-to-quality factors and risk-based quality management, and making sure risks to participant safety, patient safety and data integrity are escalated in time
* Assuring the quality systems behind clinical development and pharmacovigilance, including their integration with the enterprise QMS and accurate representation in the Pharmacovigilance System Master File
* Overseeing the clinical safety interfaces: SAE collection and reconciliation, SUSAR and expedited reporting, investigator safety reporting, safety data exchange agreements and signal escalation
* Running a globally consistent framework for significant quality issues, serious breaches, critical deviations and CAPAs, backed by rigorous root-cause analysis and reportability assessment
* Leading GCP and GVP inspection readiness and health-authority inspections, owning the patient-facing audit plan, and giving senior leadership an integrated view of quality risk, trends and regulatory intelligence

  

**Experience Required**

* At least 10 years of progressively responsible experience in pharma, biotech or regulated life sciences, with a degree in life sciences, pharmacy, medicine, nursing or a related discipline (an advanced degree or professional certification in Quality, GCP, GVP or auditing is an advantage)

* Hands-on experience of Quality by Design, risk-based quality management, quality metrics, data integrity and computerised systems, as well as oversight of CROs, vendors, affiliates and partners
* Experience managing budgets, consultants, workforce plans and talent, and building a team of trusted strategic advisers

# Research Scientist, Protein Design & Engineering

## Location

Cambridge, MA; Houston, TX; London, UK

## Employment Type

Full time

OverviewApplication

## About us

We're reverse-engineering the origin of life — one of the great unsolved problems in science, and one we think AI finally makes tractable. Understanding this transition, from geochemistry to biochemistry, is what will let us orchestrate molecular networks and build systems that are more capable, adaptive, and efficient.

If we succeed, the applications are vast: catalysis, green synthesis, ab initio synthetic biology, programmable matter. Understanding and harnessing these processes could let ten billion of us thrive on this planet — and let life keep evolving beyond it.

We're a small, diverse team of AI engineers, computational scientists, and bench scientists. We hold ourselves to the rigor of a research institute, but we ship like an engineering firm. Global team, HQs in Cambridge, MA and London, UK.

**The role**

You'll engineer proteins to carry out useful chemistry, combining enzyme discovery, directed evolution, and experimental characterisation. You'll own the experimental cycle: choosing starting points, building variant libraries, developing screens, and establishing which changes improve function and why.

This is a hands-on role working closely with our computational and ML teams. You'll test designed proteins at the bench, use experimental results to guide subsequent rounds, and develop enzymes with the activity, selectivity, and stability needed for their intended application. There’s no fixed screening pipeline to inherit — you'll help decide how we build it.

**What you'll do**

* Design and run protein engineering campaigns, from initial enzyme selection and library design through screening and characterisation of improved variants.
* Build and express variant libraries using site-directed, random, and combinatorial mutagenesis.
* Develop assays and high-throughput screens that reliably measure the properties we're trying to improve.
* Express, purify, and characterise proteins, measuring kinetics, substrate scope, selectivity, and stability under relevant reaction conditions.
* Work with computational scientists to test proposed designs, interpret successes and failures, and use the results to guide the next round.
* Develop enzymatic reactions and cascades, identifying how enzyme performance, cofactors, and reaction conditions affect overall productivity.

**Essential experience**

We're interested in the engineering campaigns you've run, the assays you've built, and what you learned from them. We care about:

* A track record of improving protein or enzyme function through directed evolution or rational engineering.
* Practical fluency in molecular biology, including cloning, library construction, mutagenesis, and recombinant protein expression.
* Experience developing and troubleshooting enzyme assays and screening workflows, with appropriate controls and follow-up validation.
* A solid grasp of enzyme mechanism, kinetics, and structure–function relationships, and the ability to use these to guide experiments.
* Experience independently taking projects through multiple design–build–test cycles and explaining what drove the results.

**Highly preferred**

* Experience with industrial biocatalysis or engineering enzymes for demanding reaction conditions.
* Experience integrating liquid handling and laboratory automation with high-throughput screening.
* Familiarity with biosensor-based screens, growth-based selection, or FACS.
* Experience testing computationally designed proteins and feeding experimental results back into design.
* Experience with enzyme cascades, fermentation, or transferring enzymatic processes from the bench to larger scales.

## Logistics

Compensation is highly competitive. We're also able to sponsor visas for the right candidate.

# Product Manager, DTCommand

We're looking for a Product Manager to take real ownership of our new innovative customer app, DTCommand, working closely alongside development teams and design rather than sitting apart from them. This is more than managing a backlog: it's being accountable for whether DTCommand genuinely works for our direct and indirect customers and for the business, within the product direction set by the Head of Product.

You'll spend meaningful time with customers, test ideas before committing development time to them, and be trusted to shape not just what gets built, but why. Success in this role looks like DTCommand delivered well and adopted by customers, not simply features shipped on schedule.

This is a new role that is still taking shape, and so is how we work day-to-day: there's no fixed playbook to follow, so we're looking for someone who brings their own structure and good habits, rather than someone who needs a process handed to them.

Whilst initially this role is scoped to DTCommand, there is also the opportunity for the scope to broaden in the future. This role represents a genuine growth opportunity for someone who wants more than a single product to own long term.  
  
  
**Whilst this is a remote role, flexibility to attend our Telford office and meet with customers, partners and suppliers as required is important. We're looking for someone who is proactive in building relationships and maintaining a visible presence across the business, recognising when face-to-face engagement adds value.**

## Key Responsibilities

**Ownership**

* Own the delivery of DTCommand, taking the agreed roadmap through to launch and into live service alongside development teams and design
* Manage the backlog and plan releases, making sure work is clearly defined, scoped, and ready for development teams to deliver
* Track DTCommand's KPIs post-launch and report of the KPIs, flagging where performance points to a change in direction
* Bring customer insight and a delivery perspective into the product direction.

**Customer understanding**

* Build a genuine, ongoing habit of speaking to customers, both direct and indirect, rather than treating it as an occasional check-in
* Use what you learn to sense-check ideas early, through conversations, prototypes, or small experiments, before asking  development teams to build something at full scale
* Take the time to properly understand a problem before jumping to a solution, so the team isn't just building the first idea that comes up

**Working with the team**

* Involve product design & development teams and design early, so their input shapes the solution rather than just its delivery
* Write clear, well-thought-through requirements once direction is set, and stay closely involved through delivery

## **About the team**

Restaurants run on a stack of tools that rarely talk to each other: one for delivery, another for online orders, another for reservations, another for loyalty, and a till that knows nothing about any of them. The same guest can look like three different customers across three different systems.

DashOS is DoorDash's platform for fixing that. It connects marketplace ordering, direct ordering, reservations, loyalty, guest management, marketing and point of sale around one shared view of the guest, so every product gets smarter as the others are used. DashOS Engineering brings together engineers from across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt into one global organisation, led from London. Our teams cover reservations and guest CRM, digital ordering and omnichannel loyalty, POS and self-order kiosks, AI-powered marketing and Voice AI, and the shared data and integration platforms that connect them. Each team owns its own roadmap. The shared mission is making them work as one system.

## **About the role**

We're looking for a backend-focused Software Engineer to build the high-performance, highly available services that restaurants depend on every day, from booking a table on a Friday night to recognising a regular the moment they order. You'll work closely with other engineers, product managers and designers, and because DashOS is newly launched, you'll help shape how its products connect rather than inheriting decisions someone else already made.

## **You're excited about this opportunity because you will...**

* Design, build, test, deploy and improve backend services for customer-facing features used by restaurants and their guests in markets around the world.
* Own features end to end, from technical design through to launch and ongoing support, including taking part in an on-call rotation to keep systems reliable.
* Work on hard problems in data, latency and scale: unifying guest identity across channels, real-time availability search across thousands of venues, and integrations with the systems restaurants already run.
* Build on DoorDash's global platform, so the features you ship can reach restaurants across DoorDash, Deliveroo and Wolt markets rather than being rebuilt for each one.
* Work in a modern engineering environment with frequent daily releases, feature flags and AI coding agents used across code review, deployment and debugging.
* Partner with engineers, product managers and designers across London and other DashOS locations to decide what to build and how.

## **We're excited about you because...**

* You have 3+ years of professional software engineering experience, and a degree in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
* You've built and operated backend services or web applications in production, with strong fundamentals in data structures, algorithms and system design.
* You're fluent in at least one modern backend language (we mostly use Python), and you're happy to pick up new languages and tools as the platform evolves.
* You care about the people using what you build, and you take ownership of technical solutions from first design to production.
* You use AI coding tools as part of how you work, or you're keen to, and you're comfortable reviewing and taking responsibility for what they produce.
* You enjoy collaborating with cross-functional teams to solve problems that don't have an obvious answer yet.

## **Tech you'll work with**

Our services are built mainly in Python, with performance-critical systems in Rust, running on Google Cloud and DoorDash's global platform. AI coding agents are part of how we design, review and ship code, so we care more about how you solve problems than about which languages you've used before. You won't need to know every part of the stack on day one.

## **Where and how we work**

This role is based in our London office at The River Building, on a hybrid pattern of 3 days a week in the office.

## **About SevenRooms**

In 2011, Joel Montaniel, Allison Page, and Kinesh Patel founded SevenRooms after noticing that hospitality operators were missing a critical ingredient in the systems they were using to run their business: guest data. What began as a mission to help restaurants better understand and serve their guests evolved into a powerful platform used by merchants around the world.

With best-in-class tools for marketing, operations, and guest experience — all deeply integrated with its industry-leading CRM — SevenRooms empowers operators to drive revenue, streamline operations, and deliver experiences that keep guests coming back.

In 2025, DoorDash acquired SevenRooms to strengthen its in-store strategy and expand its merchant-first offerings. The combination brings together DoorDash’s scale, reach, and digital innovation with SevenRooms’ in-store capabilities to support hospitality businesses across every channel — from discovery and delivery to on-premise dining.

As DoorDash builds out its in-store capabilities, SevenRooms plays a central role in enabling merchants to grow their businesses and connect more meaningfully with guests, whether they’re ordering online or dining in. job_description:
At easyJet, we are transforming Airline Operations through modern product-led technology, operational excellence, automation, data, and AI-enabled capabilities. The Airline Operations Platform serves as the single point of contact for the applications and source data keeping our network flying—owning critical crew, flight planning, network control, and engineering systems like AIMS, TOPS, LIDO, and AMOS.
We are seeking a visionary Platform Lead – Data Availability, API & Integration to join our platform leadership team. In this critical role, you will own the integration strategy and data availability capability end to end. You will lead a high-performing team of Platform Engineers and Integration Specialists to deliver the APIs, event streams, operational data stores, and feeds that safely connect vendor systems with our internal products and missions.
Your non-negotiable principle: systems of record stay protected with their vendors, and our internal engineering teams consume platform-mediated interfaces—never direct connections.
Key Responsibilities
As the capability owner, you will treat the interface estate as a product—ensuring it is documented, discoverable, versioned, and self-service for mission engineers. Your core focus areas will include:
Integration Strategy & Adoption: Develop, maintain, and publish the integration strategy in tight alignment with our architecture community. Translate this strategy into practical, adopted patterns, reference implementations, and templates that engineers can readily follow.
Capability & Product Delivery: Lead the roadmap and backlog for all APIs, event streaming, operational data stores, and feeds. Drive a strict "reuse-first" mindset to scale capabilities across multiple missions while reducing bespoke point-to-point interfaces.
Source Data Availability: Ensure the absolute availability, timeliness, and integrity of operational data. Maintain the boundaries of production and API delivery while partnering smoothly with Enterprise Data on overarching governance.
Operational Health & Resilience: Own the uptime, performance, and latency of the interface estate. Set non-functional standards for timeouts, retries, and dead-letter handling, while building deep observability into the system to catch defects before the operation feels them.
Engineering Leadership: Line manage, coach, and scale a technical bench of Platform Engineers and Integration Specialists. Actively eliminate single points of failure, foster a culture that finishes the "unglamorous parts" (monitoring, logging, error handling), and support contractor-to-permanent transitions.
Vendor Collaboration: Own the technical relationships with key vendors regarding endpoint constraints, rate limits, and API maturity. Ground your discussions in clear technical data to influence vendor roadmaps in favour of our architectural needs.


Who You Are
You are a strong, technically grounded leader who balances architectural health and long-term tech debt with the commercial realities of operating a high-volume, low-cost airline. You have the credibility to hold a technical position under pressure and the operational discipline required for a 24x7 mission-critical environment.

Enterprise Integration Mastery: Proven experience owning an API/integration capability, defining strategy, and driving pattern adoption across distributed engineering teams.
Deep Technical Expertise: Strong background in API design/management, event-driven architecture, message brokers, and operational data store concepts.
System Boundary Governance: Experience creating mediated interfaces to abstract vendor-managed systems, including strict control over write-backs and separating read paths from commits.
Modern Engineering Practices: Direct exposure to cloud platform services (ideally Azure), automated testing, CI/CD, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC).
Operational & Resilience Rigour: Proven success building and supporting interfaces for a live 24x7 environment, including error-handling standards, disaster recovery testing, and on-call rotations.
People & Matrix Leadership: Strong experience line-managing engineers, prioritizing a backlog against competing timelines, and working collaboratively within an architecture community.
Desirable Attributes:
Background in aviation, airline operations, or complex transport logistics environments.
Familiarity with industry-relevant platforms (AIMS, TOPS, LIDO, AMOS) or integrating aviation data feeds (weather, air traffic control).
Experience establishing an API-first or platform-as-a-product ecosystem featuring published catalogues and self-service onboarding.
Formal architecture training or certification, alongside a grounding in ITIL frameworks.

A high-impact role driving a core pillar of tech transformation at one of Europe’s leading airlines.

**Purpose**

The Associate Director, Sustainable Project Procurement (AD-SPP) leads the Bank’s thematic approach to sustainable and strategic project procurement across public sector operations. The role provides authoritative advice on procurement policy, standards, governance and risk; shapes the development and consistent implementation of the Bank’s Procurement Policies and Rules (PPR), associated guidance and operational standards; and leads significant initiatives relating to sustainable procurement, circular economy, low-carbon procurement and value for money.

Working across the project lifecycle, the Associate Director oversees the application of sustainability and strategic procurement requirements in complex Bank-financed operations, provides expert judgement on significant compliance, assurance and implementation matters, and engages with senior Bank management, governance bodies, clients, implementing agencies, MDB peers and other external stakeholders. ## About Eigen ltd

Eigen is a specialist software and engineering company delivering innovative digital solutions to the energy and process industries. Our technology helps customers improve operational efficiency, safety and decision-making through the integration, visualisation and analysis of complex industrial data.

Our flagship software platform, **Eigen Ingenuity**, integrates operational data from industrial systems and enterprise applications to provide advanced visualisation, analytics and workflow capabilities.

As our customer base and software deployments continue to grow, we are strengthening our capability to manage, maintain and continuously improve the applications we deliver.

## The Role

We are seeking an experienced **Application Operations Manager** to take responsibility for coordinating the operational management and continuous maintenance of Eigen’s software solutions deployed across our customers.

This is not a traditional IT support management position. The focus is on **Application Management, DevOps coordination, software reliability and continuous maintenance**, ensuring that our applications remain secure, up to date, reliable and fully functional.

The successful candidate will act as the central coordination point between Eigen’s **Customer Support, DevOps and Software Development teams**, as well as customers’ IT and technical departments.

The role combines technical understanding, analytical problem-solving, operational ownership and cross-functional coordination. The Application Operations Manager will ensure that operational issues are correctly diagnosed, prioritised, assigned and resolved, while driving proactive maintenance and improvements to prevent recurring problems.

## Key Responsibilities

**Application Management and Operational Coordination**

* Take ownership of the operational management of Eigen’s deployed software applications, ensuring their continued availability, performance, security and reliability.
* Act as the principal coordination point between Customer Support, DevOps and Software Development teams for operational and maintenance issues.
* Oversee the operational issue lifecycle, from initial identification and triage through investigation, escalation, resolution and closure.
* Establish clear ownership, priorities and accountability for operational tasks involving multiple teams.
* Monitor outstanding issues, identify bottlenecks and ensure timely resolution in accordance with contractual commitments and agreed service levels.
* Maintain visibility of the operational health of customer deployments and report on recurring issues, risks and maintenance priorities.

**Continuous Software Maintenance and Vulnerability Management**

* Coordinate the continuous maintenance of Eigen’s deployed software, including security patches, dependency updates, version upgrades and technology lifecycle management.
* Work with DevOps and Software Development to identify, assess and prioritise software vulnerabilities and technical maintenance requirements.
* Coordinate the planning, testing and deployment of software updates, ensuring that customer environments remain secure and supported.
* Track remediation activities and ensure that security vulnerabilities are addressed within agreed timeframes.
* Oversee compatibility assessments and upgrade planning for underlying technologies, frameworks, libraries and application components.
* Coordinate maintenance windows, release readiness, rollback arrangements and communications with customers where required.
* Help reduce technical debt and promote standardised, automated and repeatable maintenance processes.

**Data Connectivity and Integration Management**

* Coordinate the investigation and resolution of issues affecting the availability, quality or integrity of data feeding Eigen applications.
* Work across Eigen’s teams and customers’ IT departments to diagnose connectivity failures, authentication problems, interface errors, data interruptions and other integration issues.
* Understand and help troubleshoot integrations involving industrial data historians, Data Lakes such as Cognite CDF, Databricks, etc.;  APIs and other enterprise systems, including AVEVA PI, Aspen InfoPlus.21 and SQL databases.
* Ensure clear assignment of responsibilities when issues originate in customer-managed infrastructure or third-party data sources.
* Coordinate incident resolution across organisational boundaries and maintain effective communication with affected stakeholders.
* Identify recurring connectivity problems and recommend monitoring, resilience and preventive improvements.

**DevOps and Application Reliability**

* Coordinate the investigation of issues identified through application monitoring, automated alerts, logging and deployment pipelines.
* Ensure that build failures, unsuccessful deployments, unhandled exceptions, backend errors and application performance issues are investigated and addressed by the appropriate teams.
* Work with DevOps engineers to understand and resolve problems associated with CI/CD pipelines, containerised applications, Kubernetes and cloud environments.
* Support effective root-cause analysis and ensure that corrective and preventive actions are implemented.
* Promote improvements in application observability, automated logging, alerting and deployment tracking.
* Help establish a proactive operational environment in which emerging problems are identified and addressed before they affect customers.

**Advanced Customer Support and Technical Escalation**

* Act as an escalation point for complex customer questions or technical issues that cannot be resolved through routine first-line support.
* Coordinate investigations requiring input from several technical disciplines, ensuring customers receive clear and consistent responses.
* Develop sufficient familiarity with Eigen’s software capabilities, architecture and integrations to distinguish between configuration issues, software defects, infrastructure problems and enhancement requests.
* Work with Product Management and Software Development to determine whether reported issues require defect correction, configuration changes or product enhancements.
* Ensure that customer-facing technical explanations are accurate, understandable and delivered promptly.
* Support the continuous development of technical knowledge bases, troubleshooting procedures and operational documentation.

**Operational Processes and Continuous Improvement**

* Develop and maintain effective processes for application incident management, problem management, change coordination and software maintenance.
* Define and track operational KPIs, including incident resolution times, vulnerability remediation, recurring failures, deployment reliability and maintenance backlog.
* Promote the use of automation and self-monitoring capabilities to reduce routine manual support activities.
* Identify recurring operational problems and drive permanent solutions rather than repeated reactive interventions.
* Coordinate operational readiness for new customer deployments and major software releases, ensuring appropriate monitoring, documentation and support arrangements are in place.
* Provide regular reporting to management on application health, operational risks, maintenance activities and opportunities for improvement.

## Required Skills & Experience

* Minimum **5–6 years of relevant experience** in DevOps, software engineering, application operations, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) or advanced application support.
* Strong understanding of the software development lifecycle, release management and modern application deployment practices.
* Practical experience working with CI/CD pipelines, automated builds, deployment processes and troubleshooting failed releases.
* Working knowledge of cloud technologies, preferably Microsoft Azure, and container orchestration technologies such as Docker and Kubernetes.
* Experience with application monitoring, logging, exception handling and root-cause analysis.
* Understanding of software vulnerability management, patching, dependency upgrades and secure software maintenance.
* Good technical understanding of APIs, SQL databases, network connectivity and application integrations.
* Experience coordinating technical issues across software development, infrastructure, DevOps and customer-facing teams.
* Ability to understand complex technical problems, ask the right questions and engage effectively with specialist engineers.
* Strong organisational, prioritisation, analytical and communication skills.
* Experience working directly with customers and their IT departments to resolve technical issues.
* Excellent written and spoken English.

## Desirable Experience

* Experience in industrial software, operational technology (OT), energy or process industries.
* Familiarity with AVEVA PI, Aspen InfoPlus.21 or comparable industrial data platforms.
* Experience with Microsoft Azure application hosting and cloud security.
* Knowledge of infrastructure-as-code, automated deployment tools and modern observability platforms.

* Knowledge of ISO 27001 security management principles and vulnerability remediation processes.
* Familiarity with agile software development methodologies and tools for issue tracking and development planning.

## Job Description

**Could you be the technical expert who shapes how our solar and battery storage projects connect to the grid, guiding critical engineering decisions from early feasibility through to energisation?**   
We're looking for a Senior HV Engineer to join our Elgin's Engineering team as the in-house technical authority for grid connection and HV engineering across our utility-scale solar PV and co-located BESS projects in the UK and Ireland, with the potential to support Elgin's projects in Italy. The role follows the project lifecycle: grid feasibility and connection optioneering, development-stage engineering to support consents, land and grid applications, technical specification for procurement, and technical assurance of the contractors' design, construction and energisation. Elgin does not carry out detailed design in-house; detailed design and construction are delivered by ICP, iDNO and EPC contractors against Elgin's Employer's Requirements.  
   
   
The focus of the role is engineering and de-risking from the earliest stage of a project: bringing the grid engineering into development so that the connection method, cable route and substation requirements are settled through the feasibility work, planning applications, land agreements and grid applications rather than discovered later; making sure each connection is technically deliverable and that the contestable / non-contestable scope split is right before it is fixed in budgets and contracts; and assuring that the designs produced by ICPs, iDNOs and consultants meet Elgin's Employer's Requirements and the network operator's standards. Commercial and programme management of the DNO / TSO relationship sits outside of this role; this role provides the engineering judgement behind it.  
   
   
Elgin does not design or build its projects itself: it sets the technical requirements and its contractors deliver against them. The value of this role is in setting those requirements well and in challenging what consultants and contractors deliver. You will be the technical escalation and decision on HV and grid matters and the primary technical contact for Elgin's development-stage consultants and ICPs.

**What you will do:**  
  
**Development stage**  

* Lead the technical side of connection method and grid route optioneering for Development: scope and direct the feasibility studies, judge overhead line, underground cable and hybrid options on constructability, consentability, land take and cost, and recommend the option to take forward.
* Get the grid engineering into the development case early, so that it is reflected in consents and land rather than discovered at procurement: define the substation footprint, cable route corridor and crossing strategy for planning applications and consents, provide the technical input to land, wayleave and easement discussions, and prepare the technical inputs to grid connection and modification applications (DNO / NESO in GB, ESB Networks / EirGrid in Ireland).
* Produce concept-level single line diagrams, substation layouts and route corridors with the CAD team, to the level needed for feasibility, planning and tender purposes only; detailed design sits with the ICP, iDNO and EPC contractors. Discharge Elgin's CDM 2015 designer duties for the concept designs it produces.
* Act as primary technical contact for Elgin's development-stage consultants on cable routes, HV design and power system studies: define technical scopes, review deliverables and challenge conclusions before they enter project decisions. This is development-stage consultancy; detailed design is delivered by the EPC and ICP contractors.
* Specify and review the cable modelling, ampacity and losses studies (MV through 132 kV, and 220 kV in Ireland) carried out by consultants and contractors, and make sure the results feed the design basis, CAPEX and energy yield assumptions.
* Set and challenge the technical grid CAPEX assumptions and the engineering basis of the connection programme as they enter the investment case, and produce the technical reports, planning inputs and position papers that stand up to Investment Committee and lender scrutiny.

  
**Grid connection**  

* Technically interpret connection offers, Connection Agreements and technical schedules, on Elgin's own projects and in acquisition due diligence: what they commit Elgin to, where the contestable / non-contestable boundary sits, and the omissions, abnormal costs and onerous conditions behind them.
* Review and challenge network study outputs (fault level, harmonics, reactive capability, protection) and turn them into Employer's Requirements and contestable / non-contestable scope decisions for the ICP and EPC turnkey contracts.
* Own the contestable / non-contestable / Contractor interface on each project: define and record the scope split and close gaps and duplication between DNO, iDNO, ICP and EPC scopes before they become variations.
* Ensure the G99 / Grid Code compliance obligations in the Connection Agreement are allocated between the ICP and EPC scopes in the ERs and DoR, and own Elgin's technical compliance position with the network operator as the connection customer; lead any derogation application on Elgin's behalf, and witness compliance testing where required.

**Procurement and contracts support**  

* Author and maintain the HV and grid sections of Elgin's Employer's Requirements and Division of Responsibilities matrix, and support Procurement through ICP, iDNO and EPC tendering, evaluation and technical negotiation.

  
**Construction, commissioning and energisation (assurance and escalation)**  

* Assure the contractors' HV and grid design rather than produce it: make sure ICP, iDNO and EPC design submissions are reviewed against Elgin's Employer's Requirements and the network operator's standards (through the Owner's Engineer where one is appointed), decide Elgin's position on deviations with a reasoned justification, and close out Owner's Engineer comments.
* Act as Elgin's technical escalation point for the Project Engineers, the Owner's Engineer and the PMA through construction, commissioning and energisation: decide Elgin's response where site works deviate from design intent or the Connection Agreement, review the contractors' Grid Code compliance and energisation submissions before they go to the network operator, and attend key witness tests. Day-to-day technical queries and routine witnessing sit with the Owner's Engineer and the contractors.

  
**Ongoing**  

* Maintain Elgin's HV and grid engineering standards, templates and lessons learned, keep abreast of DNO / TSO standards and policy change.

## Your profile

* BEng / MEng in Electrical Engineering, Power Systems or a related discipline.
* Extensive HV and grid connection engineering experience (MV through 132 kV), including delivered UK utility-scale solar, BESS or ICP / DNO connection projects through to energisation.
* Detailed working knowledge of the GB connection process: G99, Connection Agreements and technical schedules, contestable and non-contestable works, the ICP and iDNO model, DNO design approval and adoption, and derogations.
* Experience of development-stage grid work: connection and modification applications, connection offer assessment, connection method and route optioneering, and technical inputs to planning applications and land agreements.
* Ability to read and challenge network study outputs and translate them into design and scope decisions.
* Strong HV design review capability: switchgear and protection, earthing, HV cables and routes, HDD and crossings, substations and transformers, metering, auxiliary supplies, SCADA / telecoms.
* Experience authoring or reviewing Employer's Requirements and Division of Responsibilities under EPC and ICP contracts, and scoping and challenging external consultants.
* Ability to translate technical decisions into CAPEX, programme and risk implications and communicate them clearly, in writing and in person, to non-technical stakeholders.
* Ability to specify, review and challenge cable modelling, ampacity and losses studies and power system studies, with working familiarity with AutoCAD and power system analysis tools.
* Full driving licence and willingness to travel to project sites in the UK and Ireland as required.

**Desirable**  

* Chartered Engineer (CEng) or working towards chartership.
* Irish connection experience (ESB Networks / EirGrid, CRU policy, ECP and RESS delivery) and transmission-level (110 kV to 220 kV) experience.
* BESS and co-located hybrid connections, including Grid Code compliance for storage.
* Power system modelling (DIgSILENT PowerFactory, ETAP or PSCAD); technical due diligence for acquisitions or lenders; CDM 2015 designer duties.
* Experience across multiple network operators (NGED, UKPN, SPEN, NPg, SSEN) and National Grid / NESO.
* Exposure to the Italian connection process (Terna and the distribution operators) for solar or BESS projects.

**About Elgin**

Elgin is a fully integrated, utility-scale solar and storage Independent Power Producer, developing, building, owning and operating renewable energy assets across the UK, Ireland, Germany, and Italy. With a 10GW+ pipeline spanning solar, co-located and standalone storage projects, Elgin brings projects from origination through development to energisation and long-term operation.

**Role Overview**

Eutelsat is seeking a engineers to work on the Physical Layer and Air Interface of both our commercial next-generation satellite communications system and the European Union’s IRIS2 system (which Eutelsat are supporting in their capacity as a member of SpaceRise).

Working within the wider System Engineering team and more broadly with our vendor, these engineers would be responsible for making key design choices on the Air Interfaces of both systems, on both the user and feeder links but these decisions need to be backed up by through quantitative and qualitative analysis.

**Key Responsibilities**

The combination of the two engineers should take on these responsibilities with the more senior role including mentoring and supervising the other engineer while both work together to achieve these.

* Physical Layer Software simulation:
  + Build a software simulator of the user link physical layer (based on 5G)
  + Build a software simulator of the feeder link physical layer (based on DVB-S2X or similar)
  + Use these tools to assess the impact of channel impairments and equipment RF performance (e.g. multipath / phase noise / group delay / frequency)
  + Use these tools to assess the system level impact (overhead / throughput etc.) of various implementations of physical layer features and procedures (e.g. ACM / HARQ / DFT-S-OFDM vs CP-OFDM)
* Air Interface Requirements
  + Establish the technical requirements for the air interfaces that our vendors need to meet for the system to work as expected.
  + Determine how the performance of the air interfaces should be validated at each stage of the programme.
  + Assess the feasibility of vendor proposed solutions to meet these requirements
  + Understand how vendor non-compliance may affect the overall system and work with the vendors to mitigate the impact.

**Required Experience**

* **Digital Communications Systems**
  + Strong understanding of the physical layer of digital communication systems, including modulation, coding, synchronization, equalization, channel estimation etc.
  + Understanding of RF impairments and their impact on air interface performance, including phase noise, frequency / doppler errors, non-linearities, and interference.
  + Experience of working with lab equipment to troubleshoot communications systems
* **Programming Skills**
  + Experience with using at least of the following for physical layer or similar signal processing modelling (note: it’s an internal tool so it doesn't need to be beautiful code – it needs to answer questions quickly!)
    - C++
    - MATLAB
    - Julia
    - Python (inc. NumPy / SciPy)

* **5G or DVB Standards Familiarity**

* + Experience working with systems based on either 3GPP standards or DVB standards
  + A deep understanding of the physical layer of at least one of the above and why they were designed the way they are.

* **Qualifications**

+ A degree in telecommunications, electrical engineering, computer science, or a related discipline**.**

**Desirable Experience**

* Use of Software-Defined Radio toolkits (e.g. GNU Radio)
* Real-world modem implementation various hardware platforms (DSPs, FPGAs, RF SoCs etc.)
* Satellite communications experience

**Candidate Profile**

A physical layer domain expert who really understands what’s going across the air interface and is comfortable interacting with vendors at a highly technical level. However, the same person needs to explain options and choices to non-experts in the rest of the company.

**The Opportunity**

  

Come join our engineering team in a hands-on technical role at the heart of a new discipline: Harness Engineering. As AI coding agents take on more of the software lifecycle, the hard part is no longer writing code - agents generate it faster than humans can review it, so the bottleneck shifts to verification and trust. Harness Engineering exists to break that bottleneck: engineering the environment that steers agents toward correct, maintainable, well-architected output so that quality is enforced by the system, not re-audited by a person on every change. We call that environment the harness (Agent = Model + Harness). As a Senior Harness Engineer you'll independently own whole harness subsystems, set the standards other engineers build to, and be involved in the end-to-end lifecycle of turning raw model capability into production-grade engineering.

  

**What You’ll Contribute**

* Design, build, deploy, and support core components of the harness - the guides, feedback loops, guardrails, and shared context that turn raw model capability into production-grade engineering. This is a hands-on role focused on systems and leverage, not hand-writing application code.
* Own and evolve feedforward guides - agent instruction files, reusable skills, architectural rules, reference docs, and codemods - and drive team-wide standardisation so agents get it right the first time.
* Build feedback sensors - custom linters, static analysis, structural and architecture-fitness tests, verification loops, and LLM-as-judge reviewers - that catch issues automatically before they reach human reviewers.
* Own quality gating and release criteria for agent-produced work, defining authority boundaries for what agents may merge unaided and the escalation rules for what must route to a human.
* Establish LLM testing infrastructure and evaluation approaches that ensure AI-generated output meets quality and safety thresholds; apply consumer/contract testing (e.g. Pact) where service integration reliability matters.
* Run the steering loop - when an agent repeats a mistake, engineer a control so it can't happen again - and treat repository knowledge (docs, specs, context) as the system of record, fighting drift with continuous garbage collection.
* Decide where each control runs in the path to production - fast checks pre-commit, more expensive checks post-integration, and continuous sensors that scan for drift outside the change lifecycle - keeping quality as far left as is economical.
* Improve observability into agent work and track the measures that matter - cost per merged PR, time-to-merge for agent-assisted PRs, review velocity relative to PR size, defect escape rate, and agent-PR survival rate - using them to decide where to invest next.
* Partner with product and platform teams to turn specifications and acceptance criteria into enforceable controls.
* Serve as a source of technical expertise and mentor engineers across teams in harness practices and the effective, responsible use of AI tools.

  

**What We’re Seeking**

* Bachelor's/Master's in Computer Science or related disciplines, or relevant commercial experience in software architecture, design, development, and testing.
* Seasoned software engineer with experience in large, complex codebases and a strong foundation in architecture and design; you care deeply about testing and maintainability.
* Hands-on experience with AI coding agents (e.g. Claude Code, Codex, or similar) and a well-developed feel for where they succeed and fail.
* Proven ability to build engineering tooling across a modern stack - linters and static analysis, CI/CD pipelines, containerised build/test environments, and instrumentation/observability - plus familiarity with agent instruction conventions such as AGENTS.md.
* Experience with spec-driven development, context engineering, agent orchestration, fitness functions, and developer-platform work.
* A systems mindset - you'd rather fix the environment than fix one output - and the ability to encode "what good looks like" into mechanical, repeatable rules.
* Judgement about when to reach for deterministic, computational controls (type checkers, linters, structural/architecture-fitness tests) versus inferential, LLM-based ones (AI code review, LLM-as-judge) - and an understanding of the cost, speed, and reliability trade-offs between them.
* Experience owning quality-gating processes and defining release criteria to ensure engineering standards are consistently met.
* Working knowledge of the security surface unique to autonomous agents - prompt injection, tool/permission scoping, sandboxed execution, and audit trails for agent actions - and how to design least-privilege guardrails around them.
* Experience with consumer/contract testing approaches (e.g. Pact) to validate service integrations across distributed systems.

# The FT World Desk Fellowship

United Kingdom

**About us**

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*

**Our commitment to inclusion and fairness**

We believe everyone should have a fair opportunity to contribute, succeed, and reach their full potential. That means ensuring everyone is heard, respected, and valued, while identifying and removing barriers that may get in the way. Our commitment is to be an employer role model, grounded in inclusion and fairness for all.

We want every application to receive fair and thoughtful consideration; therefore, all applications are reviewed by a member of our recruitment team, not by AI.

**The Financial Times has an exciting opportunity for aspiring Black foreign correspondents.**

Are you keen to report on the world at this time of tumult? Are you excited by international news and do you want a hand in interpreting and explaining it to a global audience? Are you tempted by the idea of a wide-ranging career in journalism reporting on dramatic events from across the globe? If so, then our new six-month World Desk fellowship would suit you well.   

The FT’s global, award-winning editorial team represents the gold standard in journalism, seeking depth, originality and balance that differentiates the FT from the pack and engages subscribers.

The Fellowship is a six-month, paid fellowship in the heart of the FT’s London newsroom. You will join the World News Desk, where a dozen-strong team of accomplished journalists commission and edit our global coverage.   

You will work with the editors to help deliver ground-breaking coverage. You will also work closely with our London-based regional editors, the Africa Editor, Europe Editor, Latin America Editor and Middle East Editor, helping them with their coverage.

You will support the global network of correspondents with research and ideas for how to complement their stories with the right data and visual elements. You will be encouraged to write your own stories and will have mentoring from senior FT editors, in particular the foreign editor, in how to conceive and craft an “FT story”.

**What You Will Learn**

You will be part of a team of experienced journalists covering the world, and there may also be opportunities for short-term stints on other editorial desks. You will learn the timeless arts of writing clear crisp copy and reporting on complex and sensitive stories. 

You will also gain insight into the essential skills of cutting-edge digital journalism and story-telling. The overarching ambition of the fellowship is to help to equip you one day to be a foreign correspondent, hopefully for the FT.

**Knowledge, Skills and Experience**

The successful candidate will:

* Display a keen interest in international affairs
* Want to pursue a career in journalism covering global news
* Be capable of keeping a cool head under deadline pressure
* Care deeply about writing accurately and objectively

Some experience in journalism is preferable but not essential. Career change applications are also welcome.

This opportunity is designed for Black candidates to help to address historical under-representation in the media, and to support greater diversity.

**How to apply**

All applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom.

Please upload **three documents**:

* **CV**
* **A Cover Letter detailing what you will bring to the role and why you think you are suitable**
* **An unpublished article on an international story (600 words max)**

The deadline for applications is 8pm on Sunday 15th November 2026.

**Further information**

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to an interview and to take a short writing test. The successful applicant will join the World News Desk and report to the FT’s Foreign Editor, Alec Russell.  

This 6-month fellowship is for 35 hours per week, Monday to Friday, starting in Spring 2027.

The fellow will receive a monthly bursary of £2,500.

**The use of AI**

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism.  Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

**Accessibility**

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Enterprise AI is GSK’s centre of gravity for applied artificial intelligence. **Position Summary**   
GSK’s Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. The Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) is the engineer GSK sends in to find out whether an AI idea will work — embedded with business unit (BU) teams, proving ideas through proofs of concept (PoCs), proofs of value (PoVs), and minimum viable products (MVPs) at a days-to-weeks cadence, then handing the proven solution off to the Sr. Solutions Engineer for scale-up. The pattern is proven by AI-native companies — Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI — and this role brings that model to GSK.

  

This specific role sites in the Chemical Manufacturing & Control (CMC) area. This is the GSK function that turns a validated molecule into a reliably manufactured, quality-assured medicine; its mission is to get safe, effective, consistently manufactured medicines to patients, faster. Its current mission is to double New Product Introductions (NPIs).

  

As a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll be embedded in a team shaping how AI transforms GSK’s process development around the world. Most prototyping work is AI-augmented: AI coding assistants and multi-agent workflows handle the bulk of routine coding, freeing the FDE to focus on framing, judgement, and validation. The role works directly inside the customer’s business and emerges with working software and a defensible value hypothesis, not slideware. The FDE does not carry use cases through to long-term operations and partner with the Sr. Solutions Engineer is part of the role.

  

This role will build Physical AI capabilities to create self-driving labs and simulated tech transfers. You will work on orchestration of the physical space from the digital space. You will simulate the functioning of labs and a transfer to a line via virtual commissioning and Omniverse representations. This will support the ambitions of higher throughput and one-click deployment of a line. You will work hand in hand with the automation business and tech teams across R&D and manufacturing. PoC / PoV / MVP Delivery

AI-Native Engineering

* Operate AI agent workflows (planning, coding, testing, review, documentation) for autonomous prototype delivery — selecting the right level of automation for each engagement.
* Use AI coding assistants as the default mode of building; provide judgement, course correction, and validation.

Customer Embedding & Handoff

* Embed with BU teams — attend standups, understand the domain, prototype against real data and real workflows.
* Package proven use cases cleanly for the Sr. Solutions Engineer — working code, architecture rationale, open risks, and scaling concerns.

Governance, Standards & Coaching

* Begin Code Orange, Responsible AI, and Accountability Report conversations during prototyping — so the productionisation team does not inherit governance debt.
* Contribute reusable agents, prompt templates, and reference architectures to the organisation’s pattern library after each engagement.

* Coach BU engineers on AI-augmented ways of working while embedded, building BU capability alongside delivery outcomes.
