# Staff Technical Programme Manager, Systems Software

Oxford, England, United Kingdom

**About IonQ:**

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.  
  
Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

**Role:**

System Software builds the software that runs IonQ's quantum computers: the runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport software that sit between the Quantum Operating System and the hardware. It is where a next-generation system either comes together or doesn't.

We're hiring a Staff Technical Programme Manager to lead delivery across this stack. You'll report to the Group Program Manager, Software in our Programme Management Office and be matrixed to the VP, Software for day-to-day work.

You'll work across five engineering teams (runtime, orchestration, quantum tools, controllers and transport) and the interfaces between them and their cross-functional stakeholders, serving several next-generation system programmes at once, with hardware being co-developed alongside the software and teams in both Oxford and the US. Those programmes draw on the same engineers, so the central problem of this role is making sure that capacity is spent by decision, not by default.

We run a centralised PMO model. This role will not own engineering headcount or define product but it will make the programme around those things run. It carries real ownership of delivery: the plan, the trade-offs put in front of decision-makers, and the honesty of the status. In this role you will interface with everyone from technical software engineers to a wide range of the most senior stakeholders. You will also coordinate with your fellow programme managers, across Science, Infrastructure and broader Software teams, making sure all plans are shared and coordinated, rather than operating in silos.

Turning a research-grade quantum system into a dependable product is a problem nobody has finished solving, and the delivery standard you'll work within is being built now. If writing the first version of the plan sounds like the interesting part, we should talk.

**Responsibilities:**

In this role you will own the end-to-end delivery of the Systems Software roadmap across several concurrent programmes including managing dependencies between hardware, science and systems integration teams. You will partner closely with engineering leadership, the engineering teams run the day to day planning and boards, you will provide the direction that creates incremental milestones that ship.

You will identify risks and blockers early and work with the teams to resolve them. You will also run intake and triage, so requests reach the right team with the right priority and engineers can stay focused on planned work.

Key responsibilities include:

* Make contention visible: when two programmes need the same team in the same quarter, bring it to the right decision-maker with the options and a recommendation before it becomes a slip.
* Keep the systems of record honest. Requirements, plans, schedules and Jira drift apart; you'll close the gap and automate the checking.
* Make invisible work visible: on-call load, sustaining work and technical debt tracked as rigorously as feature delivery.
* Surface risks early, before you have a full solution or complete alignment. We'd rather hear it messy and on time.
* Run intake and triage so requests reach the right team, with priority set by the people who own it, and engineers stay on planned work.
* Work hand in hand with the Quantum Systems Infrastructure and Science TPMs in Oxford and the Software TPMs in the US: shared processes where teams meet, and no duplicated ceremonies, boards or reports.
* Write concise, plain-English status on progress, risks and decisions for programme directors, engineering leaders and senior leadership.
* Help shape how IonQ runs software delivery across sites, working with the Group Program Manager, Software on the shared delivery standard.

**Requirements:**

You will have significant experience running technical programmes across several software teams, ideally in systems, embedded, compiler or platform software. You can discuss scope and trade-offs directly with engineering leads, read and reason about code, and re-plan when a timeline is no longer realistic. You will have a track record of leading teams through genuine ambiguity, writing the first version of the plan when there isn't one, not just executing a defined one.

You can break broad problems down into specific, assignable actions, and you have designed a team's operating cadence before. No quantum background is needed. Experience of software that works closely with hardware, for example in labs, robotics, aerospace or scientific instruments, would be beneficial.

You’d be a great fit with:

* A habit of turning diffuse problems into specific, minimal, assignable asks.
* Technical fluency to engage engineering leads directly on scope and trade-offs, and comfort reading and reasoning about code.
* Willingness to re-baseline against reality rather than defend dates that have stopped being true, and the judgement to tell a target that motivates from one that just generates fiction.
* Experience with software that works closely with hardware: labs, robotics, aerospace, scientific instruments or similar.
* A chase-without-nagging, escalate-without-drama style, and a clear sense of the difference between a risk and a noise.
* AI as a core part of how you work, for example agent-driven tracking, reconciliation or reporting.
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication with both technical and senior stakeholders.

Additional desirable skills include capacity and staffing modelling, designing operating cadences and experience leading work across sites and time zones. Experience working with programmes and systems such as Jira, Confluence and GitHub, with a preference for lightweight processes, is also helpful.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. We're looking for one data engineer who loves getting under the skin of data, and who is excited about what agents now make possible.
Agents have made data-driven development possible where it wasn't before. Messy real-world data needs ground truth and evaluations, and building them used to be very expensive. Now evaluation harnesses, with agents developing against them in a loop, can take the processing of such data to a precision and recall that wasn't possible before. What this needs is someone who understands what the data means, models it properly, and builds the harnesses that tell agents what right looks like.
IPRally is building a new generation of AI powered tools for understanding patents and technical knowledge, and everything our product does depends on patent data. Offices around the world publish it, each in its own format and language, and some of it exists only as scans of paper. Today it reaches us through data providers, and we expect to get more of it straight from the source.
Our users should see the right data in the right way. Your part of that is getting the data right and delivering it into the stores and APIs our product is built on. From there, product engineers, designers and product managers turn it into what users see. Doing your part well takes taste, and a feel for how the whole system fits together, from the sources to the product.
You'll join our data engineering team of three engineers and work closely with the other engineering teams and the rest of IPRally.
What you'll do
You'll learn what our data means, find where it falls short, and model it so that it reflects how patents, research papers and the companies behind them relate to each other.
You'll build the harness and evaluations that let agents fix data problems on their own, and judge when their results are good enough.
You'll build and run the pipelines that take data from our sources into the stores and APIs the product reads from. They're written in Python, run with Dagster, and monitored with data quality checks that show when something has gone wrong.
You'll work with the product teams on what data they need and in what form, and with the ML team on how we use machine learning in our processing steps.
You'll explore what new sources could give us, including data straight from patent offices, and help decide what's worth adding. With agents, we can try out a new source quickly before committing to it.
When a source stops delivering or falls short, you'll find out why and help work out what other sources could fill the gap.
What we're looking for
This role could be a strong fit if you:
Have built and run production pipelines on large, noisy real-world data, or worked with such data in statistics or ML.
Are comfortable deciding what to build when there's no fixed definition of correct and every tool is imperfect, and build statistical evaluations and measurable targets into your work from the start.
Build agent harnesses that develop our data processing systems on the same basis, so that we can be confident in the quality of both the data and the code.
Are curious about the real world behind the data: how it came to be, what it means, and how to represent it in the systems that process it.
Can work out what right data looks like when everything around it is imperfect, from who uses it, what they use it for.
Like working directly with the people who use the data, inside and outside engineering, to decide what's worth doing.
Experience with patent or other document data, distributed processing such as Ray, or running ML models over large datasets is an advantage, but isn't required.
How we build
Our engineers aren't measured by how much code they personally type. We're much more interested in whether you can understand the data and what people need from it, make good decisions, and use the tools available to turn those decisions into reliable pipelines.
AI agents are already a normal part of how we build at IPRally, and we're still working out what they change in data work. You'll have considerable room to experiment and help shape how the data team works with agents.
Our data stack includes Python, Dagster, Ray, Polars, Postgres, Vespa, Kubernetes and GCP. You don't need to know all of it, or anything about patents: we're much more interested in your judgment and ability to learn.
The salary range for the role is €5,500–7,000/month, with equity on top.
Ideally you're based in Helsinki, but elsewhere in Europe can work for the right person.
Along with your CV, write half a page answering this question: What's the most interesting dataset you've worked with, and what did it take before you could trust it? There's no right answer. We want to see how you think.

# Research Lead (Formulation Sciences), London

London

Isomorphic Labs is applying frontier AI to help unlock deeper scientific insights, faster breakthroughs, and life-changing medicines with an ambition to solve all disease.

The future is coming. A future enabled and enriched by the incredible power of machine learning. A future in which diseases are curtailed or cured starting with better and faster drug discovery.

Come and be part of an interdisciplinary team driving groundbreaking innovation and play a meaningful role in contributing towards us achieving our ambitious goals, while being a part of an inspiring and collaborative culture.

The world we want tomorrow is the one we’re building today. It starts with the culture at this company. It starts with you.

### **About Iso**

Isomorphic Labs (IsoLabs) was launched in 2021 to advance human health by building on and beyond the Nobel-winning AlphaFold system. Since then, our interdisciplinary team of drug discovery experts and machine learning specialists has built powerful new predictive and generative AI models that accelerate scientific discovery at digital speed.

Our name comes from the belief that there is an underlying symmetry between biology and information science. By harnessing AI’s powerful capabilities, we can use it to model complex biological phenomena to help design novel molecules, anticipate how drugs will perform and develop innovative medicines to treat and cure some of the world’s most devastating diseases.

We have built a world-leading drug design engine comprising AI models that are capable of working across multiple therapeutic areas and drug modalities. We are continually innovating on model architecture and developing cutting-edge capabilities to advance rational drug design.

Every day, and with each new breakthrough, we’re getting closer to the promise of digital biology, and achieving our ambitious mission to one day solve all disease with the help of AI.

### **Your impact**

As part of the ongoing expansion of our Drug Design and Medical Research function (DDMR), we are looking to recruit a Formulation expert keen to impact drug discovery project

You will be supporting the business alongside world leading AI/ML Drug Design Platform teams. You will collaborate to deliver scientific expertise and strategic direction to drive both improvements in the Platform and apply this to real drug design projects.

As a member of the DPC and Preclinical formulation team, you will be responsible for supporting the rapid progression of multiple drug discovery/DPC and preclinical development projects by providing (pre)-formulation expertise to the program team leveraging significant external CRO resources.

If you are a skilled and ambitious scientist looking to take the next step in your career, joining the Isomorphic Labs now will lift you out of your comfort zone and provide you with an amazing opportunity for personal growth and development. 

### **What you will do**

* Develop and execute comprehensive (pre)-formulation strategies for small molecules across the drug discovery and preclinical development lifecycle working closely with the drug design, pre-clinical and CMC function.
* Design and refine innovative formulation technologies, such as solid dispersions and co-crystals, to optimise solubility, stability, and manufacturability.
* Develop and interpret stability studies utilising ICH and ASAP methodologies, while implementing rigorous in-process controls to ensure product performance.
* Collaborate across multi-disciplinary preclinical teams to deliver seamless and integrated solutions.
* Author technical reports, protocols, and regulatory submissions in strict alignment with internal policies and global regulatory requirements.

### **Skills and qualifications**

#### **Essential:**

* PhD in pharmaceutical science, or a related technical field, or equivalent experience.
* 6+ years of professional experience within a biotech or pharma setting.
* Demonstrated expertise in the development of oral solid dosage forms.
* Demonstrated experience of supporting IND packages.
* Deep technical proficiency in preformulation, manufacturing processes, and the implementation of advanced drug delivery technologies.
* Rigorous understanding of global regulatory guidelines, including ICH and FDA.
* Excellent communication (written and verbal), interpersonal and influencing skills, with an ability to work effectively in a cross-functional, collaborative team environment.

#### **Nice to have**

* Specialised knowledge and practical experience in the development of amorphous dispersions is highly advantageous.

### **Culture and values**

We are guided by our shared values. It's not about finding people who think and act in the same way. These values help to guide our work and will continue to strengthen it.

**Thoughtful**Thoughtful at Iso is about curiosity, creativity and care. It is about good people doing good, rigorous and future-making science every single day.

**Brave**Brave at Iso is about fearlessness, but it’s also about initiative and integrity. The scale of the challenge demands nothing less.

**Determined**Determined at Iso is the way we pursue our goal. It’s a confidence in our hypothesis, as well as the urgency and agility needed to deliver on it. Because disease won’t wait, so neither should we.

**Together**Together at Iso is about connection, collaboration across fields and catalytic relationships. It’s knowing that transformation is a group project, and remembering that what we’re doing will have a real impact on real people everywhere.

### **Creating an extraordinary company**

We believe that to be successful we need a team with a range of skills and talents. We're building an environment where collaboration is fundamental, learning is shared and every employee feels supported and able to thrive. We value unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, and perspectives, and harness these qualities to create extraordinary impact.

We are committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis protected by applicable law. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.

### **Hybrid working**

It’s hugely important for us to share knowledge and build strong relationships with each other, and we find it easier to do this if we spend time together in person. This is why we follow a hybrid model, and **would require you to be able to come into the office 3 days a week** (currently Tuesday, Wednesday, and one other day depending on which team you’re in). OverviewApplication

# **Senior Backend Engineer - Credit Card Payments**

Hybrid in London, United Kingdom

**We're looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join the Payments Infrastructure team.**

You’ll design and build the payments platform behind iwoca’s business credit card – the services that approve each payment, monitor transactions for fraud, and pay out cashback.

**The company**

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

**The team**

iwoca launched its business credit card in 2026. It gives small businesses a fast, flexible way to pay for what they need and control their cash flow, alongside iwoca’s loans. The card is a core part of iwoca’s long-term growth.

The Payments infrastructure team builds iwoca’s card payments platform. Its job is to approve each payment in moments when a customer uses their card. The team also builds the platforms that pay out rewards as customers spend and monitor every transaction.

The team is small – a principal engineer, a product manager with a background in payments, and you. It works closely with iwoca’s ledger, fraud and customer product teams.

**The role**

As a senior backend engineer, you’ll own services and projects end to end, and shape the platform’s architecture with the principal engineer, from service boundaries to how authorisation, rewards, and transaction monitoring fit together. You’ll work closely with product to decide what the team builds and how. There’s still plenty to build, and you’ll take new services into production.

You’ll build on your payments expertise alongside the principal engineer, with scope to grow as the platform matures. Most of the challenge is technical: scaling payments within card scheme rules and the regulation iwoca has to meet. Your code will run every time a small business uses its iwoca card.

Live project examples:

* **Payment authorisation.** Extending the service built to approve or decline each card payment in real time, using data held in other services. It places a hold on available credit in the ledger and applies iwoca's own checks, such as account status, merchant category code restrictions, and spend limits.
* **Transaction monitoring.** Building the service that will screen card transactions for fraud and financial-crime risk as customers spend, so iwoca will rely less on third parties.
* **Rewards.** Extending the service that pays out cashback, as the team adds to what the card offers.
* **Testing for failure.** Designing sandbox tests that cover edge cases and failures across the card transaction lifecycle.
* **Ledger cutover and go-live.** Moving the card platform onto iwoca's own ledger and infrastructure with as little downtime as possible, then fixing the issues that only show up in production.

**The requirements**

Essential:

* **Payment systems.** You've designed and run highly available, low-latency payment systems in production, ideally on the issuing side.
* **Card payment flows.** You've worked on card authorisation and clearing, and traced transactions from the terminal, through the acquirer and card scheme, to the issuer. You've used response codes to diagnose declined transactions.
* **Backend engineering.** You have deep expertise in at least one object-oriented language. You've written and run backend services in it.
* **Distributed systems.** You've built microservices, REST APIs, and asynchronous messaging with queues or topics, and designed the database schemas behind them, ideally in PostgreSQL.
* **AI leverage.** You've built agentic workflows, or used AI to scale your engineering output beyond what you could deliver alone, at work or in your own projects. You judge when to use it and when not to, and you check its output before it reaches production.
* **Communication.** You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

Bonus:

* **Ledgers and clearing.** You've worked on a ledger, reconciliation, or clearing system – for cards, loyalty points, bank transfers, or money remittance.
* **Testing.** You've written automated tests for payment systems, ideally test-first.
* **Python.** You've used Python in production. It's the language the team works in.

**The salary**

We expect to pay from £100,000 to £120,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

**The culture**

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

**The offices**

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

* Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.
* Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

**The benefits**

* Flexible working hours.
* Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.
* A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.
* 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.
* A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.
* Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.
* 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.
* An employee equity incentive scheme.
* Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.
* Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.
* Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

* A learning and development budget for everyone.
* Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.
* Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Focused on finding more than just bugs, you want to untangle dependencies and raise the bar for quality across the board. You're comfortable stepping up to take ownership and lead the charge when things get complicated.

## **About JetBrains**

We create intelligent software development tools for developers and teams. More than 15 million users, over 300,000 companies, and 88 of the Fortune Global Top 100 rely on our products to solve real, complex problems. Our mission is simple: make development teams more productive and AI adoptable at scale.

## **What you’ll do**

DataGrip is our cross-platform IDE for databases, and its core functionality powers database tools across other JetBrains IDEs like IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, and PhpStorm. Because of the large size of this ecosystem, which spans many database systems, environments, and integrations, keeping our quality bar high is a complex, strategic challenge. You’ll take ownership of quality across these shared components and release processes. You’ll work closely with developers, DevOps, and product teams to map out expected behaviors, investigate hard-to-reproduce issues, and improve how we build and test. Your work will directly influence the reliability of tools used by millions of developers every day, making sure changes in one area don't unexpectedly break another.

Day to day, you will:

* Lead QA activities, set priorities, and coordinate testing efforts across multiple teams and components.
* Investigate unclear, poorly reproducible, and cross-component issues to find the root cause.
* Analyze logs, test results, and user reports to spot broader quality patterns behind individual failures.
* Define test strategies and apply risk-based testing to manage release cycles safely.
* Work with developers and product teams to establish expected behavior when detailed specifications aren't available.
* Improve our QA processes and guide the team in making confident release decisions.

## **What you’ll bring**

* A high degree of independence and technical curiosity.
* Comfort taking ownership of complex problems and driving them to resolution.
* The ability to see the big picture and understand how changes in one area affect the rest of the system.
* A proactive approach to improving processes rather than just following them.
* Strong analytical thinking, with the ability to turn scattered logs and user reports into clear insights.
* The communication skills to bring different teams together and coordinate testing efforts smoothly.

## **What you’ll need**

* The proven ability to test complex, multi-component systems and navigate integration and end-to-end testing.
* Practical knowledge of relational databases and SQL.
* Experience leading QA activities and shaping test strategies for multiple products and release cycles.
* Familiarity with reading and debugging code (Java or Kotlin preferred) to troubleshoot deeply embedded issues.
* Hands-on experience writing or maintaining automated tests.
* The ability to navigate and troubleshoot CI/CD systems, test environments, and infrastructure (such as Docker, Kubernetes, or TeamCity).
* Experience investigating distributed systems, APIs, and service-to-service integrations using monitoring and logging tools.

## **What success looks like**

Within your first few months, you’ll have a firm grasp of the DataGrip ecosystem and how its components interact across our IDEs. You’ll be independently identifying quality risks, setting clear testing priorities, and helping teams ship reliable releases without bottlenecks. Long-term, you’ll have established smoother QA workflows, making it easier for everyone to understand dependencies and catch cross-product issues before they reach our users.

#### **Location: Coventry**

Want to become a Graduate Pricing & Strategy Analyst in one of the UK’s leading and fastest growing B2B packaging suppliers? Kite Packaging is an employee-owned business with ferociously ambitious growth plans. We operate the UK’s largest packaging ecommerce website.

You will be joining an established, profitable, growing technology-backed business and will be part of an industry-leading team. As a Graduate Pricing & Strategy Analyst working in Kite Packaging’s ecommerce division in Coventry, you will work within a collaborative, like-minded team environment alongside our commercial, marketing, analytics and product teams.

You will analyse pricing, sales, customer and product data to identify opportunities to improve revenue and margin while maintaining target gross profit levels. You will forecast the impact of price changes, including the sales growth or volume required to offset changes in margin and deliver the desired commercial outcome.

You will collaborate across the business to determine the most effective pricing strategy for different product ranges. Pricing decisions will not be considered in isolation, but alongside customer behaviour, market position, product demand, volume, margin, competitor activity and customer acquisition.

Beyond pricing, you will use data to identify wider commercial opportunities, including products with growth potential and trends in customer, competitor and category performance.

Working alongside our Pay-Per-Click & Digital Insights team, you will develop a broader commercial understanding by combining commercial, website and marketing data to understand how pricing, customer behaviour and acquisition interact. You will also help develop competitor benchmarking using commercial software and in-house solutions with AI-assisted development.

You will test ideas and measure their impact, using data to understand what changed, why and whether the expected commercial outcome was achieved.

The ideal candidate will have strong numerical ability, curiosity and commercial awareness, with an interest in understanding why something has happened rather than simply reporting that it has. They will become comfortable working with large datasets, identifying patterns, challenging assumptions and turning their findings into clear, evidence-led recommendations.

The areas that you will be exposed to includes:

* Pricing and margin analysis
* Price elasticity, price breaks and volume discount analysis
* Sales and product performance analysis
* Customer purchasing behaviour and segmentation
* Competitor benchmarking and market analysis
* Commercial forecasting and scenario modelling
* Product and category strategy
* Developing reporting, benchmarking and analytical tools
* Using automation and AI to improve commercial analysis and decision-making

# Quality Assurance Lead - Scientific Testing & Anti-Doping

* Full-time
* Work Arrangement: On-site
* Department: Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs

## Company Description

**Location: Fordham, Cambridgeshire | On-site**

At LGC ASSURE, everything we do is driven by one purpose: *Science for a Safer World.*

As part of our Sports & Specialised Analytical Services (SSAS) team, you’ll be joining an internationally recognised scientific testing business working across animal sports medication, human drug testing and dietary supplement certification. Our work supports the integrity of sport, protects public health and helps ensure products meet the highest standards.

## Job Description

We’re looking for an experienced Quality Assurance Lead to help shape, strengthen and continuously improve quality across our scientific operations.

**This is an on-site role based at our Fordham laboratory in Cambridgeshire. A regular on-site presence is essential to the role, working directly with our scientific and operational teams.**

**The opportunity**

This is more than a traditional quality compliance role. You'll work across a diverse range of scientific and operational teams, each with different processes, priorities and accreditation requirements. You'll need to understand those differences, build strong relationships and find practical solutions that maintain compliance without creating unnecessary barriers.

We're looking for someone who can turn *“we can't do that”* into *“how can we make that work?”*

You'll bring the technical credibility to challenge existing practices, the judgement to manage risk proportionately, and the people skills to bring others with you. Alongside maintaining a robust quality framework, you'll have the opportunity to improve systems, simplify processes and make better use of technology.

If you enjoy solving complex problems, influencing change and helping teams find better ways of working, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact.

**What you'll be doing**

* **Lead quality across the business:** Act as a trusted quality partner to scientific and operational teams, providing expert guidance on accreditation, compliance, risk and continuous improvement.
* **Own and strengthen the QMS:** Maintain and develop our Quality Management System, ensuring it remains effective, compliant and fit for purpose across different areas of the business.
* **Drive accreditation and compliance:** Interpret ISO/IEC 17025 requirements, support the ongoing development of our accredited quality framework and deputise for the ISO 17025 Quality Manager as required.
* **Lead audits and investigations:** Manage audit activity, root cause investigations, non-conformances, corrective actions, risk assessments and change control, ensuring actions address underlying issues and deliver lasting improvements.
* **Turn challenges into solutions:** Work collaboratively with teams to resolve quality issues, balance compliance requirements with operational needs and influence decisions at all levels.
* **Improve systems and processes:** Lead improvement initiatives, identify opportunities to simplify processes and support the development of our electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including digital tools and SharePoint-based solutions.
* **Coordinate projects and stakeholders:** Work with internal teams and external accreditation bodies to plan and deliver accreditation activities, manage competing priorities and achieve successful outcomes.
* **Develop capability:** Coach and support colleagues, helping embed a positive quality culture and build confidence in quality practices across the organisation.

## Qualifications

* What you'll bring

  You'll be an experienced quality professional with a strong understanding of laboratory accreditation and the confidence to operate independently in a varied, fast-moving environment.

  You'll ideally have:
* Substantial experience managing or leading a Quality Management System within an ISO/IEC 17025-accredited laboratory environment.
* A strong understanding of accreditation requirements and how to translate them into effective, practical working processes.
* Experience leading audits, root cause analysis, corrective and preventive actions, risk assessments and change control.
* The ability to assess quality risks, prioritise effectively and focus on improvements that deliver meaningful results.
* Experience improving quality systems, processes or ways of working, ideally including eQMS, SharePoint or other digital quality tools.
* Strong project management and organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate activities across multiple teams and stakeholders.
* Excellent communication and influencing skills, with the confidence to challenge constructively, build credibility and bring people along with you.

**What will make you successful?**

Technical expertise is essential, but how you apply it is just as important.

**You'll be someone who:**

**Finds solutions, not just problems.** You can challenge a decision while working collaboratively to find a compliant way forward.

**Builds relationships and credibility.** You understand different perspectives and adapt your approach to the people and teams you're supporting.

**Enjoys variety.** You're comfortable switching between different scientific disciplines, operational challenges and competing priorities.

**Improves how things work.** You question established practices, identify opportunities to simplify and turn ideas into practical improvements.

**Brings structure to ambiguity.** You're proactive, comfortable working autonomously and able to create clarity where processes or responsibilities aren't always clearly defined.

**Makes quality meaningful.** You help colleagues understand not just what is required, but why it matters and how to achieve it effectively.

## Additional Information

**Our Values**

* Passion
* Curiosity
* Integrity
* Brilliance
* Respect

**Equal opportunities**

We are committed to ensuring that every job applicant and employee is valued for their individual talents. We strictly prohibit discrimination on the basis of age, disability, race, colour, ethnic or national origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender reassignment, marital or civil partnership, pregnancy or parental status, religion, or belief. We proudly support an inclusive work environment where everyone can compete and succeed based on their merits.

## About us

LGT Wealth Management UK LLP is a UK-based partnership, wholly owned by the private banking group LGT, which is in turn owned by the Princely Family of Liechtenstein. When we set up LGT Wealth Management in 2008, our aim was to offer a fresh approach to wealth management. Alongside the LLP we also have two other entities which focus on US and Jersey based clients. Our head office is based in London however we have a presence in Edinburgh, Jersey, Leeds, Birmingham and Bristol. The plan was simple: put our clients first by providing a transparent service, designed around what is right for each of them. By drawing together in-depth knowledge and experience from across the industry, we provide a flexible, bespoke service adapted to each of our clients’ needs.
  
Our mission is to create long-term value for all stakeholders. Our culture encourages individuals to generate, develop and implement ideas which will strengthen our business. Belonging, respect, integrity, conviction and entrepreneurship are our core values. As our brand recognition grows, we are fast becoming an employer of choice in our sector. We have over £29 billion in funds under management and circa 700 staff.

## Your challenge

The Wealth Planning team is responsible for the provision of comprehensive financial planning advice to individuals, companies, partnerships and trusts. We work with our clients to create bespoke financial plans, considering the whole of the market in order to find the best financial planning solutions. We are involved in a broad range of activities including:

▪ Cash flow analysis

▪ Psychometric risk profiling

▪ Retirement planning

▪ Pension aggregation

▪ Income tax planning

▪ Inheritance tax planning

▪ Business planning

▪ Protection for death and illness

▪ Long term savings and investments

▪ Offshore and international planning for non-domiciled and non-resident clients

▪ Venture Capital Trust, Enterprise Investment Scheme and Business Relief advice

**Brief Role Objective:**

The primary role of the Paraplanner is to provide a full professional and technical support function to Wealth Planners in meeting the client’s financial objectives. The Wealth Planners supported by this role are based across LGT’s UK regional offices in London, Bristol, Birmingham, Edinburgh, Manchester and Leeds. The Paraplanner will be based in London and must be comfortable providing effective support remotely, if required.

The Paraplanner is responsible for delivering allocated paraplanning work accurately and within agreed timescales. They will develop their technical judgement through standard advice cases, identify missing information or potential issues early, and seek guidance or escalate matters where a case requires more advanced analysis.

The Paraplanner may also be required to carry out other duties allocated to them by Wealth Planners, Compliance team, Administration Manager or Paraplanner Manager to meet the wider needs of the Wealth Planning team.

# **Key Responsibilities:**

**Preparation and Maintenance of Client Files**

▪  Collect and analyse client’s financial information and work with Wealth Planners to determine strategies for meeting the client’s financial objectives.

▪  Ensure that all compliance documentation is recorded in line with LGT Wealth Planning’s procedure manual and FCA guidelines.

▪  Accurately record client information and documentation within ‘Intelligent Office’ back-office management system.

▪  Identify and obtain the information necessary to complete a cash flow model (if required).

**Cashflow Planning (if required)**

▪  Interpret data received from the client and build a cash flow model using our cash flow modelling tool.

▪  Ensure that all data input into the cash flow modelling tool is accurate and correct.

▪  Build the cash flow model with consideration to the client’s financial circumstances and objectives.

▪  Prepare an analysis document which details the outputs and key findings from the modelling, in line with the requirements of the Senior/ Wealth Planner and client.

**Advice and Recommendation**

▪  Manage standard advice cases in line with agreed processes and timescales, producing accurate research, calculations and reports. Contribute to bespoke or complex cases with guidance from a Senior Paraplanner or Technical Specialist and promptly identify matters requiring escalation.

▪  The Paraplanner may attend client meetings with the Wealth Planner (as required).

▪  Research and record all technical and product data relevant to the client and to the specific advice we are providing.

▪  Research should be undertaken both independently and alongside the Wealth Planner.

▪  Provide technical support to Wealth Planners regarding specific queries relating to the advice we are providing.

▪  Analyse the client’s existing products/ financial arrangements to determine suitability in meeting the client’s objectives.

▪  Work with Wealth Planner to identify suitable solutions to meet the client’s objectives.

▪  Undertake financial calculations relevant to the financial advice.

▪  Manage the preparation and completion of comprehensive financial advice letters and suitability reports in line with LGT Wealth Planning’s procedure manual. Ensuring any recommendations are detailed in a clear, concise, jargon free manner. This would include (but not limited to) retirement planning, estate planning, cash flow reports, or financial strategy plans.

▪  Ensure that all client data detailed in our financial advice letters and suitability reports is accurate and correct.

▪  Ensure that the correct advice sign off is obtained prior to issuing the financial advice letters and suitability reports.

▪  Liaise with the client’s LGT investment manager, legal advisor, accountant and tax advisers, etc (where applicable).

**Oversee Implementation of Recommendations**

▪  Take responsibility for completing the paraplanning elements of the advice file and checking that the required information and documentation are in place before it is passed to the Administration Manager for new business submission.

▪  Overseeing completion of application forms by the administration team before being issued to the client.

▪  Working closely with the administration team to oversee implementation of the agreed recommendations

**Prepare for client reviews**

▪  Act as main point of contact with providers / third parties.

▪  Where required update existing cash flow models.

▪  Research and record on file technical and product data relevant to the client’s annual review.

**Administration**

▪  Although the team has an administration team primarily responsible for liaising with third party suppliers; the onus is on the Paraplanner to ensure the administration is completed in a time-efficient manner. This may involve letter writing, chase letters of authority, and chasing information from third parties.

▪  In the absence of the administration team, the Paraplanner will be expected to undertake their own administration.

## Your profile

**Knowledge and Qualifications**

▪  CII Diploma in Regulated Financial Planning or equivalent level 4 financial planning qualification.

▪  Completed or working towards the level 6 Advanced Diploma in Regulated Financial Planning.

▪  Three years or more of recent, comprehensive and well-rounded technical paraplanning experience. Candidates with less experience will be considered provided they can demonstrate they meet the requirements of the Paraplanner role.

**Skills and Attributes:**

▪  Excellent understanding of the financial planning and the regulatory advice process is essential.

▪  Excellent understanding of the compliance requirements within a financial planning team.

▪  Good knowledge of financial planning products and how to assess suitability relative to the client’s objectives.

▪  Ability to produce bespoke advice reports in clear and concise manner.

▪  Methodical and practical approach to work and delivering of financial advice.

▪  Good planning and organisational skills and able to prioritise own workload and meet agreed deadlines.

▪  Ability to manage expectations for both internal and external parties.

▪  Keep up to date with regulatory and legislative changes.

▪  Continue to maintain a high level of technical financial planning knowledge.

▪  Be honest and have integrity.

▪  Attention to detail.

▪  Practical experience using Voyant to build, check and explain cashflow models.

▪  Experience of Intelligent Office (iO), Synaptics Research, Defaqto Engage and IRESS Exchange would be preferable.

▪  Advanced Microsoft excel skills would be desirable.

# Senior DevOps Engineer

*This is a hybrid role that requires 3 days/week in our London (Fitzrovia) office*

## About Lorum

The structural conflict at the centre of correspondent banking is not technological. It is economic. Banks earn revenue from their balance sheets: they lend deposits, capture FX spreads, and hold funds as long as it is rational to do so. Clearing, the act of releasing funds quickly and predictably, competes directly with those economics. An institution designed to lend has a structural incentive to hold deposits; an institution designed to clear has an incentive to release them. When one institution does both, clearing loses. The result is unpredictable settlement, trapped capital, and a correspondent network shrinking by design.

## Why Lorum

Lorum was founded on a different premise: clearing as the business, not a byproduct. The model has been operational since 2023 and grew 55x in 2025, with USD clearing now the majority of volumes alongside a growing treasury offering. We have applied for a U.S. national trust bank charter. The people we hire now will build the clearing and treasury infrastructure it unlocks.

# The role

We are looking for a Senior DevOps Engineer to join our engineering team in London. You will own and improve the cloud infrastructure, CI/CD and observability that our clearing platform runs on, working directly with backend engineers and Security. As volumes grow and regulatory expectations rise, you will make production safer, more observable and easier to recover, and you will be trusted to form opinions and act on them.

* Design, build and maintain AWS infrastructure as code with Terraform, including state management and Git-driven workflows (Atlantis or equivalent) for safe, auditable changes
* Build and run GitHub Actions pipelines for build, test, release and infrastructure deployment, with fast pre-merge checks and reliable environments for engineers
* Run production services: on-call, incident response, post-mortems and capacity planning, with a focus on resilience and failover
* Instrument our systems with metrics, logs and traces, and use that telemetry to drive reliability improvements
* Work with Security and GRC on SOC 2 / ISO 27001 requirements: secure deployments, secrets management, IAM, and encryption at rest and in transit
* Automate repetitive operational work, build self-service tooling and runbooks for developers, review infrastructure changes and help raise engineering standards

## Success in the first 3 to 12 months

* Within your first weeks, ship a concrete improvement to our infrastructure or pipelines
* By month 3, be working autonomously across AWS, Terraform and GitHub Actions and have taken ownership of the tools that support them
* By month 6, have led improvements to resilience and failover for core production services, with clear runbooks and tested recovery paths

This is not a conventional consumer-facing Product Manager role. Many requests will arrive with a clear commercial goal and a proposed solution. * Decide when a request should be delivered directly, when assumptions need testing, and when repeated one-off work should become a reusable platform capability.
* Partner with the Engineering Lead and team to clarify scope, dependencies and acceptance criteria, maintain a healthy backlog and improve delivery predictability.
* Lead planning and communication across Paid Marketing, Partnerships, Operations, Data Science and Product & Technology, making trade-offs and capacity constraints explicit.
* Act as the primary Lyst product contact for the NZ-based Data Science team, aligning roadmaps and turning research outputs into secure, observable and supportable production capabilities.
* Define and track outcomes across commercial performance, data quality, platform reliability and operational efficiency.

* **ROAS and optimisation:** productionising bidding, measurement and optimisation models with the controls, monitoring and feedback loops needed to operate them safely.
* **Partner and affiliate platforms:** partner feed ingestion and validation, merchant tooling and the services that connect catalogue and commercial workflows.
* **Product-data quality:** enrichment, merging, deduplication, entity resolution, taxonomy and measurable improvements to catalogue completeness and coherence.
* **ZOZO collaboration:** joint milestones, experiments, data contracts, technical workshops and clear handovers across time zones.
* **Platform health:** SLAs, observability, runbooks, incident follow-up, peak readiness, BAU and a pragmatic technical roadmap across services such as Minion, Plasma, Merchant Uploader and Affiliate Service.

* Experience working on a MarTech team and/or with marketing and commercial stakeholders
* Enough technical depth to work confidently with APIs, schemas, data contracts, ETL or ingestion pipelines, event flows and production systems.
* A track record of turning ambiguous or fragmented stakeholder needs into coherent, deliverable roadmaps without adding process for its own sake.

* Confidence working with commercially accountable stakeholders, including constructively challenging a proposed solution when the evidence supports it.

Demographic and Geospatial Data

# About the role

We are looking for a hands-on Data Engineer to develop and maintain Databricks pipelines that combine demographic information with geographic reference data. You will produce reliable datasets for demographic reporting, population analysis and service planning, with clear rules for how records are assigned to geographic areas.

You will work with data owners, analysts and platform teams to translate requirements into reusable processing. The role includes postcode enrichment, spatial processing, data quality and management of changing geographic reference data, from development through release and production support.

# Key responsibilities

* Design, develop and deploy data pipelines using Databricks, Python, PySpark and SQL. Build reusable ingestion, transformation and validation components, with reliable scheduling, incremental processing and safe reprocessing.
* Ingest demographic records, postcode directories, geographic boundaries and organisation reference data. Maintain source metadata, data lineage and versioned raw and curated datasets using Delta Lake.
* Standardise postcode and address fields while preserving source values. Apply agreed record keys and effective dates, and manage invalid, missing, terminated or unmatched postcodes through documented exception rules.
* Enrich records using approved NHS and ONS postcode products and lookup tables. Derive agreed statistical, local authority and health geographies, and validate organisation and site codes against ODS reference data.
* Implement spatial joins, including point-in-polygon matching, and distance calculations where required. Validate geometry and coordinate reference systems, and define how boundary-edge cases and multiple matches are handled.
* Maintain versions and effective dates for postcode lookups, boundaries and organisation changes. Apply the correct geographic vintage for each reporting period so historical outputs remain reproducible.
* Keep residential geography distinct from registered-practice and provider geography. Agree demographic definitions, age reference dates and aggregation rules with analysts to avoid incorrect linkage or double counting.
* Automate checks for completeness, duplicate records, unmatched locations, invalid coordinates and unexpected geography changes. Reconcile counts before and after joins and report exceptions for investigation.
* Optimise Spark and spatial processing through appropriate partitioning, join strategies and spatial indexing where supported. Monitor runtime, data volumes and resource use as pipelines scale.
* Apply approved access, pseudonymisation and disclosure controls to demographic and location data. Use authorised reference and geocoding services, and produce outputs at the agreed geographic granularity.
* Use code review, automated tests and controlled releases. Document mappings, reference-data versions and recovery procedures, and investigate production issues with data owners and support teams.

# Essential skills and experience

* Strong Databricks, Python, PySpark and SQL skills, with hands-on experience developing and supporting production data pipelines processing large datasets.
* Experience with Delta Lake, batch and incremental ingestion, schema management, merge logic, deduplication and maintaining historical records without losing the meaning of effective dates.
* Practical geospatial data engineering experience working with points, polygons, spatial joins, geometry validation and geographic aggregation.
* Understanding of coordinate reference systems, including British National Grid and WGS84, coordinate transformation, distance units and the limitations of postcode centroids for precise location analysis.
* Experience with a scalable Spark spatial approach, such as supported native Databricks spatial functions or Apache Sedona. Able to select tooling compatible with the deployed runtime and workload.
* Ability to ingest and transform spatial formats such as GeoJSON, WKT/WKB and Shapefile or GeoParquet, alongside tabular reference files.
* Experience joining demographic or other record-level data to geographic reference data, handling unmatched and multiple matches, and controlling changes to lookup versions and boundaries.
* Strong data quality and reconciliation skills, including tests that identify record multiplication, missing mappings and incorrect geographic assignments.
* Experience with Git, CI/CD, code review, automated testing, job monitoring and performance troubleshooting. Able to document assumptions and explain data issues clearly to analysts and data owners.

# Desirable experience

* NHS demographic or patient registration data, the NHS Postcode Directory, ONS Postcode Directory, National Statistics Postcode Lookup and Organisation Data Service reference data.
* UK statistical and health geographies, including Lower layer and Middle layer Super Output Areas (LSOAs and MSOAs), local authorities and Integrated Care Boards (ICBs).
* GeoPandas, Shapely, pyproj or QGIS for investigation and validation; address matching using Unique Property Reference Numbers (UPRNs) and approved address reference sources.

**Our Purpose**

At **Medtronic Patient Care Systems (PCS),** we power the digital heartbeat behind life-saving cardiac therapies. We build the connected ecosystem that enables clinicians to monitor, manage, and protect millions of patients living with implantable cardiac devices around the world.

From secure device connectivity and real-time data platforms to intelligent clinical tools and patient-facing experiences, PCS transforms complex cardiac data into clarity, helping physicians make faster decisions, improving outcomes, and giving patients greater confidence in their care.

Every line of code we write supports someone’s parent, spouse, child, or friend. Our work ensures that life-saving therapies are not only delivered safely and reliably, but continuously improved through innovation, insight, and global scale.

If you want to build technology that truly matters, where uptime means peace of mind and innovation means more birthdays, join us. Together, we are shaping the future of connected cardiac care and changing lives every single day

***Come for a job, stay for a career!***

**A Day in The Life Of:**

  

As **Product Director** you will help shape and deliver the next generation of connected patient-care products and experiences.

This role will operate across a portfolio that includes patient-facing digital products, mobile applications, connected devices, embedded software, platform capabilities, cloud services, data, and AI-enabled experiences. The Product Director will define product direction, lead through discovery and execution, and help create products intended for patients and healthcare systems around the world.

This is a hands-on product leadership role for someone who can move comfortably between long-term strategy and near-term execution, customer needs and technical trade-offs, and product vision and measurable results. The Product Director will also be a leader in building the Product Management footprint in Galway, including product practices, operating mechanisms, partnerships, and talent.

The role reflects the expectation that Product Management owns the problem and the outcome, leads through discovery, runs products with strong business judgment, and develops the product craft and the people around it.

No two days will be exactly alike. A day may include speaking with patients or clinicians, reviewing product and operational data, shaping a multi-year product direction, working with engineers on mobile or embedded-software trade-offs, evaluating an AI-enabled opportunity, or helping leaders make an investment decision.

Other days may focus on discovery reviews, roadmap choices, product quality, global-market needs, release readiness, or developing the Galway product organization. Throughout the work, the Product Director connects customer needs, business goals, technical possibilities, organizational capacity, and measurable outcomes into a coherent direction.

  

**Key Responsibilities:**

  

* Define and communicate a clear product vision, strategy, outcome-based roadmaps, and measurable goals for connected patient-care products and platform capabilities.
* Translate patient, clinical, customer, technical, and business needs into prioritized opportunities and clear direction for Engineering and Design.

## About Neural Concept

Neural Concept is the engineering intelligence platform used by leading manufacturers in automotive, aerospace, and energy. We combine geometric and physics AI with LLM-based agents so engineering teams can move from customer requirements to validated designs in a fraction of the usual time.

## About the role

Design decisions depend on information that lives outside the CAD model: customer requirements, design rules, manufacturing and assembly constraints, and cost targets. This information is spread across specification documents, handbooks, ERP systems, requirements management tools, and system models. Engineers gather it by hand, often late in the process, and conflicts surface at design reviews or on the production line.

We call the capability that closes this gap Design Engineering Knowledge. It connects the design to the information ecosystem around it, so requirements, constraints, and trade-offs are available to engineers and AI agents while they work on the design itself.

As a Product Engineer, you will build this capability. Requirements are the first focus area: extracting them from customer specifications and requirements management systems, structuring them, and keeping them traceable. You will then extend the same foundation to design rule checks, Design for Manufacturing (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and Design for Cost, and connect it to the enterprise systems where this knowledge already lives.

You will work with the Product Manager, solution engineers, and customer engineering teams, as the primary developer from the first customer conversation to the version running in production.

## What you will do

* Build the requirements foundation: ingest customer specifications and RFQ packages, extract requirements with LLM and agent-based pipelines, and keep each one traceable to its source document and page.
* Extend this foundation to design rules, DfM, DfA, and Design for Cost, turning standards, handbooks, and company know-how into constraints that software and agents can use.
* Bring requirements, constraints, and trade-offs into the design workflow, so engineers can check a design against them at any stage and see which ones apply to the part they are working on.
* Build integrations with the systems around the design: requirements management systems, ERP (cost, materials, and supplier data), and system design and MBSE tools for architecture and system-level requirements.
* Design the data model that links requirements, rules, and constraints to parts, design parameters, and simulation results.
* Create evaluation sets and quality metrics with customers, so extraction and checking accuracy is measured and improves with every release.
* Design human-in-the-loop review flows where engineers validate and edit AI output, with versioning and a full audit trail.
* Spot recurring patterns across customers and turn them into reusable components of the Neural Concept platform.

## Who you are

### Must have

* Experience building and shipping production Python software in fast-moving, cross-functional teams.
* Hands-on experience with LLM applications in production: structured outputs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, and evaluation.
* Experience integrating with enterprise systems through APIs and data models, for example ERP, PLM, or requirements management tools.
* Experience with document processing, such as PDF parsing, OCR, or information extraction.
* Strong software practices: testing (pytest), CI, packaging, code review, and git.
* A product mindset. You talk to users, understand the problem before writing code, and ship in small, measurable steps.
* Clear, concise communication with both customer engineers and internal teams.
* Based in Cambridge (UK) or willing to relocate.

### Nice to have

* Background in mechanical engineering or physics, with exposure to DfM, DfA, or design-to-cost practices.
* Familiarity with requirements engineering and model-based systems engineering (MBSE, SysML).
* Experience working with CAD data or geometry processing.
* Experience with vision-language models, vector databases, or search ranking.

## What you get

* Ownership of a product capability that customers use in real engineering programs, with direct access to the engineers who use it.
* A competitive salary and rewarding opportunities as we continue to scale.
* A collaborative, multicultural team where your work is visible and recognized.
* Colleagues who share knowledge freely and support each other.

* **Making a Difference:** We remember who we serve. We are passionate about making a meaningful, positive impact on the lives of carers and those we support.
* **Agility:** We continuously refine and adapt. There is no room for complacency here; we are driven to constantly review and improve our products and processes.

* **Openness to Learning:** We believe no question is a silly question and all insights are valuable. Mistakes are part of the improvement process; we dust ourselves off and begin again.

## The Team & Role

Own the order to cash cycle at NCS: subscriptions, billing, collections, and ARR and revenue reporting. The role leads a team that executes billing and credit control, and is personally accountable for the outcome: a subscription book that is right, invoices that are right first time, cash collected to terms, and ARR and revenue numbers that reconcile to the CRM and the ledger without rework.

The second half of the job, and the reason the role exists at this level, is to change how the cycle works rather than run it as it is. The postholder is expected to spearhead process improvement across O2C through the use of AI, redesign of the process itself, and partnership with the internal teams on either side of it (Sales Ops, CS, Commercial Finance) and the external providers of the tools it runs on. Within 12 to 18 months the cycle should be materially more automated, better controlled and less dependent on month end effort than it is today.

## Key Responsibilities

* **Lead billing and credit control.** Own the billing and collections outcomes and lead the team that delivers them. Set priorities, standards and service levels; put the right controls around the billing run, credit notes, device overage, the weekly aged debt review and the suspension process; and review the team's output so that issues are caught before they reach the customer or the ledger. Stay close enough to the work to know where it is fragile, and step in personally on escalations, high value accounts and disputes that need finance's weight behind them. Own DSO, cash collection against forecast and the monthly bad debt provision. Develop the team so that execution becomes more capable and self sufficient over time, freeing the role to focus on improvement.
* **Own the subscription book.** Be accountable for the subscription record as the single source of truth for what each customer is entitled to and what we bill them, with every active subscription backed by a signed order form that agrees to the CRM deal on term, dates, quantities, price points and uplift terms. Set the controls for the contract lifecycle (set up before first bill, mid term changes, renewals and uplifts, churn) and the forward renewals and uplift calendar, with the team and Sales Ops executing within them. Reconcile the subscription book to billed ARR and to the CRM each month so that the three agree.
* **Own ARR and revenue reporting.** Personally own the monthly ARR bridge and its cross reference to HubSpot closed deals and churn requests, the month end upgrade/downgrade schedule, the bookings and billings commentary for the board pack (YTD vs budget and PYTD), and the ARR and receivables inputs to the PE investor's portfolio reporting. Own deferred and accrued revenue, invoice smoothing and exceptions, and the revenue, debtors, deferred income and bad debt balance sheet reconciliations within the close timetable. Lead the audit on revenue and receivables. Build the bridge from the subscription book, so ARR is derived from entitlements rather than reverse engineered from invoices.
* **Spearhead process improvement through AI and automation.** Lead the adoption of AI across O2C: identify the repeatable, rules based work in billing, collections, reconciliation and reporting and move it onto AI assisted or automated workflows (bridge building and CRM cross referencing, aged debt classification and chasing, invoice to contract checks, overage calculations, exception and ticket generation). Own the library of these workflows, their controls and their documentation, and measure the hours and errors they remove. Be the person in finance who understands what the tools can and cannot safely do.
* **Redesign the process with internal stakeholders.** Partner with Sales Ops, CS, Commercial Finance and the wider finance team to fix problems at source rather than in finance: what a deal needs to look like in HubSpot before it can be billed, how churn and downgrade requests flow, how parent/child structures are maintained, where the handoffs break. Agree and document the end to end O2C process with named owners for each step, publish it in the finance knowledge base, and hold the other teams to it.
* **Manage the external tool providers.** Be finance's owner of the relationship with the billing platform, the CRM (finance side) and any collections or AI tooling: roadmap, configuration, integration between CRM, subscription book, billing and ledger, support escalation and value for money. Lead finance's input into the systems review on billing, subscription and collections tooling, and lead the finance workstream of any resulting change.

## How Success Is Measured (first 12 to 18 months)

* Billing and collections run reliably to standard through the team: credit notes as a % of invoiced value trending down, zero material billing errors surfacing through the ARR bridge, DSO and 91+ debt reduced against agreed targets, write offs within provision.
* Subscription book reconciled to billed ARR and to the CRM monthly; no active subscriptions without a contract; no contracted uplifts or renewals missed.
* ARR bridge reconciled to CRM each month with unexplained movements cleared before the pack goes out; revenue and receivables recs complete by the close deadline; clean audit.
* A measurable reduction in manual effort across O2C, with the main month end and weekly workflows running on documented AI assisted or automated processes under control.
* An agreed, documented end to end O2C process with named owners in Sales Ops, CS and finance, in use and enforced.
