## **About Nous**

Nous is a household AI agent. It takes over the bills and admin people don't have time for and acts for them: switching energy, buying insurance, cancelling forgotten subscriptions, managing the family calendar. Nearly 250,000 UK households have signed up, and another joins every minute.

We think the real value of AI isn't writing amazing cover letters, it's doing useful things in the real world for real people. That's the hard part, and a brilliant product is only half of it. An energy switch takes weeks, so our agents run on long-running workflows, not a single chat turn. Cancelling a subscription means a browser agent handling the code Apple sends to your phone. Buying insurance meant getting our regulatory principal comfortable with an agent doing it end to end (a UK first), which comes down to knowing exactly when the LLM should hand over to rules because a mistake would cost someone real money.

We're about 30 people running one agent across energy, broadband, mobile, insurance, mortgages and subscriptions (with more being added), each with its own suppliers, rules and ways of going wrong. With far more problems than people, a person or small team owns each one end to end, from spotting it in the data or a customer conversation to shipping the fix. And because the agent acts, you find out quickly whether the fix worked.

Everyone builds here: a product engineer launched our subscription cancellation product within a couple of months of joining, and a PM rebuilt our WhatsApp agent.

And it's working. We're growing more than 20x year on year, with a market-leading NPS above +80, and we manage well over half a billion pounds of household spending. We've raised more than $30M from Heartcore, Mosaic and a who's who of entrepreneurs who founded Monzo, GoCardless, lastminute.com and Onfido. But the real draw is the team - ask anyone here why they joined and you'll get some version of "to do great work with really smart people".

The goal is household life that's simpler, cheaper and fairer, and most of that is still to build.

## **How we build (worth reading before the role)**

How products get built is changing fast. With AI tooling, a PM can prototype, dig into production data and commit production code to get a change live all in an afternoon. An engineer can own a product area end to end and decide what to build next.

We're leaning into that. Our PMs lean into code and our engineers run products: one of our engineers owns the car insurance targets. We care about whatever gets the job done most effectively, regardless of once upon a time whose job it was meant to be.

We're moving fast and adapting as we go, and we don't have all the answers yet. What should a squad look like when everyone can build? Where does process still help, and where does it just slow you down? What's a PM for when an engineer can run the experiment themselves? We're working it out, and we want someone who is excited to be part of helping figure it out.

## **About the role**

So where does a PM fit? A lot of our work still suits squads: clear targets, a few service lines and a team of engineers. Those squads need product managers to run them. All our roles in product overlap, but this one is centred on product management. If you’d rather spend all your time building, have a look at our Product Builder role.

You’ll take a squad responsible for a key section of our product and service lines and grow them: expand what they cover, understand the levers that drive their performance (automation, new suppliers, what we recommend to members) and increase their commercial value.

Being a Product Manager at Nous is one of the hardest roles we have. The product is complex and we move fast, so you need to be able to hold a lot of context. You'll switch between very different things all day: thinking about OKRs and the plan for the next couple of weeks one moment, getting a PR into production the next, while helping unblock an engineer.

That's also what makes it exciting.

You bring order to fast-moving work, get some sequencing in place so people aren’t each figuring it out on their own, evaluate what’s being shipped, own the reporting and keep the squad’s energy up. You won’t hesitate to make changes yourself, but you won’t be just another builder in the squad either: when you’re heads-down building, you can’t unblock anyone or bring the team together.

Growing a service line here means working across the boundary between product and commercial, so we’re particularly interested in PMs who’ve had real exposure to the commercial side of a business.

Our agent acts in the real world a lot, so saving someone money takes more than great product execution. We also need access to the best tariffs and suppliers, and we have to understand the regulation we operate in. And because Nous is an agent, your nice neat Amplitude funnels don't work: every user's journey can be totally different. So we're after PMs who are excited by everything it takes to make an agentic product work for real households, including the bits that wouldn't traditionally count as "product".

Worth being upfront: we can't tell you yet which service lines you'd own. It depends on the Venn diagram of your particular skill set and the problems we need to solve at the point you join.

## **What matters most**

We need all of these at once:

* Sharp. You pick things up quickly and enjoy hard problems. Given a messy one, you can lay out what you know and what you'd check first, then change your mind as new data turns up.
* Adaptable. We’re working a lot of this out as we go, so the role and the squad will change, probably more than once. You enjoy that. You pick up whatever’s needed, PM work or not, and you work in the open: sharing rough thinking early and changing course when someone has a better idea.
* Delivery. You bring order to a fast-moving squad: clear priorities, sensible sequencing, people unblocked quickly, and an honest look at whether what shipped actually worked.
* Product craft. You find the real problem behind a request and make the trade-offs explicit. You care about the details of what our users actually see.
* Commercial and analytical. You know what your area made last month, what moved it and what you'd do next, and you answer most of your own questions with data. You think in conversion, margin and lifetime value as readily as in features.
* Energy. You've probably worked at a startup. You move fast, you're happy doing the unglamorous work yourself, and you'd rather ship this week's version than polish next quarter's.

And everyone builds here, PMs included. You'll use AI tooling (Claude Code or whatever gets it done) to prototype, dig into data and ship changes yourself. You don't need to be an engineer, but you shouldn't be scared of code.

## **What you'll actually do**

* Grow your service lines. Understand what really drives their performance, be able to measure it, and lead the squad to deliver it.
* Set the squad's OKRs and roadmap, get the sequencing in place, and drive fast, efficient execution.
* Evaluate what’s being shipped, and own the reporting: make sure the reports and the data behind them make sense.
* Work across product and commercial: the suppliers and tariffs we can offer, the regulation we work within, and what that means for what gets built.
* Run experiments, and unblock yourself on the analysis without always needing an analyst.
* Get close to members and ops. Read the conversations, sit with the people handling the edge cases, and fix the parts of the journey where people drop out or get stuck.

## **About you**

You'll likely thrive here if:

* You've been a PM for a few years, ideally at a startup, and you've owned something with a number attached: revenue, conversion, retention.
* You've worked on the commercial side as well as the product side: a P&L, a supplier or partner relationship, pricing, or a whole service line.
* You're comfortable enough with data and code to unblock yourself.

Nice-to-haves:

* You were a software engineer before you moved into product.
* You've worked on a transactional or regulated product: insurance, fintech, energy, marketplaces.
* You've built and shipped your own thing: a startup, a side project, an internal tool that took off.

This probably isn't for you if your PM experience is mostly roadmaps and stakeholder management at a big company, with no number you owned.

## **How we work**

We keep the middle thin, on purpose. There's barely any middle management, which means fewer bottlenecks and room for exceptional people to have real impact without first being promoted into managing others. It's a real bet, not a free lunch. Instead of a manager buffer, you get lots of context and colleagues who help because they're invested, not because an org chart says so. If you need a clear remit handed down before you can move, this probably won't suit you.

Your first 90 days are built around getting you to real ownership safely: pairing when you want it, lots of context, and people who want you to ship. We celebrate the person who built the unglamorous version this week, not whoever thought of it first.

We're office-first, near Farringdon. We do a lot of our best thinking together and being in the same room helps, though we're pragmatic about heads-down work when you need it.

## **Remuneration and benefits**

Compelling package including share options with life-changing upside. We've raised enough to pay real salaries, and we all share in the upside. If we win, we win together.

* 🏢 A great office set up for collaborative work (we already need more whiteboards)
* 💻 The equipment, setup and training you need to do your best work
* 🤝 A high-context environment with real exposure to the big decisions, in the room when it happens
* ☕ Very good coffee
* 🍽️ A well-stocked kitchen (featuring a wildly popular toastie maker)
* 🎉 Informal social every week, something bigger every month
* ✈️ 33 days paid holiday (including bank holidays)
* 💊 Health and dental cash plans, including an employee assistance programme
* 🚴 Travel benefits, including the cycle-to-work scheme and season ticket loans

If you don't tick every box but think you'd be great at this, get in touch anyway.

# The Role

Oneleet helps customers understand the security posture of the vendors they use without repeating the same research for every company. Our shared vendor library brings together findings from public sources so customers can make informed decisions faster.

As our Vendor Supply Chain Analyst, you’ll help build and maintain that library. Your core responsibility is verifying AI-generated research: checking findings against saved sources, resolving gaps, and making sure the evidence supports the conclusions. Engineering owns the AI research pipeline; you’ll provide the feedback that makes its output more accurate and useful.

Each shared vendor record has a security posture score. Customer-specific risk scores are calculated separately using each customer’s exposure to that vendor. Your work ensures the underlying vendor research is reliable.

Preliminary research results appear immediately. Human verification follows, with a target turnaround of 1-2 days. The pipeline automatically re-researches vendors every 90 days and routes significant changes for human review.

* **Recommend criteria updates.** Identify gaps or unclear definitions in the evaluation criteria and propose changes as vendor practices and security expectations evolve.
* **Maintain defensible evidence.** Keep findings traceable to saved sources, with clear reasoning and research dates, so customers and auditors can understand the basis for a finding months later.
* **Develop verification runbooks.** Document repeatable review steps and escalation paths that help the team make consistent decisions.

# Staff AI Engineer, Developer Productivity

Hybrid - London, England

Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles.

Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.

## **About the role**

Oura is rebuilding how it builds software. Every engineer has agentic tooling, and our own pipeline already takes a well-formed ticket to a reviewed, tested commit stack. It runs interactively, headless, and on a cloud sandbox fleet, with its own evals and tracing. We are looking for engineers who use AI as a fundamental building block of both the products we ship and the way we build them.

That is a strong start on one stage of the lifecycle. The next step is the whole loop. As a Staff Engineer on the AI Transformation team, you will architect and own the system that turns agentic development from something power users do into the way hundreds of engineers across iOS, Android, backend and AI services ship every day. That means spec and intake, planning, implementation, review, testing, CI/CD, release, observability and incident follow-up, each with agents doing real work and humans keeping judgment where it matters.

This is a fast-moving, LLM-forward team. We prioritize rapid prototyping, iterative loops and AI-native development, with the speed of a startup and the reach of a product used by millions of members. You can work hybrid from our UK office in London.

You will build the pipeline, measure it, and make it trustworthy enough that teams choose it. Success is measured in validated changes reaching members faster and safer: time to a trustworthy signal, escaped defects, cost per merged change, and how many squads run on the paved path because it is better, not because they were told to.

## **What you will do**

You don't need to do all of these on day one, but these are the kinds of problems you'll own:

* **Set the technical direction for the agentic pipeline:** Make our existing ticket-to-PR pipeline dependable infrastructure. Own its architecture, including agent orchestration, context management and tool calling, and improve its reliability, throughput, cost and developer experience across mobile, backend and web repositories. Run it unattended where the risk allows.
* **Close the loop across the SDLC:** Extend agentic workflows beyond code generation into spec quality checks, test generation, automated review, CI failure triage and repair, release verification, and post-deploy signals, so the system improves from what happens after merge.
* **Prototype fast, then harden:** Get a new workflow running in days, prove it on real tickets with real squads, and turn what holds up into production infrastructure.
* **Run AI in production properly:** Agents in production take more than an API call. Own the eval sets, LLM-as-a-judge grading, versioning, tracing and dashboards that tell us whether a workflow change made things better, including the hardest case: a change that passes CI and is still wrong. Track the numbers that matter (merge rate, rework, time-to-signal, cost per change, escaped defects) and make them visible to engineers and leadership.
* **Make autonomy safe:** Design sandboxing, permissions, human checkpoints and guardrails proportional to risk, with privacy by design as the default. Health data, security and infrastructure changes get stronger controls; low-risk, easily verified work runs hands-off.
* **Lead AI-native engineering by example:** Set the bar for AI-augmented engineering across the organization. Show in your own work what a pipeline-first engineer ships, and raise the craft of the engineers around you.
* **Drive adoption with the teams:** Embed with squads and their AI DRIs, find where the pipeline breaks on real work, fix the system rather than the single output, and turn what works into paved paths, skills, templates and docs other engineers can extend.
* **Partner cross-functionally:** Work with platform, developer productivity, security and privacy, AI infrastructure, mobile and backend squads, product and design, and engineering leadership to make trade-offs explicit and keep everyone moving on one system instead of five parallel ones.

## **Requirements**

We'd love to hear from you if you are:

* **An experienced builder:** Building and operating production systems that other engineers depend on, including developer tooling, internal platforms, or AI infrastructure at scale. We weigh demonstrated outcomes over years.
* **Proven with agentic loops in production:** You have built and operated agentic coding workflows or autonomous loops in a real engineering organization, beyond demos: background agents producing PRs, automated review, CI repair, test generation, or similar, with adoption and measured results.
* **A whole-lifecycle thinker:** You reason about specification, review, testing, CI/CD, release and operations as one system, and you know where the bottleneck moves when code generation gets cheap.
* **A technical leader:** You set direction across teams you don't manage, write the designs others build on, and are trusted with the hard calls on architecture and risk.
* **Strong on fundamentals:** mobile domain or backend APIs, concurrency, distributed systems, testing, debugging and reliability. You treat AI output as a draft and can show how you verify it.
* **Technically versatile:** Fluency in one domain of backend, iOS, or Android, with a stretch into others. You use the tools available to work across platforms and pick up new stacks quickly.
* **Security and privacy conscious:** You understand the responsibility of handling sensitive personal data and of giving agents access to real systems, and you design for both from the start.
* **High agency:** You thrive in ambiguity and shape the requirements yourself through experimentation.
* **Collaborative and resilient:** You bring teams along, take feedback from engineers who are skeptical, share credit, and keep going when experiments fail or the tooling changes under you. You communicate clearly with engineers, managers and non-engineering partners.

## **Would be a benefit**

You don't need all of these, but they're nice signals of fit:

* Experience with coding agents at depth: skills, MCP servers, hooks, sub-agent orchestration, headless runs.
* Built evaluation harnesses or benchmarks for coding agents, or LLM-as-judge grading tied to build and test outcomes.
* Experience with sandboxed execution at scale: ephemeral dev environments, VM or container fleets, macOS build infrastructure.
* Background in developer productivity measurement (DORA, SPACE, DX Core 4) and in turning metrics into decisions without turning them into targets.
* Shipped to mobile apps or other environments with slow, expensive feedback loops.
* Experience in digital health, wearables, MedTech, or other privacy-sensitive or regulated products.

* Valuing good engineering practices: you practise, or want to deepen, XP-style ways of working such as pairing, TDD, refactoring, simple design, and frequent releases.

### About ElevenLabs

ElevenLabs is an AI research and product company transforming how we interact with technology.

We launched in January 2023 with the first human-like AI voice model. Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

### How we work

* High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.
* Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.
* AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.
* Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
* Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

### What we offer

* Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.
* Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.
* Learning & development: ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.
* Social travel: We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.
* Annual company offsite: Each year, we bring the entire team together in a new location - past offsites have included Croatia and Italy.
* Co-working: If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

We're looking for an experienced Analytics Engineer to join our Data team as one of its first hires. You will own the transformation layer between raw data and business decisions: modelling our data in dbt, defining the certified metrics the company runs on, and setting the standards that every analyst and data scientist at ElevenLabs builds.

* Drive the implementation of a world-class metric layer for the company: modelling conventions, project structure, testing, CI, and documentation.
* Design and maintain the certified KPI layer for product (activation, adoption, retention, usage), finance (billing, ARR, revenue), and company-wide topics, built to withstand audit scrutiny.
* Partner with Data Engineering on evolving the data warehouse architecture, and with stakeholders to turn ambiguous questions into trusted, reusable data products, including data served through AI agents.

Requirements

Demonstrated experience building and scaling a dbt project and metrics layer, ideally as one of the first analytics engineers on a growing team.

* Expert knowledge of dbt and advanced SQL (required); strong grasp of dimensional modelling, grain, and incremental patterns.
* Proficiency across the modern data stack (BigQuery or similar warehouse, Python, BI tools such as Looker).
* Rigour around data quality: you test, document, and reconcile by default, and you spot a model that runs cleanly but is quietly wrong.
* Strong ability to understand varied stakeholder requirements, push back where needed, and translate them into generalised, well-documented models.

Bonus:

* Experience modelling billing, subscription and ARR data (Stripe, Salesforce) or product event data at scale.
* Experience serving data to LLM-based agents or building semantic / metrics layers consumed by AI tools.
* Experience with CI for data (Slim CI, data contracts, PII policy tags) and infrastructure-as-code for warehouse access.

This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in Europe, with the ability to operate in GMT and GMT+1 timezones. If you prefer, you can work from our offices in London and Warsaw.

**2. Get hands-on in delivery where it adds most value**

**Attributes**

Shawbrook provides finance to a wide range of customer segments that value the premium experience, flexibility and certainly we deliver.  We are a purpose-led organisation, with a focus on delivering long-term sustainable value for all our stakeholders.

We have a diversified offering, with our innovative lending propositions tailored to meet specific customer needs in carefully selected markets across SME, Real Estate and Personal. Our products range from complex structured credit facilities for growth-focused businesses to mortgages for professional landlords and property investors, as well as simple loans for consumers delivered digitally.  We fuel our lending through customer deposits, which we attract by delivering a premium experience, choice and consistently great value to smart savers.

The business model we have created is unique and difficult to replicate, with our ‘best of both’ approach combining deep human expertise with advanced digital, tech and data capabilities.  This combination not only allows us to deliver excellent customer experiences, but to do so efficiently and at scale.  We are proud of our innovative and agile culture, which drives consistently high employee engagement scores and makes Shawbrook an attractive destination for the best talent. If you’re willing to roll up your sleeves, contribute new ideas and believe anything is possible, you’re our kind of person.

Work with us because you:

* Want to be part of a bank built for the dynamics of the modern world

* Want to belong to a diverse culture that stands shoulder to shoulder with minority and underrepresented groups
* Care about society and the environment and want to be part of a business that cares too
* Want to continue to grow professionally and be the best version of yourself

## The Role & Responsibilities

This role is the operational control point for the internal valuations function. It ensures valuation requests are complete, appropriately triaged, allocated, tracked and evidenced, enabling RICS-qualified valuers to focus on technical assessment and assurance. The role does not make technical valuation judgements or credit decisions.

* The Valuation Operations and Workflow Coordinator owns the efficient and controlled flow of back book valuations through the end-to-end process.
* The role holder will coordinate case allocation, triage support,  maintain documentation and reliable records and ensure that cases meet agreed service levels, coordinates operational MI and governance requirements.
* Act as the first operational point of contact for valuation requests, ensuring each request is logged, complete and traceable from receipt to closure.
* Coordinate workflow and allocation across internal valuers and external panel providers in line with agreed methodology, capacity, allocation and conflict-of-interest rules.
* Maintain accurate and timely records in the authoritative valuation system and valuation register, including supporting evidence and audit trail.
* Monitor case progress, due dates, service-level performance, outstanding actions and exceptions; escalate emerging risks or delays promptly.
* Produce and coordinate operational MI that provides clear visibility of requests/demand, outputs, backlogs, turnaround times, exceptions, data quality and supplier performance.
* Support a robust control environment through reconciliations, document control, evidence retention and data-quality checks.
* Provide dependable administrative and workflow support to the RICS-qualified surveyor team, while respecting the separation between operational coordination, technical judgement and credit decision making.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Case intake and triage support.** Receive and log valuation requirements arising from periodic regulatory revaluations, new lending post valuation queries, impairment or provisioning amendments, valuation expiry and data-quality exceptions.
* **Instruction preparation and allocation.** Prepare clear, complete instructions for external providers or internal assessment, including the agreed scope, valuation basis, property details, lending information and required completion date.
* **Workflow management and service delivery.** Maintain an accurate live workflow view of all cases, including stage, owner, due date, ageing, dependency and status.
* **System data and evidence management.** Maintain and update valuation systems and registers promptly for onward use and visibility to  impairment and capital requirements as appropriate.
* **MI reporting and supplier performance.** Coordinate monthly operational MI covering demand, outputs, turnaround times, backlog, service-level performance, data quality and revaluation activity.
* **Controls and continuous improvement.** Operate in line with valuation policy and methodology standards.  Maintain a controlled audit trail for each case.  Identify opportunities to simplify workflow, reduce manual effort and utilise AI where appropriate to strengthen data quality and improve MI, controls or system use

## The Person

**Skills & Experience**

* Experience of case management and workflow coordination, operational controls or MI within a regulated financial services, property or lending environment.
* Strong administrative control, organisation and prioritisation skills, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams and fixed deadlines.
* Excellent attention to detail and a proven ability to maintain accurate, complete and auditable records.
* Confident use of data systems and reconcile records, identify exceptions and produce meaningful MI.
* Ability to communicate clearly and constructively with internal stakeholders, RICS professionals and external suppliers.
* Understanding of residential and/or commercial property valuations, lending collateral or panel-management processes is desirable.
* Awareness of data protection, record retention, outsourced supplier controls and conduct expectations in a regulated lending environment.

**Education/Professional Qualifications**

Shawbrook is committed to providing opportunities to all candidates, and understand that not all candidates may possess a qualification or education aligned to the role. We will assess each candidate on their individual experience and skills, and not solely on level of education.

Established in 2009 in Sleaford, Lincolnshire, SHD remain committed to providing exceptional levels of service and flexibility coupled with a wealth of experience within the composite industry.   SHD Composite Materials Ltd are at the leading edge of advanced composites technology and manufacture a wide range of thermoset prepregs, which include carbon, glass, aramid, natural and hybrid fabrics whilst also offering a toll impregnation service.

The purpose of this role is to set up every production run for success. You will prepare accurate pre-production paperwork and calculate, prepare, inspect and allocate raw materials for the Fabric Lines, ensuring that only correct, quality-checked fabric is committed to manufacturing, that production runs continuously, that stock is controlled and that full traceability is maintained.

In this role, you will be the vital link between planning and production: organising the pre-production paperwork, calculating material requirements, and preparing and checking every fabric before it is committed to manufacturing. * Work in accordance with company Health and Safety procedures at all times.
* Work to SHD’s quality standards and procedures, acting as the first quality checkpoint before materials are released to manufacturing
* Prepare, check and organise all pre-production paperwork (e.g. SOCs works orders, batch records, material requirements, bottom end sheets and labels) so that every job is complete, accurate and ready before it reaches the line
* Calculate material requirements for each order on the production plan, including fabric lengths, areas, weights, roll quantities and waste allowances, and allocate the correct materials to each line to ensure continuity of production

* Exceptional attention to detail and a methodical, quality-first approach to work

These values are the foundation of our work, and we are committed to upholding them in everything we do.
Our co-founders are Bret Taylor and Clay Bavor. Bret currently serves as Board Chair of OpenAI. Previously, he was co-CEO of Salesforce (which had acquired the company he founded, Quip) and CTO of Facebook. Bret was also one of Google's earliest product managers and co-creator of Google Maps. What you’ll do
Design and deliver production-grade AI agents: You'll build and ship highly performant, reliable, and intuitive AI agents that are central, mission-critical and drive revenue directly to Sierra's growth. These aren't prototypes—they are powerful, scalable systems running in production environments across industries like finance, healthcare, and commerce.
Drive the Agent Development Life Cycle (ADLC): You'll have complete ownership and autonomy from initial pilot through deployment and continuous iteration. You'll be responsible for building, tuning, and evolving AI agents in production environments, defining the standard for ADLC best practices along the way.

Create generalizable AI agent frameworks tailored for industry-specific use cases. See some examples in our financial services blog!

Experiment with the latest voice models and figure out how to integrate them at scale to enterprise-grade customers

Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems

* Runbooks and operational hardening across the tools this role manages.

## About Supermove

Supermove builds software and AI for moving companies. We've raised $30M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors.

We started in 2019 as the system that runs a moving business: sales, operations, crews, billing. Today that system runs moving companies across the US, Canada, and Australia, from single-location movers to some of the largest van lines and franchise systems in North America.

Now we're putting AI to work on top of it. Our Voice Agents answer and call leads, book moves, and hand off to a person at the right moment. Autopilot, our agent platform, goes further. It understands what's happening across a business, flags what needs attention, and executes work that previously required employees to handle manually.

We're building AI that doesn't just assist employees. It takes on real operational work.

## The Role

We're looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer to build and deploy AI agents for some of the largest moving companies in North America.

You'll work directly with customers to understand their operations, design and implement AI workflows, write production code, and get agents working reliably in the real world.

**You'll be both deploying our AI products and building them.**

Some problems can be solved through configuration and prompting. Others require new integrations, changes to our agent architecture, better tooling, or entirely new product capabilities. You'll be expected to make those changes directly in our codebase, working alongside our core engineering team.

You'll own deployments from initial discovery through go-live and ongoing improvement, working closely with customer executives, operations teams, implementation managers, and Supermove engineers.

One day you might be onsite with a customer understanding how their call center operates. The next, you're writing code to improve how our agents handle complex workflows, debugging tool calls, or building evaluations to identify why an agent failed.

Enterprise moving is complicated. A single customer can have hundreds of locations, several disconnected systems, and different processes across branches. Getting AI to work reliably in that environment is a difficult engineering problem.

We want engineers who enjoy working directly with customers, figuring out what needs to be built, and shipping it.

## What You'll Do

* **Build and improve our AI agents.** Write production code to extend our Voice Agent and Autopilot platforms. Improve agent capabilities, tool integrations, workflow execution, reliability, and performance.
* **Own enterprise AI deployments.** Work directly with customers to understand their operations, design solutions, and take agents from initial configuration through production rollout and optimization.
* **Design and implement AI workflows.** Translate real business processes into agent behavior, tools, integrations, and human handoffs. Determine what can be handled through configuration versus what requires new engineering.
* **Debug and optimize agents in production.** Analyze call transcripts, execution traces, tool calls, and customer data. Identify failure modes, improve prompts and code, build evaluations, and measure whether your changes actually work.
* **Build integrations and technical solutions.** Connect Supermove's agents with customer systems, APIs, and third-party platforms. Work across the stack to solve deployment problems and extend product capabilities.
* **Turn customer needs into reusable product features.** Identify patterns across deployments and build improvements that benefit more than one customer. Work closely with product and engineering to make our platform more powerful and easier to deploy.
* **Drive deployments and customer outcomes.** Own technical delivery, coordinate with implementation managers and other teams, lead onsite working sessions, and ensure customers achieve measurable business results.
* **Work directly with customer leadership.** Explain technical decisions, understand business requirements, manage tradeoffs, and build trust with everyone from executives to frontline operators.

## What We're Looking For

* **3+ years of software engineering experience.** You've built, shipped, and maintained production software. You're comfortable working in an existing codebase, debugging complex systems, and independently delivering features.
* **Strong engineering fundamentals.** You're proficient in at least one modern programming language, comfortable with APIs, databases, integrations, and backend systems, and able to work across the stack when needed.
* **Experience building with AI.** You've worked with LLM APIs, agents, tool calling, or AI-powered applications. You understand the challenges of making nondeterministic systems reliable, and you're comfortable working with prompts, evaluations, and agent workflows.
* **Product-minded problem solving.** You don't just implement requirements. You understand the underlying problem, design practical solutions, and think about how your work can scale beyond a single customer.
* **Comfort working directly with customers.** You can lead technical discovery, explain complex systems clearly, and translate ambiguous business requirements into working software.
* **Strong ownership and execution.** You can manage competing priorities, work independently, and drive complex projects to completion. When something breaks, your instinct is to investigate and fix it.
* **Ability to operate across technical and business contexts.** You're as comfortable discussing architecture with an engineer as you are explaining business impact to a CEO or COO.

Experience with voice AI, real-time systems, agent frameworks, or enterprise integrations is a plus. Experience in moving, logistics, or field services is helpful but not required.

## Why This Role Matters

We're moving from AI that answers questions to AI that actually runs business operations.

Our largest customers are where that transition gets proven. They operate across hundreds of locations, with complex workflows, legacy systems, and thousands of employees. Building AI that works reliably in these environments will shape what our entire platform becomes.

As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you'll be on the front lines of that work. You'll see firsthand where agents succeed and fail, write the code to make them better, and turn what you learn into product capabilities that scale across our customers.

You'll work directly with our CEO, engineering, and product leadership, with substantial ownership over both customer deployments and the evolution of our AI platform.

## Interview Process

Intro call → Technical interview → Practical AI engineering and deployment exercise → Founder interview.

### Team Leadership

* Mentor and develop more junior Data Solutions scientists, growing their domain knowledge as well as their client-facing skills

* Build standardized, scalable scientific workflows (feasibility templates, analysis frameworks, data POVs) so the team can rapidly support more partners without lowering quality
* Act as the first point of escalation for complex or non-standard scientific requests, and involve senior leadership early on enterprise-level opportunities

  

### Partnerships and Revenue Growth

In practice they are usually the same merchant at different points in time: a merchant who goes quiet in March becomes, by June, an unpaid fee, a terminal still in the field and a balance nobody is chasing. Collections activity also sits in pockets across the business, from unpaid subscriptions and fees, negative balances and chargebacks to terminal recovery, dissolved companies and fraud losses. As our credit products grow, so will the need.  
  
You’ll bring all of this together under one strategy, one queue and one set of metrics. We want someone who knows collections and its pain points, and who approaches the whole lifecycle with a product and design mindset: redesigning journeys end to end, and deciding where AI and automation belong and where people add the most value. You’ll start hands-on and build a small credit control team as the capability grows.  
  
**What you’ll do**

* Own the retention-to-recovery pipeline end to end, from the first churn signal to write-off or debt sale, running from one prioritised queue with one set of definitions.
* Work with our data team to build and run an AI retention engine that identifies merchants heading towards churn, recommends the next best action for each and puts them in a queue to be worked. Prove what works with holdout groups, and do more of it.
* Agree with Commercial how save conversations are delivered, and make sure our own risk actions, such as held settlements, are weighed before they push a good merchant out.
* Design a proper exit for every merchant who leaves: a recorded reason, fees stopped, terminal returned, final balance netted and a final statement, so merchants do not need to contact Customer Relations to close their account.
* Build automated collections that start the day a balance turns negative: settlement netting, direct debit, card on file, payment links and payment plans. Journeys run through the Teya app and portal first, with phone as the exception.
* Run managed and external recovery for larger balances: credit control, payment plans, an agency panel, write-off thresholds and, as a last resort, debt sale.
* Own the recovery strategy for fraud-related balances with Fraud Operations and Legal. They keep investigation and legal action; you make sure every balance has a recovery route and a priority.
* Run the existing book as a separate remediation project with its own end date, so it does not pull focus from the new flow.
* Connect the work of Billing, Payments, Logistics (terminal recovery), Credit, Customer Relations and the termination and withheld funds process into one joined-up flow.

**In your first six months**

* Definitions agreed and reported for flow recovery rate, stock recovery rate and true churn.
* A single queue live, worked by hand from simple rules while the model is built.
* An exit process in place for every leaving merchant, and an automated collections first version running in at least one market.
* The credit control team hired or in hiring, and the legacy book project under way with a clear plan.

* The first retention model live, beating the rules-based baseline and tested against holdout groups.

* The first debt sale completed, where the legal and data preconditions are met.
* Measurably fewer Customer Relations contacts from merchants who are leaving or owe us money.

* Comfortable with data: defining metrics, working with data scientists on models and reading the results of tests and holdouts.
* A sound grasp of fair treatment and regulation in collections: treating small businesses fairly, spotting vulnerability, applying Consumer Duty principles where they apply, and knowing why we never contact a merchant under AML or fraud review.

Growth & Natural Capital (EGNC) Portfolio based in Palladium's Americas region, partners with mining companies

reforestation, and sustainable agriculture—that benefit mining communities and

innovative solutions that drive inclusive growth and deliver sustainable value

Turning Point’s drug & alcohol services are currently expanding during a really exciting time in the sector with new funding and investment. ### Role Responsibility

Recovery Workers act as ‘key workers’ to a caseload of service users, supporting them to decide their goals around treatment and develop plans to achieve these. The role includes maintaining regular contact with your clients, offering advice, information and psycho-social interventions as well as providing assessments, risk management planning and working closely with our clinical staff around prescribing needs and partner agencies. However, we also recognise that many people have transferrable skills from other backgrounds such as mental health, housing or other health and social care provision. The roles are varied, so flexibility, an ability to work dynamically on a one to one and group basis and knowledge of relapse and other barriers to recovery will be vital but we can help to shape these skills where needed. # Overnight Mental Health Crisis Peer Support Worker

### Job Introduction

Our Recovery Lounge in Manchester was first commissioned in 2021 and has provided vital evening support to people across the city for the past five years. During this time, we have developed a strong track record of supporting people in mental health crisis who are seeking immediate support.

Due to the success of the service, we are now extending our opening hours to provide overnight support. This exciting new project is initially funded for 12 months, with a further two years of funding already earmarked subject to successful delivery. We are now recruiting a dedicated team to help shape and deliver this enhanced service.

**The Role**

As an Overnight Peer Support Worker, you'll be at the heart of the service, providing emotional and practical support to people who may be experiencing emotional distress or a mental health crisis.

Drawing on your own lived experience of mental health challenges and recovery, you will use this experience appropriately to inspire hope, build trust and support people accessing the service. Your ability to share aspects of your recovery journey in a safe and professional way will help people feel understood, empowered and less alone in their experiences.

Working in an environment where no two shifts are the same, you'll help create a safe, welcoming and supportive space where people feel listened to, understood and empowered to move forward.

You'll work alongside colleagues to support individuals accessing the service, helping them explore coping strategies, build resilience and identify positive next steps as part of their recovery journey.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Provide compassionate, recovery-focused support to individuals experiencing a mental health crisis.
* Build positive and supportive relationships with individuals accessing the service.
* Use your lived experience in a safe, purposeful and professional way to support and encourage others in their recovery.
* Undertake triage assessments to identify individuals' needs and determine the most appropriate support.
* Complete risk assessments and contribute to ongoing risk management plans.
* Identify and respond appropriately to risk, safeguarding concerns and crisis situations.
* Offer emotional support and encouragement to help people manage difficult situations and work towards their recovery goals.
* Support individuals to identify their strengths, develop coping strategies and make informed choices about their wellbeing.
* Promote hope, independence and self-confidence through meaningful engagement and person-centred support.
* Maintain accurate and timely records in line with GDPR and organisational requirements.
* Work collaboratively with colleagues and partner agencies to ensure the best outcomes for service users.
* Contribute to the smooth running of the service, including general housekeeping duties to maintain a comfortable and welcoming environment.
* Promote a safe, inclusive and welcoming environment where everyone is treated with dignity and respect.

**About You**

We're looking for passionate, resilient and empathetic individuals who are committed to supporting people with mental health needs.

You will ideally have:

* Lived experience of mental health challenges, emotional distress or crisis, and experience of recovery.
* The ability to use and appropriately share your lived experience to inspire hope and support others on their recovery journey.
* Experience working within mental health, health and social care, or a related support environment.
* Experience of undertaking triage, risk assessments and risk management, ideally within a mental health, health or social care setting.

**Role Overview**

The **Build & Release Support Engineer** provides high-impact technical support for the customer’s **build, release, and CI/CD systems**, which every developer depends on to ship software.

This role is deeply developer-facing and centers on **build pipelines, software supply chain workflows, and release tooling**. You will help engineers resolve blockers across tools like Maven, Java build systems, Docker, Spinnaker, Artifactory, and Jenkins.

Success depends on strong troubleshooting skills, clear communication, and the ability to manage multiple threads and tickets in parallel. You will be the front line, ensuring developers can deliver reliably, safely, and at high velocity.

* Healthy volume of threads and tickets handled with high-quality outcomes
* Consistent achievement of time-based SLAs
* High customer satisfaction through surveys
* Accurate classification of issue type, severity, and patterns

**What Will Be True When You Succeed**

* Developers ship faster with fewer build and release blockers
* CI/CD and software supply chain tooling become more reliable and more usable
* Escalations decrease due to strong frontline troubleshooting

**Core Work Units**

**1. Frontline Support for Build & Release Systems**

* Manage Slack threads and tickets (roughly 50/50)
* Triage build failures, broken pipelines, dependency issues, and configuration errors
* Provide fast, accurate context before escalating
* Handle multiple interactions in parallel without losing track

**2. Deep-Dive Troubleshooting & Incident Support**

* Diagnose complex build, packaging, or artifact problems independently
* Investigate issues involving Maven builds, Java compilation, Docker images, Artifactory repos, Jenkins jobs, and Spinnaker pipelines

**3. Escalation Management**

* Complete a thorough analysis before escalating
* Gather all required details upfront to reduce back-and-forth
* Produce clean, high-quality escalation tickets that downstream teams can act on immediately

* Maintain and refine FAQs and internal documentation
* Create problem–solution one-pagers for recurring issues
* Document newly solved problems instinctively and thoroughly

**Frontline Support**

* Quickly identifies whether the issue is build-related, config-related, or infra-related
* Moves smoothly from triage to deeper analysis
* Juggles multiple developer inquiries without missing follow-ups

**Deep-Dive & Incident Support**

* Coordinates multi-user incidents involving large build failures
* Communicates clearly during investigation, root-cause analysis, and resolution

**Escalations**

* Provides complete logs, reproduction steps, build metadata, and context
* Saves downstream engineers time with clean, accurate handoffs

**Documentation**

* Proactively updates and refines materials for clarity and accuracy
* Quickly turns real-world issues into reusable knowledge

**What You’ll Love**

## Description

## Embedded QA Engineer

**Bring your curiosity. Bring your troubleshooting skills. Expect to get hands-on.**

A device stops responding. Is it the software, a network setting, a loose connection or something nobody has thought of yet? If you enjoy following the evidence until you find the answer, you could be exactly who we’re looking for.

At Vix Technology, we’re looking for an Embedded QA Engineer to test the software behind physical devices, displays and on-vehicle equipment. Your work will help us release reliable products that perform in the real world—even when the power drops, the network disappears or a device needs to recover on its own.

**What you’ll get stuck into**

You’ll take ownership of manual and system-level testing, setting up equipment, installing software builds and creating reliable, repeatable test environments. From checking everyday functionality to exploring awkward edge cases, you’ll put our products through their paces and provide clear evidence of what’s ready for release.

Some days, you’ll be working through Linux logs, checking application behaviour or investigating communication between devices and supporting services. On others, you’ll be tracing a wiring fault, making a test cable or reaching for a multimeter. You’ll need to feel equally comfortable at the command line and the test bench.

You’ll explore how equipment behaves during startup, shutdown, reboots, power loss and network interruptions. When something fails, you’ll reproduce the problem, work out where it originates and give developers the detail they need to resolve it.

Along the way, you’ll keep test plans, defect reports, release versions and device configurations accurate and easy to follow. You’ll also run existing automated tests, investigate failures and help identify where additional coverage would make a difference. Sharing discoveries and supporting junior colleagues will be part of the job too.

## Requirements

**What you’ll bring**

We’re interested in people who combine strong testing instincts with practical technical skills. You should have:

* Experience testing software on embedded hardware, with strong manual, exploratory and integration testing skills.
* Confidence troubleshooting embedded Linux using command-line tools, SSH, logs, process checks and configuration files.
* Practical networking knowledge, including TCP/IP, ports, static IP addresses, gateways and DNS.
* Hands-on electronics skills: making and repairing cables, soldering and crimping connections, reading wiring diagrams and schematics, and using multimeters and oscilloscopes to investigate faults.
* A clear, methodical approach to test documentation, release records and defect reporting, with experience using tools such as Git and Jira.

You’ll be comfortable investigating across software, operating systems, networking, power and hardware, including unfamiliar or legacy platforms. You don’t need advanced circuit design experience, but you should be able to set up equipment safely and investigate hardware-related failures independently.

**A few useful extras**

Experience with Robot Framework, scripting in Python or Bash, MQTT, serial communications, GPIO or watchdogs would be welcome. Familiarity with Windows CE, .NET Compact Framework, Docker, simulators or device connections to cloud and back-office services would also come in handy.

We’re open to thoughtful use of approved AI tools to help develop test scenarios, analyse findings and improve documentation. You’ll remain responsible for checking the results and protecting confidential information.

**Sound like your kind of challenge?**

You’re curious, persistent and organised. You can work through incomplete documentation, explain a tricky fault clearly and keep investigating when a problem only appears once every twenty reboots.

If you enjoy understanding how the whole system works—and helping make it more reliable—we’d love to hear from you.

**With us, you can shape the commercial decisions that drive our Consumer business forward.**

As Senior Finance Business Partner – Consumer, you’ll take on a senior leadership role across our Finance and Consumer Leadership Teams, reporting into the CFO organisation and working closely with the Consumer Director and Senior Leadership Team.

You’ll be the principal finance adviser to the Consumer business, helping shape our commercial strategy and translating our priorities into clear plans, investment choices and measurable outcomes. You’ll bring an independent, enterprise-wide perspective to decisions across growth, pricing, propositions, portfolio choices, channel economics, customer value, cost and transformation, balancing near-term performance with sustainable revenue, profitability and customer outcomes.

You’ll lead the Consumer planning, budgeting and forecasting agenda and own the integrated view of performance across revenue, margin, Opex, Capex, customer, channel and operational drivers. Through monthly and in-cycle performance reviews, you’ll turn performance data, variance analysis and forward indicators into clear actions, providing early visibility of risks and opportunities and ensuring accountable mitigation and transparent escalation to local and Group stakeholders. You’ll also oversee the financial performance of relevant shared services, including Retail Stores, Publicity and Terminals, and present and defend Consumer plans, forecasts and performance with senior local and Group stakeholders.

A key part of your role will be steering how we invest and allocate resources. You’ll own the financial evaluation, challenge and approval of material Consumer business cases, including tariffs, pricing, propositions, promotions, products and strategic investments. You’ll ensure decisions are supported by robust economics, modelling, sensitivities and scenarios, with clear consideration of risk, customer impact and strategic alignment. You’ll set the standard for concise, forward-looking and decision-relevant management information, integrating financial and non-financial KPIs to create a consistent performance narrative and trusted single version of the truth. Using HFM, SAP, SAP BI and local reporting tools, you’ll deepen commercial insight while simplifying, standardising and automating recurring activity. You’ll sponsor improvements across data quality, forecasting, reporting, governance and decision processes, and encourage thoughtful experimentation and innovation while maintaining disciplined management of return and risk.

You’ll act as a trusted and independent sounding board to the Consumer Director, CFO and wider leadership team, communicating complex financial and commercial issues clearly and bringing evidence-based recommendations to executive discussions. You’ll build relationships across Consumer, Finance, Strategy, Technology, Operations, Group and other operating companies, bringing customer, competitor and wider market perspectives into our decision-making and helping the organisation respond effectively to change and uncertainty.

Just as importantly, you’ll lead and develop a team of finance professionals, creating the capability, confidence and commercial mindset needed to influence the business at pace. You’ll set clear outcomes and standards, coach and develop talent, create stretch opportunities and build a diverse succession pipeline. As a member of both the Vodafone Ireland Finance Leadership Team and Consumer Leadership Team, you’ll contribute to wider Finance and company people priorities, capability building and ways of working, while acting as Cost Centre Manager for Commercial Finance and ensuring the function’s resources are managed with discipline and a clear focus on value.

You need to enjoy working closely with your peers of very talented engineers.
A day in the life
You'll solve complex challenges by designing and implementing scalable solutions that protect Amazon's customers and systems. You'll work with security engineering teams to transform domain expertise into software that mitigates risks at unprecedented scale. In a typical day, you might:
• Develop code that reduces manual security processes by 50% or more, enabling our teams to respond faster and more effectively
• Partner with cross-functional teams to translate intricate security requirements into elegant, high-performance software solutions
• Prototype and implement security tools that protect millions of customers and billions in transactions
You'll work in an environment that values rapid innovation, where your ideas can move from concept to production in weeks, not months. Your work directly impacts Amazon's ability to maintain the highest standards of customer trust and system resilience.
About the team
This team will work with local and international security teams to design a greenfield product that solves the complex problem of rapidly knowing critical security details about every Amazon application. This team of problem solvers is heavily customer obsessed with a leaning toward rapid prototyping and implementation.
Diverse Experiences
Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why Amazon Security
At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores.
Work/Life Balance

* University degree in a relevant area of engineering or science (e.g. Control Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mechatronics).
* Relevant work experience, preferably in industry.
* Practical experience with industrial control systems such as PLCs and Variable Frequency Drives.
* Good programming skills, including Python and familiarity with C.
* High degree of autonomy, the ability to learn new applications and technologies rapidly, and enthusiasm for learning.
* Good communication skills.

## Desirable

* Practical experience of system identification and characterisation of electromechanical and dynamic systems.

# Senior GIS Product Engineer

## Build cloud-native geospatial products that make Earth observation data accessible and actionable, shaping how AI and customers understand our changing planet.

**We are Here to Protect Tomorrow.**

**Xoople is Earth’s System of RecordTM**

At Xoople, we're building the Earth's data infrastructure layer for AI. Our mission is to enable AI to understand and predict physical changes on the world's surface by creating Earth’s System of RecordTM—a trusted, enterprise-grade data foundation that connects the physical world to digital systems.

By transforming vast amounts of Earth observation data into actionable insights, we help enterprises and governments make faster, smarter decisions about risk, operations, sustainability, and growth. Working at Xoople means joining a team creating a world-first capability that will fundamentally change what AI can understand and do, bringing real-world context into every business decision.

**About the Role**

As a Senior GIS Product Engineer, you will design and deliver Xoople's geospatial Data & AI products, enabling scalable and efficient access to Earth observation data. Combining GIS, remote sensing and data engineering expertise, you will build the cloud-native platform, services and map interfaces that turn complex spatial data into reliable, accessible products for advanced analytics and AI-driven use cases. Flexible work model depending on location (Spain or the UK)

**Impact You Own**

* Enable scalable geospatial data products by designing architectures that support efficient and scalable access to Earth observation data.
* Build and operate the serving layer that makes the archive usable, including STAC catalogue and search, dynamic raster tiling, and vector tile pipelines.
* Develop and maintain robust GIS applications, tools and interactive map interfaces using cloud-native and ESRI-based technologies.
* Design and optimise geospatial data models, workflows and spatial analysis capabilities, including the freshness, completeness and lineage metrics that make a data product trustworthy.
* Contribute to product innovation and R&D, including putting AI models into production over the archive and emerging remote sensing capabilities.
* Support interoperability across Xoople's data ecosystem and with the tools our customers already use, ensuring reliable, observable and secure operation.
* Collaborate with product and engineering teams to translate business needs into impactful technical solutions, and evaluate emerging GIS, cloud and AI technologies to apply them pragmatically to the platform.

**What We’re Looking For**

* Proven experience developing geospatial Data & AI products or GIS solutions across the full product lifecycle, owning technical delivery from design through to production operation.
* Hands-on experience building interactive geospatial visualisations and web mapping applications using ESRI or open-source technologies (MapLibre GL JS, deck.gl, OpenLayers, CesiumJS).
* Experience designing and operating raster and vector tiling solutions using COG, Zarr, STAC, TiTiler, PostGIS or similar technologies, with sound judgement on dynamic versus pre-rendered tiling and its caching and cost consequences.
* Strong understanding of OGC standards, including OGC API, WMS, WFS, WMTS and WCS, as well as XYZ tile schemes, STAC API and CQL2 filtering.
* Strong expertise in geospatial analysis, spatial data structures, algorithms and geospatial data modeling, including spatial indexing and coordinate reference system handling.
* Solid programming skills in Python and SQL applied to geospatial processing, APIs and data platforms (GDAL/OGR, rasterio, GeoPandas, xarray, PostGIS, FastAPI).
* A pragmatic, expert-level approach to AI-assisted and agentic development tools, holding the same quality bar as hand-written work.
* Effective collaboration and communication skills gained in cross-functional, international teams.
* A degree in Computer Science, Geography, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

**What Makes You Stand Out**

Experience integrating AI models into production, working with geospatial foundation models and embedding-based approaches, running distributed remote sensing workflows, designing cloud-native geospatial architectures, or contributing to open-source projects and R&D in Earth observation.

**What We Offer**

We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to support your wellbeing and growth, together with meaningful ownership, continuous learning and the opportunity to build a world-first Earth data capability with a global, mission-driven team.

**Our Value in Action**

Our vision is **‘To be the most trusted source of Earth intelligence’**.

We live it through four guiding principles:

* **Everyone is welcome.** We value uniqueness and authenticity.
* **Think beyond boundaries.** Real change comes from listening and thinking differently.
* **Make a positive difference.** We exist to protect tomorrow — for the planet and people’s lives.
* **Together we are stronger.** We partner, share expertise and win as one.

**DEI & Belonging**

At Xoople, our strength lies in our differences. We’re building a workplace where everyone feels safe to be themselves, heard, valued and empowered to shape a more inclusive future. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are glad to make reasonable adjustments during hiring, just let us know.

**Ready to help build Earth’s System of RecordTM?**

***Born in Spain, designed for the world.* #EarthAI #EarthIntelligence #TechForGood**

# Robotics Engineer

## Location

London Office

## Employment Type

Full time

## Location Type

OverviewApplication

**Help shape the future of robotics in construction.**

**ABOUT XYZ REALITY**

XYZ Reality created the world’s first and only engineering-grade augmented reality solution, purpose-built for the construction industry. Our holographic technology sits within The Atom, a smart, site-safe headset and hardhat, and is used on live projects to ensure schemes are delivered on time and on budget.

XYZ has grown to over 150 staff across the UK, US and Europe, and works with mission-critical organisations and construction companies to deliver major projects.

**THE ROLE**

Construction sites are some of the hardest environments for robot autonomy: they change every day and are full of clutter, obstacles and people. XYZ Reality’s robotics programme is extending our technology toward robots that can operate reliably in them, from autonomous data collection and construction progress capture through to executing construction tasks.

We’re looking for a Robotics Engineer to make that real. You’ll work hands-on with robot hardware in our London office, using a modern stack (ROS 2, NVIDIA Isaac Lab, learning-based control), and see your work tested in real construction environments, not just in simulation.

This is a hands-on, individual contributor role focused on robot software and algorithmic control, backed by a good working knowledge of robot hardware. If you have strong robotics fundamentals from an MSc, PhD or applied research group, love making systems work on real robots, and want your ideas to shape the direction of a programme, we want to hear from you.

This is an office-based role at our London site in Angel, Islington.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Integrate robots with XYZ’s software, bringing up ROS / ROS 2 interfaces, robot control, sensors, compute and data flows, and building repeatable tools for bring-up, configuration, logging and monitoring.
* Establish reliable baseline control and develop task-specific behaviours for navigation, positioning and capture, training and tuning control policies in simulation and validating them on hardware.
* Develop localisation-aware path planning, waypoint execution and obstacle handling, working with project and site teams to turn work plans and BIM-derived locations into robot missions.
* Integrate capture payloads so images, pose, timing and mission status flow reliably into XYZ’s construction progress workflows, working with navigation, SLAM and perception colleagues.
* Design test scenarios and measure mission completion, coverage, localisation quality, intervention, recovery and repeatability, improving the system through measured iterations.
* Bring technical expertise and new ideas to the programme, comparing scripted, motion-planning and learning-based approaches and helping shape what comes next.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* MSc or PhD in Robotics, Controls, Computer Science, Mechatronics or a related discipline, or equivalent applied robotics experience. Industry experience is not required.
* Hands-on experience building, programming or directly controlling a physical robot, from an academic project, research lab or industry.
* Strong Python and C++, practical ROS experience (ideally ROS 2) and working knowledge of kinematics, coordinate frames, feedback control, state estimation, path planning and robot hardware.
* Experience training or tuning robot control policies (e.g. reinforcement or imitation learning) using NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim or similar tools, with a rigorous experimental approach.
* The right to work in the UK. We’re unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

**KEY EXPERIENCE & SKILLS**

* ROS / ROS 2, Python & C++
* Robot control, kinematics, state estimation & path planning
* NVIDIA Isaac Lab / Isaac Sim, reinforcement or imitation learning
* Sim-to-real transfer on physical hardware (desirable)
* Navigation, SLAM, perception & sensor fusion (desirable)
* Mobile or field robotics, BIM/CAD or construction technology (desirable)

**BENEFITS**

🏝️ 25 days annual leave + public holidays  
🩺 Private healthcare with Vitality  
🎄 Christmas shutdown days on top of leave allowance (2–4 per year usually)  
🚇 Office located within a 5-minute walk from Angel station  
🪙 Annual salary reviews  
🥳 Summer & Christmas staff parties  
🍣 Free lunch on Thursdays, followed by after-work drinks  
💰 Employee referral scheme  
🚀 Make a real-world impact by helping transform the construction industry

# Senior Project Planner

## Location

Europe

## ABOUT XYZ REALITY

XYZ Reality is transforming the construction industry through cutting-edge Augmented Reality (AR) technology.

We're the creators of The Atom, the world's first engineering-grade AR headset purpose-built for construction. By combining innovative technology with hands-on construction expertise, we're helping project teams improve accuracy, reduce rework and deliver complex projects with greater confidence.

Working with leading construction and mission-critical organisations across international markets, we're challenging traditional ways of working and helping shape the future of construction.

As we continue to grow, we're looking for ambitious, talented people who want to make a genuine impact.

## THE ROLE

Are you an experienced Senior Project Planner looking to take your career beyond traditional construction planning?

We're looking for a talented and commercially minded Senior Project Planner to play a key role in delivering complex construction projects across Europe and the Middle East.

This is an exciting opportunity to combine your technical planning expertise with innovative construction technology, working closely with clients, contractors and multidisciplinary project teams to improve how major projects are planned, monitored and delivered.

You'll take ownership of planning and programme controls across multiple projects, with a particular focus on data centres and mission-critical environments.

More than a traditional planning role, you'll have the opportunity to influence senior stakeholders, shape best practice and contribute to the continued development of our project delivery capabilities.

## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

* **Lead project planning:** Take ownership of planning and scheduling across multiple complex construction projects, from pre-construction through to handover.
* **Drive programme excellence:** Develop, review and challenge detailed construction programmes, ensuring clear milestones, dependencies and realistic delivery schedules.
* **Integrate planning and technology:** Support the integration of project programmes, including MEP installation and commissioning sequences, with BIM and 4D planning tools.
* **Manage programme risks:** Conduct critical path, schedule risk and delay analysis, identifying potential challenges and developing effective mitigation and recovery strategies.
* **Deliver meaningful insights:** Provide clear, actionable progress reporting and programme analysis to clients and senior stakeholders.
* **Build strong partnerships:** Collaborate with client and contractor planning teams, providing expert guidance, constructive challenge and technical leadership.
* **Influence and develop others:** Support planning standards, share best practice and mentor colleagues to strengthen planning capabilities across the business.
* **Represent XYZ Reality:** Act as a trusted planning expert in client discussions, contributing to project delivery strategy and supporting new business opportunities.

## REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

1. Construction-related degree or relevant M&E trade background with progression into project planning.
2. Demonstrable experience in construction planning or scheduling, including at least 3 years in a senior or lead planning role.
3. Advanced proficiency in Primavera P6.
4. Willingness to travel regularly across Europe and the Middle East.

## KEY EXPERIENCE & SKILLS

* Proven planning experience within data centre, mission-critical or similarly complex construction environments.
* Strong understanding of MEP installation, commissioning and integrated systems testing.
* Experience developing and managing complex construction programmes across multiple stakeholders.
* Strong knowledge of critical path analysis, programme risk management and delay mitigation.
* Experience delivering projects across Europe and/or the Middle East, ideally with knowledge of NEC or FIDIC contracts.
* Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to influence and challenge at senior level.
* A proactive, solutions-focused approach with the ability to balance technical detail and broader project priorities.
* Experience with Asta Powerproject, 4D planning tools such as Synchro or Navisworks, or Power BI would be advantageous.

**Ready to help shape the future of construction?**

If you're an experienced Project Planner who enjoys solving complex challenges, influencing project outcomes and embracing innovative ways of working, we'd love to hear from you.
